meaning: Expresses conjecture or probability without absolute certainty: 'Probably / It will likely be X'. Also used with rising tone to seek agreement ('Right?').
connection: Plain form + でしょう (Polite) / だろう (Plain) [Noun & な-adj attach directly without だ!]
nuance: NO だ BEFORE DESHOU: For nouns and な-adjectives, drop だ completely: 暇でしょう (NOT 暇だでしょう ❌), 雨でしょう (NOT 雨だでしょう ❌).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Attach directly without だ! (雨でしょう = It will probably rain).

sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日は午後から雨が降るでしょう。
sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, it will probably rain from the afternoon tomorrow.
sentences.literal: Weather-forecast according-to, tomorrow afternoon-from rain fall probably.
sentences.nuanceNote: Meteorological conjecture.

sentences.japanese: 明日は寒いでしょう。
sentences.english: It will probably be cold tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: でしょう expresses a prediction, not a numerical probability guarantee.

sentences.japanese: あの人は先生でしょう。
sentences.english: That person is probably a teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: A non-past affirmative noun attaches directly to でしょう, without だ.

quiz.question: 田中さんはよく勉強していますから、明日の試験に（　　）でしょう。
quiz.translation: Tanaka studies hard, so they will probably pass tomorrow's exam.
quiz.grammarFocus: Conjecture 〜でしょう with plain verb
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + でしょう (Polite) / だろう (Plain) [Noun & な-adj attach directly without だ!]

explanations.reason: The dictionary form connects directly to でしょう.
The te-form does not connect directly to でしょう here.
The bare stem does not form the required predicate.
Do not put だ after a finite verb before でしょう.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 272 (PDF p. 280). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜んです
meaning: Explain background or ask for an explanation.
connection: Plain form + んです; N/な-adjective + なんです
nuance: Use it when the reason or background is relevant to the conversation. It is not required in every factual statement.
keyTakeaway: Plain form + んです; N/な-adjective + なんです

sentences.japanese: 今日は早く帰ります。試験があるんです。
sentences.english: I am going home early today. I have an exam.

sentences.japanese: 今日は早く帰ります。用事があるんです。
sentences.english: I am going home early today. I have something to do.
sentences.nuanceNote: んです presents the second statement as an explanation relevant to the first.

sentences.japanese: どうして休んだんですか。熱があったんです。
sentences.english: Why were you absent? I had a fever.
sentences.nuanceNote: The explanatory question asks for background; the past predicates retain their past forms before んです.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 272 (PDF p. 280). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ほうがいい
meaning: Give advice.
connection: Vた + ほうがいい; Vない + ほうがいい
nuance: The affirmative uses the past form even when advising about the future. It can sound strong, so consider the relationship and situation.
keyTakeaway: Vた + ほうがいい; Vない + ほうがいい

sentences.japanese: 今日は早く寝たほうがいいですよ。
sentences.english: You should go to bed early today.

sentences.japanese: 疲れているなら、少し休んだほうがいいです。
sentences.english: If you are tired, you should rest a little.
sentences.nuanceNote: The affirmative advice uses Vた even though the recommended action is still in the future.

sentences.japanese: 夜遅くにコーヒーを飲まないほうがいいです。
sentences.english: You should not drink coffee late at night.
sentences.nuanceNote: Negative advice uses Vない; it is advice, not the formal prohibition てはいけない.

sentences.japanese: どうして遅刻したのですか。「目覚まし時計が鳴らなかったんです。」
sentences.english: Why were you late? "The thing is, my alarm clock didn't ring."
sentences.nuanceNote: Explanatory んです provides the empathetic reason for the mishap.

sentences.japanese: どうして遅刻したのですか。電車が止まったんです。
sentences.english: Why were you late? It's because the train stopped.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜んです provides an underlying causal explanation for an observed situation.

sentences.japanese: 頭が痛いんです。少し休んでもいいですか。
sentences.english: The thing is, I have a headache. May I rest a little?
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜んです frames personal circumstances before requesting permission.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 272 (PDF p. 280). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 可能形 (Potential Verbs: Ability & Possibility)
meaning: Expresses that an agent has the ability to do an action or that circumstances permit it.
connection: Ru-verbs: 食べる→食べられる | U-verbs: 書く→書ける, 飲む→飲める | Irregular: する→できる, くる→こられる
nuance: The potential expresses ability or possibility. The object often takes が, but を also occurs in suitable constructions; do not treat it as universally wrong. Ru-verbs use られる in the standard form; colloquial ら抜き forms such as 食べれる are common but should be distinguished from the standard forms taught here. Some potential and passive/honorific forms overlap, so context matters.
keyTakeaway: The potential expresses ability or possibility. The object often takes が, but を also occurs in suitable constructions; do not treat it as universally wrong. Ru-verbs use られる in the standard form; colloquial ら抜き forms such as 食べれる are common but should be distinguished from the standard forms taught here. Some potential and passive/honorific forms overlap, so context matters.

sentences.japanese: 漢字が難しくて、新聞がすらすら読めません。
sentences.english: The kanji are difficult, so I cannot read the newspaper smoothly.
sentences.literal: Kanji difficult-being, newspaper smoothly read-cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む potential negative: 読める → 読めません.

sentences.japanese: 私は日本語の新聞が読めます。弟はまだ読めません。
sentences.english: I can read Japanese newspapers. My younger brother cannot yet.
sentences.nuanceNote: An u-verb changes 読む→読める; the potential verb then has polite affirmative/negative forms.

sentences.japanese: この店では、新鮮な魚が食べられます。
sentences.english: You can eat fresh fish at this restaurant.
sentences.nuanceNote: 食べる→食べられる is the standard ru-verb potential; this example describes an available opportunity, not just a personal skill.

quiz.question: 「食べることができません」という意味です。生魚が食べ（　　）。
quiz.translation: I cannot eat raw fish.
quiz.grammarFocus: 可能形 potential negative
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: 食べる→食べられる | U-verbs: 書く→書ける, 飲む→飲める | Irregular: する→できる, くる→こられる

explanations.reason: 食べられません is the standard potential negative.
食べさせます is causative: make/let eat.
食べたいです expresses desire.
食べました is past affirmative.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki II: Potential Verbs (可能形) Matrix (Lesson 13)
table.subtitle: Expressing ability and situational possibility ("can do").

rows.label: Group 2: Ru-Verbs
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べられる, 見られる, 起きられる (Drop る, attach られる)
Direct object particle を shifts to が: 漢字が読める, 日本語が話せる
Colloquial "ra-nuki" (ら抜き): 食べれる, 見れる (frequent in spoken Japanese, but avoid on formal JLPT!)
rows.note: Identical form to passive; context disambiguates.

rows.label: Group 1: U-Verbs
cells: 行く, 飲む, 話す, 待つ, 泳ぐ
行ける, 飲める, 話せる, 待てる, 泳げる (Shift final -u sound to -e sound and add る)
All potential verbs conjugate as Group 2 (Ichidan) verbs once transformed: 話せる → 話せます / 話せない
Do NOT add られる to U-verbs! 行く becomes 行ける, NOT 行かられる ❌!
rows.note: Clean shift: -u → -eru.

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular
cells: する (to do), 来る (くる, to come)
する → できる, 来る → こられる (来られる)
Particle shift: 運転ができる (Can drive), 日本語ができる (Can speak Japanese)
Note the reading of 来 changes to "ko": こられる (NOT ちられる ❌).
rows.note: する completely transforms into the independent potential verb できる.

title: 〜し、〜し (Listing Multiple Parallel Reasons)
meaning: Lists two or more complementary reasons leading up to a conclusion or emotion ('Not only... but also...').
connection: Plain form + し (Noun/な-adj non-past affirmative takes だ: 綺麗だし, 休みだし)
nuance: し lists contributing reasons or characteristics and often implies that other reasons exist. A single explicit し clause is possible. Both plain and polite predicates can precede it; plain affirmative nouns/な-adjectives need だ. It is not the only way to combine several reasons, and から is not limited to just one reason.
keyTakeaway: し lists contributing reasons or characteristics and often implies that other reasons exist. A single explicit し clause is possible. Both plain and polite predicates can precede it; plain affirmative nouns/な-adjectives need だ. It is not the only way to combine several reasons, and から is not limited to just one reason.

sentences.japanese: 物価も安いし、治安もいいし、この街に住んでよかったです。
sentences.english: Prices are cheap and public safety is great, so I am really glad I live in this town.
sentences.literal: Prices-also cheap-and, safety-also good-and, this town-in living glad-was.
sentences.nuanceNote: Two positive factors combined using 〜し.

sentences.japanese: この店は安いし、おいしいし、よく来ます。
sentences.english: I come here often because it is cheap and the food is good.
sentences.nuanceNote: し accumulates contributing reasons; it need not claim that these are the only ones.

sentences.japanese: 明日は休みだし、少し夜更かししてもいいでしょう。
sentences.english: Tomorrow is a day off, among other things, so staying up a little should be fine.
sentences.useLabel: One explicit reason with others implied
sentences.nuanceNote: A single stated し reason is possible; a noun predicate uses だし.

quiz.question: この部屋は（　　）し、駅にも近いです。
quiz.translation: This room is quiet and is also near the station.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective connection to 〜し
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + し (Noun/な-adj non-past affirmative takes だ: 綺麗だし, 休みだし)

explanations.reason: A plain affirmative na-adjective takes だ before し.
The bare na-adjective stem does not attach directly to し.
な is the noun-modifying linker, not the ending before し.
で is connective but does not form the required predicate before し.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てみる (Trying Out an Action: Doing Something to See What Happens)
meaning: Performs an experimental action to test the waters or see what the outcome will be: 'try doing / give it a try'.
connection: V-て + みる (Conjugates as a Ru-verb: 〜てみます, 〜てみたい)
nuance: TESTING THE WATERS: Literally uses the verb 見る (to see): 'do and see'. 履いてみる (try shoes on), 食べてみる (taste it), 行ってみる (go and check).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + みる = Give it a try to see the result! (やってみよう = Let's give it a shot!).

sentences.japanese: 日本の納豆はまだ食べたことがないので、一口食べてみます。
sentences.english: Since I have never eaten Japanese natto yet, I will try taking a bite to see what it's like.
sentences.literal: Japan's natto yet eaten experience have-not since, one-bite eat-and-see.
sentences.nuanceNote: Experimental culinary trial.

sentences.japanese: この靴を履いてみてもいいですか。
sentences.english: May I try these shoes on?
sentences.nuanceNote: てみる means carrying out the action to see what it is like or what happens.

sentences.japanese: 先生に聞いてみましたが、先生も知りませんでした。
sentences.english: I tried asking the teacher, but the teacher did not know either.
sentences.useLabel: Try an action, learn the result
sentences.nuanceNote: The attempt at asking occurred; the desired information was not obtained.

quiz.question: この服、サイズが合うかどうか一度（　　）みてもいいですか。
quiz.translation: May I try this clothing on once to see if the size fits?
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + みる (Try doing)
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + みる (Conjugates as a Ru-verb: 〜てみます, 〜てみたい)

explanations.reason: Correct! 着る is a Ru-verb: te-form 着て + みてもいいですか (着てみてもいいですか).
Incorrect. 着る is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 着 is bare stem.
Incorrect. 着た is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: なら (Contextual Limitation Conditional: If It's X / As For X)
meaning: Singles out a specific topic from context: 'If we're talking about X, then... / As for X (though other things might not be)'.
connection: Noun + なら (Attaches directly without だ!) | Plain form + なら
nuance: なら takes a stated or assumed situation as a premise. It can narrow a topic (ひらがななら読める) or introduce advice based on the listener's plan. A narrowed topic suggests a contrast but does not logically prove that every other option is impossible. The action after なら may occur before the premise event, unlike a simple after-marker.
keyTakeaway: なら takes a stated or assumed situation as a premise. It can narrow a topic (ひらがななら読める) or introduce advice based on the listener's plan. A narrowed topic suggests a contrast but does not logically prove that every other option is impossible. The action after なら may occur before the premise event, unlike a simple after-marker.

sentences.japanese: 英語なら話せますが、フランス語は全く話せません。
sentences.english: If it's English, I can speak it, but I cannot speak French at all.
sentences.literal: English if-talking-about speak-can but, French at-all speak-cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: Selective linguistic competence.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行くなら、少し日本語を勉強しておくといいです。
sentences.english: If you are going to Japan, it is a good idea to study some Japanese beforehand.
sentences.nuanceNote: The recommended preparation comes before the trip; なら does not mean after going.

sentences.japanese: ひらがななら読めますが、漢字はまだ苦手です。
sentences.english: I can read hiragana, but I am still not good at kanji.
sentences.nuanceNote: なら focuses the ability claim on hiragana. The contrast is supplied explicitly here.

quiz.question: 「明日京都に行くんですが。」「京都（　　）、金閣寺がおすすめですよ。」
quiz.translation: 'I'm going to Kyoto tomorrow.' 'If it's Kyoto, Kinkaku-ji is highly recommended!'
quiz.grammarFocus: Contextual conditional なら
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + なら (Attaches directly without だ!) | Plain form + なら

explanations.reason: Correct! なら picks up the conversational topic mentioned by the partner.
Incorrect. たら is temporal sequence ('if/when Kyoto happens').
Incorrect. ば requires a predicate (verb/adjective).
Incorrect. と is natural inevitable consequence.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜そうです：様子
meaning: An appearance-based impression.
connection: い-adjective without い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう; verb stem + そう
nuance: おいしそう means looks tasty; おいしいそうだ reports what someone said. いい→よさそう、ない→なさそう. V-stemそう can signal an imminent event.
keyTakeaway: い-adjective without い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう; verb stem + そう

sentences.japanese: このケーキはおいしそうです。雨が降りそうです。
sentences.english: This cake looks tasty. It looks like it will rain.

sentences.japanese: このケーキはおいしそうです。
sentences.english: This cake looks delicious.
sentences.nuanceNote: Appearance そう drops the final い of the adjective; compare hearsay おいしいそうです.

sentences.japanese: 空が暗くなってきました。雨が降りそうです。
sentences.english: The sky has become dark. It looks as if it will rain.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb stem + そう predicts an event from signs, rather than reporting what someone said.

sentences.japanese: この方法はよさそうです。問題もなさそうです。
sentences.english: This method looks good. There do not seem to be any problems either.
sentences.nuanceNote: いい→よさそう and ない→なさそう are special forms; do not use いそう for good.

sentences.japanese: 漢字が難しくて、新聞をすらすら読むことができません（読めません）。
sentences.english: The kanji are difficult, so I cannot read the newspaper smoothly.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む (U-verb) becomes 読める in potential form (読めません).

sentences.japanese: 以前は泳げませんでしたが、今は一キロ泳げます。
sentences.english: Previously I could not swim, but now I can swim one kilometer.
sentences.useLabel: Potential verb with が particle flip
sentences.nuanceNote: Potential verbs commonly take が instead of を for the object of ability.

sentences.japanese: この図書館では、誰でも無料で本を借りることができます。
sentences.english: In this library, anyone can borrow books for free.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜ことができる expresses circumstantial permission or institutional feasibility.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.subtitle: Expressing ability and situational possibility ("can do").

rows.label: Group 2: Ru-Verbs
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べられる, 見られる, 起きられる (Drop る, attach られる)
Direct object particle を shifts to が: 漢字が読める, 日本語が話せる
Colloquial "ra-nuki" (ら抜き): 食べれる, 見れる (frequent in spoken Japanese, but avoid on formal JLPT!)
rows.note: Identical form to passive; context disambiguates.

rows.label: Group 1: U-Verbs
cells: 行く, 飲む, 話す, 待つ, 泳ぐ
行ける, 飲める, 話せる, 待てる, 泳げる (Shift final -u sound to -e sound and add る)
All potential verbs conjugate as Group 2 (Ichidan) verbs once transformed: 話せる → 話せます / 話せない
Do NOT add られる to U-verbs! 行く becomes 行ける, NOT 行かられる ❌!
rows.note: Clean shift: -u → -eru.

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular
cells: する (to do), 来る (くる, to come)
する → できる, 来る → こられる (来られる)
Particle shift: 運転ができる (Can drive), 日本語ができる (Can speak Japanese)
Note the reading of 来 changes to "ko": こられる (NOT ちられる ❌).
rows.note: する completely transforms into the independent potential verb できる.

title: 期間に回数
meaning: Frequency within a period.
connection: Period + に + number of times
nuance: 一週間に二回 means twice a week, not for two weeks. 回 counts occurrences.
keyTakeaway: Period + に + number of times

sentences.japanese: 週に三回、日本語を練習しています。
sentences.english: I practice Japanese three times a week.

sentences.japanese: 一週間に三回、泳いでいます。
sentences.english: I swim three times a week.
sentences.nuanceNote: The period takes に before the number of occurrences.

sentences.japanese: 二日に一回、花に水をやります。
sentences.english: I water the flowers once every two days.
sentences.nuanceNote: 二日に一回 gives a repeated interval, not two occurrences every day.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: ほしい (Expressing Desire for an Object: Want Something)
meaning: Expresses first-person desire to possess a concrete object or commodity: [Item] が ほしい ('I want [Item]').
connection: [Item] が ほしいです (Conjugates 100% as an い-adjective: ほしくない, ほしかった)
nuance: HOSHII VS TAI: たい is for ACTIONS ('I want to BUY a car' = 車を買いたい). ほしい is for NOUN OBJECTS ('I want a car' = 車がほしい). Target takes が!
keyTakeaway: Basic desire for a thing: Nがほしい. Desire to perform an action: V-stem + たい.

sentences.japanese: 今度の誕生日に、新しいノートパソコンがほしいです。
sentences.english: For my upcoming birthday, I want a new laptop computer.
sentences.literal: This-time's birthday-on, new laptop want is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Desire for material item marked with が.

sentences.japanese: 新しい辞書がほしいです。
sentences.english: I want a new dictionary.
sentences.nuanceNote: ほしい describes desire for a thing; the basic target is marked with が.

sentences.japanese: 車がほしいですが、今は買いたくありません。
sentences.english: I want a car, but I do not want to buy one now.
sentences.nuanceNote: ほしい expresses wanting the thing; たい expresses wanting to perform an action. The two need not coincide.

quiz.question: 今は何も（　　）くないです。ただゆっくり休みたいです。
quiz.translation: Right now I don't want anything. I just want to rest leisurely.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative of ほしい (ほしくない)
quiz.ruleHint: [Item] が ほしいです (Conjugates 100% as an い-adjective: ほしくない, ほしかった)

explanations.reason: Correct! ほしい drops い + くない = ほしくない (Nothing wanted).
Incorrect. ほしいくない retains the extra い.
Incorrect. ほしく is already adverbial; adding another くない is invalid.
Incorrect. ほしな is ungrammatical.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜かもしれない / 〜かもしんない (Epistemic Possibility: Might / May)
meaning: States that something is possible without guaranteeing it: 'might / may be X' (roughly 50% or less certainty).
connection: Plain form + かもしれません | Noun / な-adj attach directly without だ!
nuance: NO だ BEFORE KAMOSHれない: Just like でしょう, nouns and な-adjectives drop だ: 雨かもしれない (NOT 雨だかもしれない ❌), 暇かもしれない.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Attach directly without だ! (風邪かもしれない = Might have caught a cold).

sentences.japanese: 午後から天気が崩れて、雨が降るかもしれません。
sentences.english: The weather may deteriorate from the afternoon, and it might rain.
sentences.literal: Afternoon-from weather deteriorate, rain fall might.
sentences.nuanceNote: Epistemic possibility of rain.

sentences.japanese: 明日は雪が降るかもしれません。
sentences.english: It may snow tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: かもしれない leaves open a possibility; it does not encode a fixed numerical probability.

sentences.japanese: 今日は休みかもしれません。昨日も休みだったかもしれません。
sentences.english: It may be closed today. It may have been closed yesterday too.
sentences.nuanceNote: Non-past affirmative nouns omit だ before かもしれない; a past predicate retains だった.

quiz.question: 山田さんは道に迷っ（　　）かもしれません。
quiz.translation: Yamada may have got lost.
quiz.grammarFocus: Past conjecture with 〜かもしれない
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + かもしれません | Noun / な-adj attach directly without だ!

explanations.reason: 迷った is a past predicate before かもしれません.
The te-form does not directly connect to かもしれません.
たり needs a different continuation.
のに is a conjunction and does not form this possibility predicate.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜たらどうですか (Casual Advice / Suggestion: Why Don't You?)
meaning: Offers a suggestion or recommendation to the listener: 'Why don't you try X? / How about doing X?'.
connection: V-た + らどうですか
nuance: たらどうですか offers advice. Depending on tone and context, it may sound critical or presumptuous, especially to someone senior. Choose an appropriately indirect suggestion when needed.
keyTakeaway: たらどうですか offers advice. Depending on tone and context, it may sound critical or presumptuous, especially to someone senior. Choose an appropriately indirect suggestion when needed.

sentences.japanese: 頭が痛いなら、無理をしないで薬を飲んで寝たらどうですか。
sentences.english: If you have a headache, why don't you stop overworking, take medicine, and sleep?
sentences.literal: Head hurts if, overwork do-not medicine take slept-if how is?
sentences.nuanceNote: Sympathetic peer recommendation.

sentences.japanese: 分からないなら、先生に聞いてみたらどうですか。
sentences.english: If you do not understand, why not try asking your teacher?
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたらどう suggests a possible solution; it does not assert that the action already happened.

sentences.japanese: 疲れているなら、今日は早く寝たらどう。
sentences.english: If you are tired, why not go to bed early today?
sentences.nuanceNote: The same construction can sound caring or critical depending on tone and relationship.

quiz.question: 分からない単語があるなら、辞書で（　　）たらどうですか。
quiz.translation: If there are vocabulary words you don't understand, why don't you look them up in a dictionary?
quiz.grammarFocus: Advice formula 〜たらどうですか
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + らどうですか

explanations.reason: Correct! 調べる (Ru-verb) past form is 調べた + らどうですか (調べたらどうですか).
Incorrect. 調べる is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 調べて is te-form.
調べた plus the supplied たら would produce 調べたたら; the blank must contain 調べ.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: あげる・くれる・もらう
meaning: Giving and receiving objects.
connection: Giver は receiver に Nをあげる/くれる; receiver は giver に/から Nをもらう
nuance: くれる describes giving toward the speaker or their in-group. もらう makes the recipient the subject. The forms encode viewpoint, not just politeness.
keyTakeaway: Giver は receiver に Nをあげる/くれる; receiver は giver に/から Nをもらう

sentences.japanese: 妹が私に本をくれました。私は妹に本をもらいました。
sentences.english: My younger sister gave me a book. I received a book from her.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に本をあげました。
sentences.english: I gave a book to a friend.
sentences.nuanceNote: The giver is the subject and the receiver takes に. あげる views the gift as moving away from the speaker's side.

sentences.japanese: 友達が私に本をくれました。
sentences.english: A friend gave me a book.
sentences.nuanceNote: くれる presents the giver's action toward the speaker or their side.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に本をもらいました。
sentences.english: I received a book from a friend.
sentences.nuanceNote: The receiver is the subject with もらう; this describes the same transfer from another viewpoint.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Giving & Receiving Triad (授受動詞): あげる vs くれる vs もらう
table.subtitle: Tracks social perspective, insider/outsider psychology, and debt of gratitude.

rows.label: X は Y に あげる / 〜てあげる
cells: X (Giver / "I" or insider)
From Speaker/Insider OUTWARD to Receiver
差し上げる (さしあげる - Humble toward higher status)
CAUTION: Doing a favor directly to a superior with 〜てあげます can sound condescending. Avoid!
rows.note: Subject = Giver. Particle に = Receiver.

rows.label: X が 私に くれる / 〜てくれる
cells: X (Giver / Outside party)
From Outside party INWARD to Speaker / My In-Group
くださる (Honorific - Superior gave to me)
The giver is the subject. The recipient is understood from the speaker or empathy viewpoint, typically the speaker or their in-group.
rows.note: 先生が私に本をくださった (Teacher gave me a book).

rows.label: 私 は X に/から もらう / 〜てもらう
cells: 私 (Receiver / Beneficiary as Subject)
The subject receives from the giver; the subject need not be the speaker.
いただく (Humble - I humbly received from superior)
The receiver is the subject (often presented as a は-topic). The giver takes に; から is possible for receiving objects, but not freely interchangeable with に in てもらう.
rows.note: 田中さんに手伝ってもらった (I got Tanaka-san to help me).

title: 数量＋も・しか〜ない
meaning: A surprisingly large amount or a restricted amount.
connection: Number + も; number + しか + negative
nuance: も emphasizes as many/as much as. しか requires a negative predicate but the meaning is only that amount.
keyTakeaway: Number + も; number + しか + negative

sentences.japanese: 一時間も待ちました。お金は五百円しかありません。
sentences.english: I waited a whole hour. I have only five hundred yen.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は十時間も寝ました。
sentences.english: I slept as many as ten hours yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: Quantity + も signals that the speaker considers the amount notable or large.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は三時間しか寝ませんでした。
sentences.english: I slept only three hours yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: Quantity + しか pairs with a negative predicate. It excludes a larger amount in the statement.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 意向形 (The Volitional Form: Casual Let's Do / Self-Resolve)
meaning: The casual plain equivalent of 〜ましょう: 'Let's do X!' In monologue, expresses personal determination: 'I shall do X!'.
connection: Ru-verbs: drop る + よう (食べよう) | U-verbs: change final -u to -ou (行こう, 飲もう) | する→しよう, くる→こよう
nuance: CASUAL COMPANION: In peer conversation, '行こう!' replaces '行きましょう!'. In internal monologue, 'よし、頑張ろう!' expresses resolve.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Ru-verbs = drop る + よう. U-verbs = change final -u to long -ou (書く→書こう).

sentences.japanese: 今日は天気がいいから、海までドライブに行こう！
sentences.english: The weather is great today, so let's go for a drive to the beach!
sentences.literal: Today weather good since, beach-to drive-to let's-go!
sentences.nuanceNote: Casual peer invitation.

sentences.japanese: 一緒に帰ろう。
sentences.english: Let's go home together.
sentences.nuanceNote: 帰る is an u-verb: 帰ろう. The volitional can invite another person to join.

sentences.japanese: よし、もう一度やってみよう。
sentences.english: All right, I will try once more.
sentences.nuanceNote: The volitional can express the speaker's resolve without inviting anyone else.

quiz.question: 少し休もう。これは「休みましょう」の（　　）形です。
quiz.translation: Let us rest a little. Which form of rest is 休もう?
quiz.grammarFocus: U-verb volitional form 休もう
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: drop る + よう (食べよう) | U-verbs: change final -u to -ou (行こう, 飲もう) | する→しよう, くる→こよう

explanations.reason: 休もう is the plain volitional form.
The passive is 休まれる, not 休もう.
The plain negative is 休まない.
The plain past is 休んだ.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 70 (PDF p. 78). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 意向形 + と思っている (Firm Ongoing Determination: Intending To)
meaning: Expresses an ongoing, settled determination that the speaker has been contemplating over time: 'I have been planning/intending to do X'.
connection: V volitional + と思う / と思っている
nuance: Volitional + と思う expresses intention. と思っている presents an ongoing intention, often held before speaking, but it need not be firm or guaranteed. A dictionary-form clause + と思う is also grammatical and reports a belief; it is a different construction from volitional intention.
keyTakeaway: Volitional + と思う expresses intention. と思っている presents an ongoing intention, often held before speaking, but it need not be firm or guaranteed. A dictionary-form clause + と思う is also grammatical and reports a belief; it is a different construction from volitional intention.

sentences.japanese: 来年から日本企業で働こうと思っています。
sentences.english: I am planning on working at a Japanese firm starting next year.
sentences.literal: Next-year-from Japanese firm-at work-shall quote thinking-am.

tokens.word: 働こうと思っています
tokens.reading: はたらこうとおもっています

sentences.nuanceNote: Ongoing career resolution.

sentences.japanese: 来年、日本へ留学しようと思っています。
sentences.english: I intend to study abroad in Japan next year.
sentences.nuanceNote: The volitional 留学しよう makes this an intention, while と思っている presents it as an ongoing plan.

sentences.japanese: 今日は歩いて帰ろうと思います。
sentences.english: I think I will walk home today.
sentences.nuanceNote: と思います expresses an intention here; it does not prove that the decision was made at this exact second.

quiz.question: 「登る」の意向形を使います。夏休みに富士山に（　　）と思っています。
quiz.translation: Use the volitional form: I intend to climb Mount Fuji during summer vacation.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-意向形 + と思っている
quiz.ruleHint: V volitional + と思う / と思っている

explanations.reason: 登ろう is the volitional and expresses intention with と思っている.
登ると思う can report a belief, but 登る is not the requested volitional form.
登り is the polite stem, not volitional.
登った is the plain past, not volitional.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 70 (PDF p. 78). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 連体修飾節 (Relative Clauses / Qualifying Nouns with Sentences)
meaning: Embedding an entire sentence before a noun to modify it without any relative pronoun ('The book that I bought yesterday').
connection: Plain modifying clause + noun; embedded subjects commonly marked with が
nuance: A plain modifying clause precedes its noun without an English-style relative pronoun. Its subject commonly takes が (or の in some noun-modifying clauses). Contrastive は is possible; avoid a universal prohibition.
keyTakeaway: A plain modifying clause precedes its noun without an English-style relative pronoun. Its subject commonly takes が (or の in some noun-modifying clauses). Contrastive は is possible; avoid a universal prohibition.

sentences.japanese: これは私が昨日デパートで買ったセーターです。
sentences.english: This is the sweater that I bought at the department store yesterday.
sentences.literal: This topic I-subject yesterday department-store-at bought sweater is.

tokens.word: 私が昨日デパートで買った
tokens.meaning: that I bought at department store yesterday
tokens.reading: わたしがきょうデパートでかった
tokens.romaji: watashi ga kinou depaato de katta

sentences.nuanceNote: Direct noun qualification without pronouns.

sentences.japanese: これは友達が作ったケーキです。
sentences.english: This is the cake my friend made.
sentences.nuanceNote: The modifying clause goes before ケーキ; its subject takes が in this example.

sentences.japanese: 昨日会った人は医者です。
sentences.english: The person I met yesterday is a doctor.
sentences.nuanceNote: The person is understood as the one met inside 昨日会った; do not insert an English-style relative pronoun.

quiz.question: あそこに立って（　　）人は、私の高校の英語の先生です。
quiz.translation: The person standing over there is my high school English teacher.
quiz.grammarFocus: Relative clause noun modification with plain form
quiz.ruleHint: Plain modifying clause + noun; embedded subjects commonly marked with が

explanations.reason: Correct! Plain form いる modifies the head noun 人 (立っている人).
Incorrect. Polite form います cannot modify a noun directly.
Incorrect. いたの人は has unnecessary nominalizer の.
Incorrect. いまして is te-form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 70 (PDF p. 78). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ておく
meaning: Prepare in advance or leave something in a state.
connection: Vて + おく
nuance: The action serves a later purpose. Leaving a state unchanged is another use. Casual contractions include 買っておく→買っとく.
keyTakeaway: Vて + おく

sentences.japanese: 明日のために資料を読んでおきます。
sentences.english: I will read the materials in advance for tomorrow.

sentences.japanese: 旅行の前に、ホテルを予約しておきます。
sentences.english: I will reserve a hotel before the trip.
sentences.nuanceNote: ておく presents the action as preparation for a later purpose.

sentences.japanese: あとで使うので、電気はつけておいてください。
sentences.english: We will use it later, so please leave the light on.
sentences.nuanceNote: ておく can maintain a useful state rather than perform a new action immediately.

sentences.japanese: パーティーの前に、部屋を綺麗に掃除しておきます。
sentences.english: Before the party, I will clean up the room nicely in advance.
sentences.nuanceNote: Preparatory action executed specifically for the upcoming party.

sentences.japanese: 明日友達が遊びに来るので、部屋を掃除しておきました。
sentences.english: Because my friends are coming over tomorrow, I cleaned my room in advance.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-ておく denotes an action performed in preparation for a future event.

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けておいてください。部屋の空気を入れ替えたいので。
sentences.english: Please leave the window open, as I want to air out the room.
sentences.useLabel: Leaving a state as it is
sentences.nuanceNote: V-ておく can express leaving a resultant state intact for a purpose.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 70 (PDF p. 78). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki II: Volitional Form (意向形 / 意志形) Matrix (Lesson 15)
table.subtitle: Casual "Let's do" (~ましょう) and ongoing personal intentions (~と思っています).

rows.label: Group 2: Ru-Verbs
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べよう, 見よう, 起きよう (Drop る, attach よう)
1. Casual invitation: 一緒に行こう (Let's go together!)
rows.note: Casual equivalent of 〜ましょう.

rows.label: Group 1: U-Verbs
cells: 行く, 飲む, 話す, 買う, 待つ
行こう, 飲もう, 話そう, 買おう, 待とう (Shift final -u to -o sound and elongate with う)
2. On-the-spot decision: 〜ようと思う (I think I will...)

cells: する, 来る (くる)
しよう, 来よう (こよう)
3. Ongoing firm resolve: 〜ようと思っている (I have been intending to...)
rows.note: Pronounced ko-you.

title: 〜といい (Hoping for Favorable Outcomes: I Hope That...)
meaning: Expresses hope or wish that a favorable condition will happen: 〜といいね (Hoping for listener's sake) vs 〜といいんですが (Hoping for speaker's own sake).
connection: Plain non-past verb + といいですね / といいんですが
nuance: といい expresses a hoped-for situation. といいですね often shares a wish about the listener; といいんですが softens a personal wish, but the endings are not rigid person markers. For an action under the speaker's control, a potential form can make the desired possibility clearer: 行けるといい. Distinguish wishing from advising with ばいい/たらいい in other contexts.
keyTakeaway: といい expresses a hoped-for situation. といいですね often shares a wish about the listener; といいんですが softens a personal wish, but the endings are not rigid person markers. For an action under the speaker's control, a potential form can make the desired possibility clearer: 行けるといい. Distinguish wishing from advising with ばいい/たらいい in other contexts.

sentences.japanese: 明日の試合、晴れるといいですね。「ええ、本当に。」
sentences.english: I hope it will be sunny for tomorrow's match, don't you? 'Yes, truly.'
sentences.literal: Tomorrow's match, clear-up if good is right? Yes, really.
sentences.nuanceNote: Expressing mutual hope for good weather.

sentences.japanese: 試験に合格できるといいですね。
sentences.english: I hope you can pass the exam.
sentences.nuanceNote: Potential + といい expresses a hoped-for possibility; ですね shares the wish with the listener.

sentences.japanese: 来年また会えるといいんですが。
sentences.english: I hope we can meet again next year.
sentences.nuanceNote: んですが softens the wish; it is not a rigid first-person-only ending.

quiz.question: 合格できると（　　）ですね。
quiz.translation: I hope you pass.
quiz.grammarFocus: Hoping formula 〜といい
quiz.ruleHint: Plain non-past verb + といいですね / といいんですが

explanations.reason: といいですね expresses a hope.
よく cannot serve as the adjective predicate here.
よいに is not the required form.
いいな cannot be followed directly by ですね in this construction.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 92 (PDF p. 100). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜時（とき）の時制 (Tense Nuances in 'When' Clauses: V-る時 vs V-た時)
meaning: Tense distinctions before とき: V-る時 (Action NOT yet completed before main verb) vs V-た時 (Action ALREADY completed before main verb).
connection: V-辞書形 + 時 (Prior/During) | V-た + 時 (After completion)
nuance: With a bounded action, dictionary-form とき commonly locates the main event before completion, while たとき commonly locates it after completion. Compare 日本へ行くとき買った and 日本へ行ったとき買った. This is a relative-time contrast, not a rule that every たとき refers to a finished event: 困ったとき means when in trouble, and 子供だったとき means when I was a child. Interpret tense together with the predicate's meaning and the surrounding situation.
keyTakeaway: Use relative timing and the type of situation; とき is not mechanically before versus after.

sentences.japanese: 出かける時、鍵をかけるのを忘れました。
sentences.english: When I was heading out, I forgot to lock the door.
sentences.literal: Head-out when, lock apply forgot.
sentences.nuanceNote: Action was in progress/prior to completing the departure.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行くとき、空港でお土産を買いました。
sentences.english: When I was going to Japan, I bought souvenirs at the airport.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary-form 行くとき commonly locates the purchase before reaching the destination.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行ったとき、京都を訪ねました。
sentences.english: When I went to Japan, I visited Kyoto.
sentences.nuanceNote: たとき presents the trip as realized; interpret the relation to the main action in context rather than translating every た as after everything finished.

quiz.question: 旅行に行く（　　）、パスポートを確認しました。
quiz.translation: Before going on a trip, I checked my passport.
quiz.grammarFocus: Tense before とき (V-る時 prior action)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + 時 (Prior/During) | V-た + 時 (After completion)

explanations.reason: 前に marks before the event.
前で would mark a physical action location, not this time relation.
前を does not connect this temporal clause.
前が cannot connect these clauses as written.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 92 (PDF p. 100). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てあげる・てくれる・てもらう
meaning: Describe beneficial actions from a viewpoint.
connection: Vて + あげる / くれる / もらう
nuance: 先生が教えてくれた makes the teacher the giver; 先生に教えてもらった makes me the recipient. Offering てあげる directly can sound presumptuous.
keyTakeaway: Vて + あげる / くれる / もらう

sentences.japanese: 友達に作文を見てもらいました。
sentences.english: I had a friend look over my composition.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に日本語を教えてあげました。
sentences.english: I taught my friend Japanese as a favor.
sentences.nuanceNote: てあげる frames an action as benefiting someone else; directly announcing favors to a superior can sound presumptuous.

sentences.japanese: 友達が駅まで迎えに来てくれました。
sentences.english: My friend came to the station to pick me up.
sentences.useLabel: Receive a favor from the giver's viewpoint
sentences.nuanceNote: The friend is the subject; くれる presents the action as benefiting the speaker.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に駅まで送ってもらいました。
sentences.english: I had a friend take me to the station.
sentences.useLabel: Receive a favor from the receiver's viewpoint
sentences.nuanceNote: The receiver is the subject, and に identifies the person performing the helpful action.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 92 (PDF p. 100). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Giving & Receiving Triad (授受動詞): あげる vs くれる vs もらう
table.subtitle: Tracks social perspective, insider/outsider psychology, and debt of gratitude.

rows.label: X は Y に あげる / 〜てあげる
cells: X (Giver / "I" or insider)
From Speaker/Insider OUTWARD to Receiver
差し上げる (さしあげる - Humble toward higher status)
CAUTION: Doing a favor directly to a superior with 〜てあげます can sound condescending. Avoid!
rows.note: Subject = Giver. Particle に = Receiver.

rows.label: X が 私に くれる / 〜てくれる
cells: X (Giver / Outside party)
From Outside party INWARD to Speaker / My In-Group
くださる (Honorific - Superior gave to me)
The giver is the subject. The recipient is understood from the speaker or empathy viewpoint, typically the speaker or their in-group.
rows.note: 先生が私に本をくださった (Teacher gave me a book).

rows.label: 私 は X に/から もらう / 〜てもらう
cells: 私 (Receiver / Beneficiary as Subject)
The subject receives from the giver; the subject need not be the speaker.
いただく (Humble - I humbly received from superior)
The receiver is the subject (often presented as a は-topic). The giver takes に; から is possible for receiving objects, but not freely interchangeable with に in てもらう.
rows.note: 田中さんに手伝ってもらった (I got Tanaka-san to help me).

title: 〜ていただけませんか
meaning: Politely request a favor.
connection: Vて + いただけませんか
nuance: The potential negative question asks whether you could receive the favor. It is more indirect than てください.
keyTakeaway: Vて + いただけませんか

sentences.japanese: もう一度説明していただけませんか。
sentences.english: Could you please explain it one more time?

sentences.japanese: すみませんが、この漢字の読み方を教えていただけませんか。
sentences.english: Excuse me, could you tell me how to read this kanji?
sentences.nuanceNote: The preface helps introduce the request. The verb still needs its te-form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 92 (PDF p. 100). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てすみません・なくてすみません
meaning: Apologize for an action or omission.
connection: Vて + すみません; Vなくて + すみません
nuance: For not doing something use the negative connecting form なくて, not the instruction pattern ないでください.
keyTakeaway: Vて + すみません; Vなくて + すみません

sentences.japanese: 連絡が遅くなってすみません。
sentences.english: I am sorry for contacting you late.

sentences.japanese: 遅れてすみません。
sentences.english: I am sorry for being late.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vて gives the action/state for which the speaker apologizes.

sentences.japanese: 連絡しなくてすみませんでした。
sentences.english: I am sorry I did not contact you.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vなくて gives the negative cause for the apology; it differs from Vないで used for doing something without another action.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 92 (PDF p. 100). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜そうです (Hearsay / Quoting Reports: I Heard That / Reportedly)
meaning: Relays information obtained from external news, reports, or rumors without personal verification: 'I heard that... / Reportedly'.
connection: Plain form + そうです (Noun / な-adj non-past takes だ: 暇だそうです, 雨だそうです)
nuance: CRUCIAL DIFFERENCE FROM CONJECTURE: Appearance: drop い (おいしそう = looks tasty). Hearsay: KEEP い and keep だ (おいしいそうです = I heard it's tasty; 暇だそうです = I heard he's free).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Hearsay attaches to 100% UNCHANGED plain form (including だ for nouns/na-adj)! Drop nothing!

sentences.japanese: ニュースによると、明日は関東地方で雪が降るそうです。
sentences.english: According to the news, I heard that it will snow in the Kanto region tomorrow.
sentences.literal: News according-to, tomorrow Kanto-region snow fall reportedly.
sentences.nuanceNote: Relaying journalistic weather forecast.

sentences.japanese: この店はおいしいそうです。この料理もおいしそうです。
sentences.english: I hear this restaurant is good. This dish looks tasty too.
sentences.nuanceNote: Hearsay keeps い; appearance drops it. The information source differs.

sentences.japanese: 新しい先生は親切だそうです。
sentences.english: I hear the new teacher is kind.
sentences.nuanceNote: Hearsay keeps the plain affirmative だ before そうです.

quiz.question: 田中さんの話では、新しい先生はとても（　　）そうです。
quiz.translation: According to Tanaka-san, I heard that the new teacher is very kind.
quiz.grammarFocus: Hearsay 〜そうです with な-adjective
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + そうです (Noun / な-adj non-past takes だ: 暇だそうです, 雨だそうです)

explanations.reason: Correct! Hearsay requires plain affirmative copula だ for な-adjectives: 親切だそうです.
Incorrect. 親切 without だ creates appearance/conjecture ('looks kind').
Incorrect. 親切な is noun-modifying form.
Incorrect. 親切に is adverbial.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 114 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜たら (Specific & Temporal Conditional: If / When / Once Done)
meaning: Universal conditional: 1) Hypothetical condition ('If X happens, then Y'). 2) Temporal certainty in future ('When / Once X finishes, Y will happen').
connection: V-た + ら | い-adj かった + ら | な-adj / Noun だった + ら
nuance: MOST VERSATILE CONDITIONAL: Unlike と (which forbids commands) or ば (which restricts volitions), 〜たら allows commands, invitations, requests, and future decisions in clause B!
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Formed by adding ら to past た-form! Allows commands and requests in clause B.

sentences.japanese: 家に帰ったら、すぐに手を洗ってうがいをしましょう。
sentences.english: Once you return home, let's wash our hands and gargle right away.
sentences.literal: Home return-once, immediately hands wash gargle let's-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: Temporal sequential conditional triggering action.

sentences.japanese: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
sentences.english: Please call when you arrive at the station.
sentences.nuanceNote: たら can introduce a request to be carried out after the condition is met.

sentences.japanese: 家に帰ったら、誰もいませんでした。
sentences.english: When I got home, nobody was there.
sentences.nuanceNote: たら can introduce an actual past discovery, not only a hypothetical condition.

quiz.question: 東京駅に（　　）ら、私に電話をかけてください。
quiz.translation: Once you arrive at Tokyo Station, please call me.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-たら conditional connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + ら | い-adj かった + ら | な-adj / Noun だった + ら

explanations.reason: Correct! 着く past is 着いた + ら = 着いたら ('once you arrive').
Incorrect. 着く is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 着き is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 着いて is te-form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 114 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: The 4 Great Conditionals Decoded: と vs ば vs たら vs なら
table.subtitle: The #1 JLPT trap point across N4, N3, and N2. Never confuse them again.

rows.label: 〜と (Natural / Mechanic)
cells: Natural law, physics, mechanical trigger: "Once X happens, Y automatically follows."
Normally excludes requests and intentions in the result of a hypothetical condition.
YES ✅ (Discovered a new surprise: 窓を開けると、雪が降っていた)
For a request triggered by a future event, use a suitable たら construction. Distinguish conditional と from quotation と.
rows.note: Example: ボタンを押すと、切符が出る (Press button -> ticket dispenses).

rows.label: 〜ば (Provisional Hypothetical)
cells: Logical requirement: "Provided that X is met, Y is true."
RESTRICTED ⚠️ (Only if verb is non-action / state like ある, or subjects differ)
Not the usual form for a one-off past discovery; habitual past results are possible.
TRAP: "薬を飲めば、熱が下がった" is WRONG. Use 飲んだら.
rows.note: Classic saying: 安ければ買う (If it is cheap, I will buy it).

rows.label: 〜たら (Chronological Trigger)
cells: "Once X is completed, THEN Y happens." The most versatile conditional.
YES ✅ (Freely allows requests, intentions, invitations: 〜てください, 〜ましょう)
YES ✅ (Indicates sequential discovery in the past: 家に帰ったら、手紙があった)
SAFE HARBOR: When in doubt on volitional clauses or conversational requests, たら is king.
rows.note: Connection: Past short form (た) + ら.

rows.label: 〜なら (Contextual Topic / Advice)
cells: "If that is the case you are talking about..." Topic conditional based on listener input.
YES ✅ (Excellent for advice, recommendations: 〜がいいですよ)
Not a chronological after-marker; it can refer to a past premise.
TRAP: Time inversion! In "日本へ行くなら、カメラを買ったほうがいい", you buy the camera BEFORE going!
rows.note: Noun / Plain form + なら (no だ).

title: 〜なくてもいいです (Lack of Obligation: You Do Not Have To)
meaning: States that an action is unnecessary: 'You do not have to do X / It is fine even if you don't do X'.
connection: V-ない (drop い) + くてもいいです
nuance: LITERAL MEANING: Even if you do not do X, it is fine. Releases the listener from social or official obligation.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ない (drop い) + くてもいいです = You don't have to do it!

sentences.japanese: 明日は祝日ですから、朝早く起きなくてもいいですよ。
sentences.english: Since tomorrow is a national holiday, you do not have to wake up early.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow national-holiday is since, morning early wake-not-even-if good is.

tokens.word: 起きなくてもいいですよ
tokens.meaning: you don't have to wake up
tokens.reading: おきなくてもいいですよ

sentences.nuanceNote: Releasing listener from waking up early.

sentences.japanese: 明日は学校へ来なくてもいいです。
sentences.english: You do not have to come to school tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: Permission not to act is different from a prohibition against acting.

sentences.japanese: 書かなくてもいいです。でも、ここに書いてはいけません。
sentences.english: You do not have to write it. But you must not write here.
sentences.nuanceNote: なくてもいい removes necessity; てはいけない forbids an action in the specified place.

quiz.question: 明日は来（　　）てもいいです。
quiz.translation: You do not have to come tomorrow.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜なくてもいい lack of obligation
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない (drop い) + くてもいいです

explanations.reason: 来ない becomes 来なくてもいい.
ないても is not the negative te-form.
なかても is not a conjugation.
なかったても is not the required form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 114 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜って・みたいです
meaning: Casual quotation and inference/resemblance.
connection: Plain clause + って; V/い-adjective plain or N/な-adjective stem + みたいだ
nuance: って can quote or report speech; it can also mark a topic. みたいだ expresses resemblance or an inference, not simply quoted news.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + って; V/い-adjective plain or N/な-adjective stem + みたいだ

sentences.japanese: 店は今日休みだって。だれもいないみたいです。
sentences.english: I heard the shop is closed today. It seems no one is there.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは明日来ないって。
sentences.english: Tanaka said they are not coming tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: って conveys reported content in casual speech.

sentences.japanese: 電気が消えています。誰もいないみたいです。
sentences.english: The lights are off. It looks as if nobody is there.
sentences.nuanceNote: みたい expresses an inference in this context; it is not automatically a report from another person.

sentences.japanese: この雲は動物みたいです。
sentences.english: This cloud looks like an animal.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nみたい describes resemblance; distinguish it from information-based inference.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 114 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: The 4 Great Conditionals Decoded: と vs ば vs たら vs なら
table.subtitle: The #1 JLPT trap point across N4, N3, and N2. Never confuse them again.

rows.label: 〜と (Natural / Mechanic)
cells: Natural law, physics, mechanical trigger: "Once X happens, Y automatically follows."
Normally excludes requests and intentions in the result of a hypothetical condition.
YES ✅ (Discovered a new surprise: 窓を開けると、雪が降っていた)
For a request triggered by a future event, use a suitable たら construction. Distinguish conditional と from quotation と.
rows.note: Example: ボタンを押すと、切符が出る (Press button -> ticket dispenses).

rows.label: 〜ば (Provisional Hypothetical)
cells: Logical requirement: "Provided that X is met, Y is true."
RESTRICTED ⚠️ (Only if verb is non-action / state like ある, or subjects differ)
Not the usual form for a one-off past discovery; habitual past results are possible.
TRAP: "薬を飲めば、熱が下がった" is WRONG. Use 飲んだら.
rows.note: Classic saying: 安ければ買う (If it is cheap, I will buy it).

rows.label: 〜たら (Chronological Trigger)
cells: "Once X is completed, THEN Y happens." The most versatile conditional.
YES ✅ (Freely allows requests, intentions, invitations: 〜てください, 〜ましょう)
YES ✅ (Indicates sequential discovery in the past: 家に帰ったら、手紙があった)
SAFE HARBOR: When in doubt on volitional clauses or conversational requests, たら is king.
rows.note: Connection: Past short form (た) + ら.

rows.label: 〜なら (Contextual Topic / Advice)
cells: "If that is the case you are talking about..." Topic conditional based on listener input.
YES ✅ (Excellent for advice, recommendations: 〜がいいですよ)
Not a chronological after-marker; it can refer to a past premise.
TRAP: Time inversion! In "日本へ行くなら、カメラを買ったほうがいい", you buy the camera BEFORE going!
rows.note: Noun / Plain form + なら (no だ).

title: 〜前に・〜てから
meaning: Before and after an action.
connection: V dictionary + 前に; Nの前に; Vてから
nuance: Use dictionary form before 前に even for a past main event. てから emphasizes that the first action precedes the second.
keyTakeaway: V dictionary + 前に; Nの前に; Vてから

sentences.japanese: 出かける前に電話しました。帰ってから勉強します。
sentences.english: I called before going out. I will study after returning.

sentences.japanese: 寝る前に、歯を磨きます。
sentences.english: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary-form V前に gives a temporal relation even if the main sentence later uses past tense.

sentences.japanese: 宿題をしてから、遊びに行きます。
sentences.english: I will go out to play after doing my homework.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vてから foregrounds completing the first action before the next.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 114 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 自動詞 vs 他動詞 (Intransitive vs Transitive Verb Pairs)
meaning: Pairs of verbs distinguishing self-occurring natural phenomena (自動詞: marked with が) from deliberate actions on an object (他動詞: marked with を).
connection: Entity が 自動詞 (開く, 閉まる, つく, 消える) | Agent が Object を 他動詞 (開ける, 閉める, つける, 消す)
nuance: An intransitive verb describes an event or state without a direct object; a transitive verb takes an object. Intransitive does not prove that an event happened spontaneously, and transitive does not by itself prove deliberate intention.
keyTakeaway: An intransitive verb describes an event or state without a direct object; a transitive verb takes an object. Intransitive does not prove that an event happened spontaneously, and transitive does not by itself prove deliberate intention.

sentences.japanese: 風でドアが閉まりました。寒かったので、私がドアを閉めました。
sentences.english: The door closed in the wind. Because it was cold, I deliberately closed the door.
sentences.literal: Wind-by door closed (intrans). Cold was since, I door closed (trans).
sentences.nuanceNote: Side-by-side contrast of intransitive vs transitive pairs.

sentences.japanese: 窓が開きました。私が窓を開けました。
sentences.english: The window opened. I opened the window.
sentences.nuanceNote: 開く is intransitive; 開ける takes the window as its object. Intransitive does not itself prove there was no human cause.

sentences.japanese: 電気がついています。テレビは消えています。
sentences.english: The light is on. The television is off.
sentences.nuanceNote: Intransitive ている describes resulting states rather than a continuing act of turning something on/off.

quiz.question: 部屋が暗いですね。電気を（　　）ましょう。
quiz.translation: The room is dark, isn't it? Let's turn on the lights.
quiz.grammarFocus: Transitive verb つける with direct object を
quiz.ruleHint: Entity が 自動詞 (開く, 閉まる, つく, 消える) | Agent が Object を 他動詞 (開ける, 閉める, つける, 消す)

explanations.reason: Correct! Direct object marker を requires transitive verb つける (stem つけ + ましょう).
Incorrect. つく is intransitive (電気がつく).
Incorrect. 消す means turn off.
Incorrect. 消える is intransitive turn off.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜と (Natural Consequence & Inevitable Conditional: When / If)
meaning: States an inevitable natural consequence, physical law, or habitual fact: 'Whenever X happens, Y automatically occurs'.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-ない + と
nuance: Conditional と describes a regular consequence or discovery. Requests and intentions are normally not used as its consequence in this sense. Narrative と can also connect actual past actions; not every use is an automatic physical law.
keyTakeaway: Conditional と describes a regular consequence or discovery. Requests and intentions are normally not used as its consequence in this sense. Narrative と can also connect actual past actions; not every use is an automatic physical law.

sentences.japanese: このボタンを押すと、お釣りが出ます。
sentences.english: When you press this button, the change automatically comes out.
sentences.literal: This button press-when, change comes-out.
sentences.nuanceNote: Automatic mechanical consequence.

sentences.japanese: このボタンを押すと、ドアが開きます。
sentences.english: If you press this button, the door opens.
sentences.nuanceNote: Conditional と presents the mechanism's result rather than a request or decision.

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けると、雪が降っていました。
sentences.english: When I opened the window, it was snowing.
sentences.nuanceNote: Narrative と can introduce an actual discovery in the past; it is not limited to universal natural laws.

quiz.question: あの交差点を右に（　　）と、左手に大きな郵便局が見えます。
quiz.translation: When you turn right at that intersection, you will see a large post office on your left.
quiz.grammarFocus: Route guidance conditional 〜と
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない + と

explanations.reason: Correct! Plain non-past 曲がる connects directly to と for automatic route guidance.
Incorrect. Past 曲がった cannot connect to と for future directions.
Incorrect. 曲がって is te-form.
Incorrect. 曲がり is masu-stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ばよかった (Retrospective Regret: I Should Have Done)
meaning: Expresses retrospective regret or remorse over an unfulfilled action: 'I should have done X (but unfortunately I didn't)'. Negative: 'I shouldn't have done X'.
connection: V-ば + よかった (Affirmative regret: should have) | V-なければ + よかった (Negative regret: shouldn't have)
nuance: ばよかった often expresses regret about a choice that was not made. It does not by itself imply a specific dramatic result: 傘を持ってくればよかった says bringing an umbrella would have been better, not necessarily that the speaker is already drenched. Negative なければよかった expresses regret about doing something.
keyTakeaway: ばよかった often expresses regret about a choice that was not made. It does not by itself imply a specific dramatic result: 傘を持ってくればよかった says bringing an umbrella would have been better, not necessarily that the speaker is already drenched. Negative なければよかった expresses regret about doing something.

sentences.japanese: 昨夜もっと早く寝ればよかった。今日は一日中頭がぼーっとしています。
sentences.english: I should have gone to bed earlier last night. Today my head is in a daze all day long.
sentences.literal: Last-night more early slept-if was-good. Today all-day head dazed-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Remorse over late night.

sentences.japanese: もっと早く予約すればよかったです。
sentences.english: I should have booked earlier.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker evaluates the unchosen action as the better choice.

sentences.japanese: あんなことを言わなければよかったです。
sentences.english: I should not have said such a thing.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative conditional expresses regret that the action did occur.

quiz.question: こんなに雨が降るなら、傘を持って（　　）ばよかった。
quiz.translation: If it was going to rain this much, I should have brought an umbrella.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ばよかった retrospective regret
quiz.ruleHint: V-ば + よかった (Affirmative regret: should have) | V-なければ + よかった (Negative regret: shouldn't have)

explanations.reason: Correct! 持ってくる conditional is 持ってくれば + よかった (should have brought).
Incorrect. くる is dictionary form.
Incorrect. こ is negative stem.
Incorrect. きた is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てしまう
meaning: Completion or an unwanted result.
connection: Vて + しまう
nuance: Context determines whether it is simple completion or regret. Spoken forms include ちゃう and じゃう.
keyTakeaway: Vて + しまう

sentences.japanese: 大切なメールを消してしまいました。
sentences.english: I accidentally deleted an important email.

sentences.japanese: この本を今日中に読んでしまいます。
sentences.english: I will finish reading this book today.
sentences.nuanceNote: てしまう can emphasize completing an action; it need not express regret.

sentences.japanese: 大切な写真を消してしまいました。
sentences.english: I accidentally deleted an important photo.
sentences.nuanceNote: Context makes the completed action regrettable. The grammar alone does not guarantee an accident.

sentences.japanese: 宿題はもうやっちゃった。
sentences.english: I have already finished the homework.
sentences.nuanceNote: てしまう can contract to ちゃう; voiced でしまう can become じゃう, as in 飲んじゃった.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki II: Transitive vs Intransitive (他動詞 vs 自動詞) Pairs (Lesson 18)
table.subtitle: Human deliberate action with を vs Spontaneous state change with が + 〜ている.
columns: 他動詞 (Transitive: Subject + を + V)
自動詞 (Intransitive: Subject + が + V)
Resulting State: 自動詞 + 〜ている

rows.label: Open (To open)
cells: 窓を開ける (Open the window)
窓が開く (The window opens)
窓が開いている (The window is open)
rows.note: Transitive takes を; Intransitive takes が.

rows.label: Close (To close)
cells: ドアを閉める (Close the door)
ドアが閉まる (The door closes)
ドアが閉まっている (The door is closed)
rows.note: Intransitive -aru ending indicates state change.

rows.label: Turn on / Light up
cells: 電気をつける (Turn on light)
電気がつく (Light turns on)
電気がついている (Light is on)
rows.note: State: It is currently illuminated.

rows.label: Turn off / Extinguish
cells: 電気を消す (Turn off light)
電気が消える (Light goes out)
電気が消えている (Light is off)
rows.note: 消す (transitive, -su) vs 消える (intransitive, -eru).

rows.label: Drop / Fall
cells: 財布を落とす (Drop wallet)
財布が落ちる (Wallet drops/falls)
財布が落ちている (A wallet is lying dropped)
rows.note: 落とす is human action; 落ちる is spontaneous event.

rows.label: Put in / Enter
cells: 本をかばんに入れる (Put book in bag)
部屋に入る (Enter room)
かばんに本が入っている (A book is inside the bag)
rows.note: 「入る（はいる）」は一段動詞の形ですが、五段（う動詞）活用です。

rows.label: Take out / Come out
cells: ペンを出す (Take out pen)
月が出る (Moon comes out)
手紙が出ている (Letter has been sent out)
rows.note: 出す (transitive) vs 出る (intransitive).

rows.label: Break / Break down
cells: 時計を壊す (Break a clock)
時計が壊れる (Clock breaks)
時計が壊れている (Clock is broken)
rows.note: 壊れている describes existing condition of brokenness.

rows.label: Soil / Get dirty
cells: 服を汚す (Soil one's clothes)
服が汚れる (Clothes get dirty)
服が汚れている (Clothes are stained/dirty)
rows.note: Intransitive state marker.

title: 〜ながら
meaning: Do two actions at the same time.
connection: Vます-stem + ながら
nuance: For this simultaneous-action use, both actions share a subject. The main action comes last. Concessive ながら is a separate construction.
keyTakeaway: Vます-stem + ながら

sentences.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら料理します。
sentences.english: I cook while listening to music.

sentences.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら、料理をしています。
sentences.english: I am cooking while listening to music.
sentences.nuanceNote: The same person performs both actions. The final predicate is the main activity.

sentences.japanese: 料理をしながら、友達と電話で話しました。
sentences.english: I talked to a friend on the phone while cooking.
sentences.nuanceNote: Changing the final predicate changes which activity is presented as central; ながら itself does not specify a fixed priority for cooking or talking.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 尊敬語 (Honorific Speech: Special Verbs & Regular Formulas)
meaning: Honorific verbs show respect toward the person whose action is described.
connection: Honorific verb; お + suitable verb stem + になる; some verbs have special forms
nuance: 尊敬語 raises the person performing the action; use it for the person being respected, not to elevate your own ordinary actions. It is not restricted to bosses or older people: customers and other people outside your group can be honored. In business speech to an outsider, your own colleague or manager belongs to your group, so do not automatically honor that manager. Special verbs such as いらっしゃる and おっしゃる have special polite forms: いらっしゃいます and おっしゃいます.
keyTakeaway: Choose the viewpoint and social relation first; honorific language respects the actor.

sentences.japanese: 先生は昨日の学会で、非常に興味深い研究成果をおっしゃいました。
sentences.english: The professor stated highly intriguing research findings at yesterday's academic conference.
sentences.literal: Professor yesterday's conference-at, intriguing findings honorably-said.
sentences.nuanceNote: Elevating professor's speech act via おっしゃる.

sentences.japanese: 先生は何を召し上がりますか。
sentences.english: What will you have to eat/drink, Professor?
sentences.nuanceNote: 召し上がる honors the actor's eating/drinking; do not use it to honor yourself.

sentences.japanese: 先生はもういらっしゃいましたか。
sentences.english: Has the teacher arrived yet?
sentences.nuanceNote: いらっしゃる has the special polite stem いらっしゃい. The intended sense can be come/go/be depending on context.

quiz.question: 社長はもうお昼ご飯を（　　）ましたか。
quiz.translation: Has the company president already eaten lunch?
quiz.grammarFocus: Special honorific verb 召し上がる
quiz.ruleHint: Honorific verb; お + suitable verb stem + になる; some verbs have special forms

explanations.reason: Correct! 召し上がる is the special honorific (尊敬語) verb for 食べる/飲む.
Incorrect. いただく is humble (謙譲語) for oneself eating.
Incorrect. 参る is humble for going/coming.
Incorrect. 拝見する is humble for looking.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 160 (PDF p. 168). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Keigo (敬語) Survival Matrix: Sonkeigo vs Kenjougo
table.subtitle: Elevating the listener/superior (尊敬語) vs humbling yourself/in-group (謙譲語).

rows.label: 行く / 来る / いる
cells: いらっしゃる / おいでになる
参る (まいる) / おる (いる)
Other: お+V-stem+になる | Me: お+V-stem+する
rows.note: 社長はいらっしゃいますか (Is the company president in?)

rows.label: 言う (To say)
cells: おっしゃる
申す (もうす) / 申し上げる
Other says: おっしゃる | I say: 申します
rows.note: 田中と申します (My name is Tanaka - humble).

rows.label: 食べる / 飲む
cells: 召し上がる (めしあがる)
いただく
Other eats: 召し上がる | I eat: いただきます
rows.note: どうぞ召し上がってください (Please enjoy the food).

rows.label: 見る (To look/see)
cells: ご覧になる (ごらんになる)
拝見する (はいけんする)
Other looks: ご覧になる | I inspect: 拝見する
rows.note: 資料を拝見しました (I reviewed the documents).

rows.label: 知っている (To know)
cells: ご存知だ (ごぞんじだ)
存じている (ぞんじている) / 存じ上げている
Other knows: ご存知 | I know: 存じております
rows.note: Never say "私はご存知です" ❌! That is honoring yourself!

rows.label: する (To do)
cells: なさる
致す (いたす)
Other does: なさる | I do: いたします
rows.note: よろしくお願いいたします (Humble request).

title: お + V-stem + ください (Polite Honorific Request: Please Graciously Do)
meaning: A graceful, courteous request formula for superiors or customers: 'Please graciously do X' (much more polite than 〜てください).
connection: お + V-stem + ください (Group 3 する verbs: ご + Noun + ください: ご注意ください)
nuance: CUSTOMER SERVICE REGISTER: Ubiquitous in stores, public transit, and professional offices: お座りください (Please be seated), お入りください (Please come in), ご覧ください (Please take a look).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: お + [Masu-stem] + ください (Native verbs) / ご + [Noun] + ください (Sino-Japanese).

sentences.japanese: 足元が滑りやすくなっておりますので、十分にお気をつけください。
sentences.english: Because the footing has become slippery, please take great care.
sentences.literal: Footing slippery become since, sufficiently take-care please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite safety announcement.

sentences.japanese: 少々お待ちください。
sentences.english: Please wait a moment.
sentences.nuanceNote: お + verb stem + ください makes an honorific request; not every verb takes the pattern freely.

sentences.japanese: こちらの写真をご覧ください。
sentences.english: Please look at this photograph.
sentences.nuanceNote: ご覧ください is the conventional honorific form for looking; do not invent ご見ください.

quiz.question: どうぞこちらのお席にお（　　）ください。
quiz.translation: Please graciously have a seat here in this chair.
quiz.grammarFocus: Honorific request formula お + stem + ください
quiz.ruleHint: お + V-stem + ください (Group 3 する verbs: ご + Noun + ください: ご注意ください)

explanations.reason: Correct! 腰を掛ける stem is 掛け: お掛けください (Please have a seat).
Incorrect. 掛ける is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 掛けて is te-form.
Incorrect. 掛けた is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 160 (PDF p. 168). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てくれてありがとう・〜てよかった
meaning: Thank someone or express relief.
connection: Vてくれて + ありがとう; Vて / Vなくて + よかった
nuance: くれて makes the helpful person's action explicit. よかった evaluates a situation favorably after it occurs.
keyTakeaway: Vてくれて + ありがとう; Vて / Vなくて + よかった

sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれてありがとう。間に合ってよかったです。
sentences.english: Thank you for helping. I am glad we made it in time.

sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれて、ありがとう。
sentences.english: Thank you for helping me.
sentences.nuanceNote: くれる presents the action as a benefit toward the speaker's side. A more formal thanks uses くださってありがとうございます.

sentences.japanese: 無事に着いてよかったです。
sentences.english: I am glad you arrived safely.
sentences.nuanceNote: てよかった evaluates the event positively; it does not mean that the event was morally good in every sense.
