sentences.nuanceNote: Warning against persistent idleness.

sentences.japanese: 毎晩そんなに遅く寝ては、体に悪いですよ。
sentences.english: If you go to bed that late every night, it is bad for your health.
sentences.nuanceNote: ては introduces a condition evaluated negatively in the following clause.

sentences.japanese: この字では、小さすぎて読めません。
sentences.english: With writing like this, it is too small to read.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nでは presents the existing condition as inadequate for the desired result.

quiz.question: こんなに高く（　　）、買えません。
quiz.translation: If it is this expensive, I cannot buy it.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + では negative consequence conditional
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + は | い-adj くて + は | な-adj / Noun + では

explanations.reason: 高い becomes 高くては.
高くには is not this construction.
高くでは is not the required adjective te-form.
高くとは is not the required conditional form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 32 (PDF p. 55). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜さえ〜ば (If Only / Provided That Sole Prerequisite Is Met)
meaning: As long as; if only the highlighted condition is satisfied.
connection: Noun + さえ + V-ば / い-adj-ければ / な-adj-なら / Noun + なら | V-stem + さえすれば
nuance: Highlights a condition the speaker treats as sufficient for the stated result. It does not assert that every other circumstance in the world is irrelevant. Nさえ attaches to the focused item; V-stemさえすれば focuses on performing an action.
keyTakeaway: Highlights a condition the speaker treats as sufficient for the stated result. It does not assert that every other circumstance in the world is irrelevant. Nさえ attaches to the focused item; V-stemさえすれば focuses on performing an action.

sentences.japanese: パスポートさえあれば、とりあえず飛行機に乗ることはできる。
sentences.english: As long as you have your passport, you can board the plane for the time being.
sentences.literal: Passport only if-exists, for-now airplane board can.

tokens.word: パスポートさえあれば
tokens.meaning: if only you have a passport
tokens.reading: ぱすぽーとさえあれば

sentences.nuanceNote: Highlighting the indispensable prerequisite.

sentences.japanese: 住所さえ分かれば、荷物を送れます。
sentences.english: As long as I know the address, I can send the package.
sentences.nuanceNote: さえ highlights the condition the speaker treats as sufficient.

sentences.japanese: 毎日練習しさえすれば、少しずつ上達します。
sentences.english: As long as you practice every day, you will gradually improve.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + さえすれば emphasizes carrying out the action. It expresses the speaker's assessment, not a universal guarantee.

quiz.question: 薬を飲み（　　）すれば、すぐに熱は下がりますよ。
quiz.translation: As long as you just take your medicine, your fever will go down promptly.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + さえすれば (Sole required action)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + さえ + V-ば / い-adj-ければ / な-adj-なら / Noun + なら | V-stem + さえすれば

explanations.reason: Correct! Verb-stem + さえすれば expresses 'as long as you just do X'.
Incorrect. こそすれば is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. すらすれば is invalid.
Incorrect. ばかりすれば means repeatedly doing nothing else.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 32 (PDF p. 55). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: たとえ〜ても (Even If / Even Granting That Hypothetical X Occurs)
meaning: Even if X is assumed, Y still holds.
connection: たとえ + Vても / adjectiveくても / Nでも / な-adjectiveでも
nuance: たとえ explicitly introduces a hypothetical concession. The result may be a fact, judgment, intention or recommendation; it need not be the speaker's unshakable resolve. Distinguish a hypothetical case from a known fact, although ても itself can be used with either.
keyTakeaway: The assumed condition does not overturn the conclusion.

sentences.japanese: たとえどんなに給料が高くても、危険な仕事は引き受けたくない。
sentences.english: Even if the salary were exceptionally high, I would never want to undertake a hazardous job.
sentences.literal: Even-if how-much salary high-even-if, dangerous job undertake not-want.
sentences.nuanceNote: Steadfast refusal prioritizing personal safety over money.

sentences.japanese: たとえ雨が降っても、試合は行います。
sentences.english: Even if it rains, the match will go ahead.
sentences.nuanceNote: The assumed obstacle does not change the stated decision.

sentences.japanese: たとえ無料でも、必要のない物はもらいません。
sentences.english: Even if something is free, I will not take it if I do not need it.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nでも forms the concession; it is not Nても.

quiz.question: （　　）失敗しても、最後まで全力を尽くしたなら悔いはない。
quiz.translation: Even if I fail, as long as I gave it my absolute all until the very end, I will have no regrets.
quiz.grammarFocus: たとえ〜ても (Hypothetical concession)
quiz.ruleHint: たとえ + Vても / adjectiveくても / Nでも / な-adjectiveでも

explanations.reason: Correct! たとえ pairs with 〜ても to mean 'Even if / Even supposing that'.
Incorrect. まるで pairs with ようだ ('just like').
Incorrect. 決して pairs with negative verbs ('never').
Incorrect. まさか expresses disbelief ('don't tell me...').

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 32 (PDF p. 55). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜なら・〜ば・〜たら
meaning: Select a conditional to match the relation between clauses.
connection: Plain form + なら; conditional ば; past form + ら
nuance: なら takes up a premise and can give advice before the action. たら can mean after completion. ば describes a sufficient condition; restrictions on requests depend on predicates and subjects.
keyTakeaway: Plain form + なら; conditional ば; past form + ら

sentences.japanese: 京都に行くなら、先にホテルを予約したほうがいいです。
sentences.english: If you are going to Kyoto, you should book a hotel first.

sentences.japanese: 京都へ行くなら、この地図を持っていってください。
sentences.english: If you are going to Kyoto, take this map with you.
sentences.nuanceNote: なら takes the proposed trip as a premise. The map is taken before or during the trip; なら does not mean after.

sentences.japanese: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
sentences.english: Please call when you arrive at the station.
sentences.nuanceNote: たら permits a request triggered after arrival.

sentences.japanese: 時間があれば、参加します。
sentences.english: If I have time, I will participate.
sentences.nuanceNote: A stative ば condition can accompany the speaker's intention. Do not ban intentions after every ば clause.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 32 (PDF p. 55). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ということだ・〜とのことだ
meaning: Report information received.
connection: Plain clause + ということだ / とのことだ
nuance: A formal way to relay news or a message. ということだ can also express an interpretation, so identify whether there is an information source.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + ということだ / とのことだ

sentences.japanese: 連絡によると、会議は延期されたとのことです。
sentences.english: According to the message, the meeting has been postponed.

sentences.japanese: 受付の人によると、面接は三階で行うとのことです。
sentences.english: According to the receptionist, the interview will be held on the third floor.
sentences.nuanceNote: とのことだ formally relays information from a source; it is not a claim of direct observation.

sentences.japanese: 案内によると、参加費は無料だということです。
sentences.english: According to the notice, participation is free.
sentences.useLabel: Reported information with a noun predicate
sentences.nuanceNote: A noun predicate retains だ before reported ということだ. 案内によると identifies the information source.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 36 (PDF p. 59). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜と言われている
meaning: Report a widespread view.
connection: Plain clause + と言われている
nuance: The passive presents what people commonly say, without identifying a particular speaker. It does not itself prove the claim.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + と言われている

sentences.japanese: この町は住みやすいと言われています。
sentences.english: This town is said to be easy to live in.

sentences.japanese: その建物には百年の歴史があると言われていますが、資料は残っていません。
sentences.english: The building is said to have a hundred-year history, but no records remain.
sentences.nuanceNote: と言われている reports a claim without proving its truth.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 36 (PDF p. 59). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜とか・〜って・〜という
meaning: Informal reports, quotations and labels.
connection: Plain clause + とか / って; name or clause + というN
nuance: とか can relay uncertain information; って is casual. という links a name or content to a following noun. Do not confuse hearsay とか with listing AとかBとか.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + とか / って; name or clause + というN

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは来月引っ越すとか。
sentences.english: I hear Tanaka is moving next month.

sentences.japanese: 店は今日は休みだって。
sentences.english: I heard the shop is closed today.
sentences.nuanceNote: って is a casual reporting form here; the noun predicate has だ.

sentences.japanese: 鈴木さんという人から電話がありました。
sentences.english: There was a call from someone named Suzuki.
sentences.nuanceNote: という links a name to a following noun. This naming use is different from a full reported proposition.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 36 (PDF p. 59). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜とは限らない (Partial Truth: Not Necessarily the Case)
meaning: Denies the absolute validity of a generalization: 'It does not necessarily mean that X is always true in every single case'.
connection: Plain form + とは限らない (Frequently pairs with adverbs: 必ずしも, いつも, だれもが)
nuance: DEBUNKING ASSUMPTIONS: '高いものが必ずしも良いとは限らない' (Expensive things are not necessarily good). Softens rigid dogmas.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: 必ずしも [Plain form] とは限らない = Not always necessarily true!

sentences.japanese: 有名大学を卒業したからといって、仕事ができるとは限りません。
sentences.english: Just because someone graduated from a famous university, it does not necessarily mean they are competent at work.
sentences.literal: Famous university graduated just-because, work able is-not-necessarily.

tokens.word: できるとは限りません
tokens.reading: できるとはかぎりません

sentences.nuanceNote: Debunking academic credentials as sole proof of competence.

sentences.japanese: 高い物が必ずしも長持ちするとは限りません。
sentences.english: Expensive things do not necessarily last a long time.
sentences.nuanceNote: Some may last, but the price does not guarantee that result.

sentences.japanese: 週末だからといって、いつも暇だとは限りません。
sentences.english: Just because it is the weekend does not mean I am always free.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negation targets an assumed generalization; it does not mean I am never free.

quiz.question: 高い服が長持ちするとは（　　）。
quiz.translation: Expensive clothes do not necessarily last long.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜とは限らない partial negation
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + とは限らない (Frequently pairs with adverbs: 必ずしも, いつも, だれもが)

explanations.reason: とは限らない means not necessarily.
限りない means boundless and is a different form.
限って does not finish this negative conclusion.
限らずに is a connective needing more material.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 61). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ないことはない / 〜ないこともない (Double Negative Litotes: It's Not That I Can't)
meaning: Double negative expressing reluctant admission or modest possibility: 'It's not that I completely can't do it... / If pushed, I could possibly manage'.
connection: V-ない + ことはない | い-adj くない + ことはない | な-adj / Noun でない + ことはない
nuance: RELUCTANT HESITATION: You don't want to boast 'I can do it easily'. You say '走れば間に合わないことはない' (If I run, it's not that I couldn't make it).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Negative] + ことはない = Double negative! 'It is not impossible for me to do X'.

sentences.japanese: 納豆はあまり好きではありませんが、食べられないことはありません。
sentences.english: I don't like natto very much, but it's not that I can't eat it if offered.
sentences.literal: Natto not-very like-not but, eat-cannot fact-is-not.

tokens.word: 食べられないことはありません
tokens.meaning: it is not that I cannot eat it
tokens.reading: たべられないことはありません

sentences.nuanceNote: Reluctant dietary concession.

sentences.japanese: 一人でできないことはないですが、時間がかかります。
sentences.english: It is not impossible to do it alone, but it will take time.
sentences.nuanceNote: The double negative acknowledges possibility while keeping a reservation.

sentences.japanese: おいしくないことはないけれど、少し高いです。
sentences.english: It is not that it is not tasty, but it is a little expensive.
sentences.nuanceNote: An い-adjective negative can form the same qualified affirmation.

quiz.question: 時間はかかりますが、一人ででき（　　）ことはありません。
quiz.translation: It takes time, but it is not impossible to do it alone.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ない + こともない double negative
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない + ことはない | い-adj くない + ことはない | な-adj / Noun でない + ことはない

explanations.reason: できないことはない concedes that it is possible.
なく does not directly modify こと here.
なかったの adds an unnecessary の.
なくて is connective and cannot directly modify こと.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 61). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜わけがない (There Is Absolutely No Way That... / Utter Impossibility)
meaning: Expresses the speaker's adamant, logical conclusion that something is completely impossible or out of the question.
connection: 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + の/である) + わけがない / わけはない
nuance: Expresses the speaker's strong rejection of a possibility, often based on a stated reason. The form does not turn the speaker's belief into an objective or mathematical proof. Contrast わけではない, which denies an inference or a full/general claim without necessarily asserting the opposite.
keyTakeaway: Expresses the speaker's strong rejection of a possibility, often based on a stated reason. The form does not turn the speaker's belief into an objective or mathematical proof. Contrast わけではない, which denies an inference or a full/general claim without necessarily asserting the opposite.

sentences.japanese: こんなに複雑なプロジェクトを、たった一人で一日で終わらせられるわけがない。
sentences.english: There is absolutely no way that a project this complex could be finished by a single person in just one day.
sentences.literal: This complex project, just one-person-by one-day-in can-finish no-way.

tokens.word: 終わらせられるわけがない
tokens.meaning: there's no way it could be finished
tokens.reading: おわらせられるわけがない

sentences.nuanceNote: Adamant rejection of unrealistic workload expectation.

sentences.japanese: まだ五歳なのだから、こんな難しい本が読めるわけがありません。
sentences.english: Since the child is only five, there is no way they can read a book this difficult.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker rejects the possibility based on a premise; this expresses the speaker's reasoning, not independently verified impossibility.

sentences.japanese: あの人が犯人のわけがない。
sentences.english: That person cannot possibly be the culprit.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのわけがない is a strong denial. である can also link a noun in a more formal style.

quiz.question: 一日で全部覚えられるわけ（　　）ない。
quiz.translation: There is no way I can memorize it all in one day.
quiz.grammarFocus: 普通形 + わけがない (Logical impossibility)
quiz.ruleHint: 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + の/である) + わけがない / わけはない

explanations.reason: わけがない denies the possibility.
を is not the particle in this pattern.
わけにない is incomplete; わけにはいかない is different.
と is not the particle in this pattern.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 61). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜わけではない (It Doesn't Mean That... / Partial Negation)
meaning: Softens an assumption or clarifies that while things might appear so, it is not entirely or universally true: 'Not necessarily / It's not that...'.
connection: 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + の/な/である) + わけではない / わけじゃない
nuance: Denies a proposed interpretation, reason or generalization. The scope matters: 全部分かったわけではない denies understanding everything, while 嫌いなわけではない denies dislike as the explanation. It is not invariably a weak partial denial; it can reject the whole particular inference.
keyTakeaway: Denies a proposed interpretation, reason or generalization. The scope matters: 全部分かったわけではない denies understanding everything, while 嫌いなわけではない denies dislike as the explanation. It is not invariably a weak partial denial; it can reject the whole particular inference.

sentences.japanese: 日本に住んでいるからといって、誰もが日本語を上手に話せるわけではない。
sentences.english: Just because someone lives in Japan does not mean that everyone can speak Japanese fluently.
sentences.literal: Japan-in living just-because, everyone Japanese skillfully can-speak not-necessarily.

tokens.meaning: does not mean they can speak
tokens.reading: はなせるわけではない

sentences.nuanceNote: Refuting an overly simplistic stereotype.

sentences.japanese: 嫌いなわけではありませんが、今日は食べたくありません。
sentences.english: It is not that I dislike it, but I do not want to eat it today.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker denies the inferred reason, not the factual refusal to eat.

sentences.japanese: 全部分かったわけではありません。
sentences.english: It is not that I understood everything.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative applies to understanding everything. Some parts may have been understood.

quiz.question: 嫌いだという意味ではありません。嫌いなわけ（　　）ありません。
quiz.translation: It does not mean that I dislike it.
quiz.grammarFocus: な-adj + な + わけではない (Partial denial)
quiz.ruleHint: 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + の/な/である) + わけではない / わけじゃない

explanations.reason: わけではない denies the stated interpretation.
を does not form this negative predicate.
に does not form this construction.
と does not form this construction.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 61). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ことは〜が
meaning: Concede a point with a reservation.
connection: V/い-adjective + ことは + same predicate + が
nuance: Repeat the predicate: 読んだことは読んだが admits reading while qualifying what that means. It does not deny the action happened.
keyTakeaway: V/い-adjective + ことは + same predicate + が

sentences.japanese: 読んだことは読みましたが、全部は理解できませんでした。
sentences.english: I did read it, but I could not understand all of it.

sentences.japanese: 読んだことは読みましたが、細かいところは覚えていません。
sentences.english: I did read it, but I do not remember the details.
sentences.useLabel: Admit an action, add a reservation
sentences.nuanceNote: The verb is repeated with matching tense; the first clause concedes the action.

sentences.japanese: 安いことは安いですが、駅から遠いです。
sentences.english: It is cheap, certainly, but it is far from the station.
sentences.useLabel: Admit a quality, qualify its importance
sentences.nuanceNote: The adjective is conceded, then another consideration limits the endorsement.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 61). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜がる / 〜がっている (Third-Person Manifestation of Desires & Sensations)
meaning: Describes observable behaviors indicating that someone other than the speaker feels an emotion, sensation, or desire.
connection: い-adj (drop い) + がる / がっている | な-adj (drop な) + がる | V-たい (drop い) + たがる / たがっている
nuance: がる describes observable indications of a feeling or desire, often about someone else. Reports, quotations and narrative contexts also allow other ways to describe a third person; it is not a blanket ban on third-person adjective predicates.
keyTakeaway: がる describes observable indications of a feeling or desire, often about someone else. Reports, quotations and narrative contexts also allow other ways to describe a third person; it is not a blanket ban on third-person adjective predicates.

sentences.japanese: 弟は注射をひどく怖がって、病院の前で泣き出してしまった。
sentences.english: My little brother showed tremendous fear of the injection and burst into tears in front of the hospital.
sentences.literal: Little-brother injection terribly feared-showing, hospital front burst-out-crying.
sentences.nuanceNote: Describing observable childish reaction to medical procedure.

sentences.japanese: うちの猫は外に出たがって、ドアの前で鳴いている。
sentences.english: Our cat wants to go outside and is meowing in front of the door.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜たがる describes an observable third-person desire through physical behavior.

sentences.japanese: 彼は注射をひどく痛がっていた。
sentences.english: He was showing severe pain from the injection.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜がる attaches to an adjective stem to report observed discomfort rather than claiming direct telepathy.

quiz.question: 子供が外へ行きた（　　）います。
quiz.translation: The child is showing that they want to go outside.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-たい → たがらなくなる (3rd person desire trend)
quiz.ruleHint: い-adj (drop い) + がる / がっている | な-adj (drop な) + がる | V-たい (drop い) + たがる / たがっている

explanations.reason: たがっている reports observable desire in progress.
たがる does not attach directly to います.
たがり does not attach directly to います.
たがった does not attach directly to います.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 44 (PDF p. 67). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てもらいたい・〜てほしい
meaning: Want another person to do something.
connection: Person に Vてもらいたい / Vてほしい
nuance: てもらいたい frames the wish as receiving a favor; てほしい directly describes the desired action. Negative wishes use Vないでほしい.
keyTakeaway: Person に Vてもらいたい / Vてほしい

sentences.japanese: 先生に作文を確認してもらいたいです。
sentences.english: I would like my teacher to check my composition.

sentences.japanese: 先生に作文を見てもらいたいです。
sentences.english: I would like my teacher to look over my essay.
sentences.nuanceNote: に marks the person whose help is desired; もらいたい frames receiving the favor.

sentences.japanese: 子供には健康でいてほしいです。
sentences.english: I want my child to stay healthy.
sentences.nuanceNote: てほしい states the speaker's desired situation for someone else, not that person's own desire.

sentences.japanese: ここでは写真を撮らないでほしいです。
sentences.english: I would like people not to take photos here.
sentences.useLabel: Want someone not to do something
sentences.nuanceNote: Vないでほしい requests the absence of an action. Tone and relationship affect how direct it sounds.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 44 (PDF p. 67). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜させてもらいたい
meaning: Want permission to do something.
connection: Causativeて + もらいたい / いただきたい / ほしい
nuance: The speaker wants to be allowed to act. いただきたい is more deferential; permission and benefit should be relevant, not merely a decorative honorific.
keyTakeaway: Causativeて + もらいたい / いただきたい / ほしい

sentences.japanese: 次の会議で私にも発表させていただきたいです。
sentences.english: I would also like permission to present at the next meeting.

sentences.japanese: 会議で私にも意見を言わせてもらいたいです。
sentences.english: I would like to be allowed to express my opinion at the meeting too.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker wants permission to perform the causative-marked action, not to make the listener speak.

sentences.japanese: 事情を説明させていただきたいのですが。
sentences.english: I would like to be allowed to explain the circumstances.
sentences.nuanceNote: いただきたい is more deferential than もらいたい. Permission/benefit must fit the situation; the phrase is not a universal politeness decoration.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 44 (PDF p. 67). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜といい・〜ばいい・〜たらいい
meaning: Express a hope or suggest a solution.
connection: Plain non-past + といい; conditional ば/たら + いい
nuance: In a wish, the desired outcome is not presented as fully under the speaker's control. The same forms can also give advice, depending on context.
keyTakeaway: Plain non-past + といい; conditional ば/たら + いい

sentences.japanese: 明日は晴れるといいですね。
sentences.english: I hope it is sunny tomorrow.

sentences.japanese: 旅行の日、晴れるといいですね。
sentences.english: I hope it is sunny on the day of your trip.
sentences.nuanceNote: といい can express a wish about something outside the speaker's direct control.

sentences.japanese: 来年、日本へ行けたらいいなと思っています。
sentences.english: I am hoping I can go to Japan next year.
sentences.nuanceNote: The potential 行ける makes the desired possibility clear. たらいい is not limited to giving advice.

sentences.japanese: もう少し時間があればいいのですが。
sentences.english: I wish I had a little more time.
sentences.nuanceNote: ばいい can express a wish; context distinguishes this from a suggestion about what to do.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 44 (PDF p. 67). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜べきだ / 〜べきではない (Should / Ought To - Moral Duty)
meaning: Should; ought to; what one judges appropriate.
connection: V-辞書形 + べきだ / べきではない (する irregular: すべきだ or するべきだ)
nuance: Expresses what is appropriate, expected or advisable from the speaker's viewpoint. It can sound strong or moralizing, but is not restricted to universally agreed moral duties. Both するべき and すべき occur.
keyTakeaway: Expresses what is appropriate, expected or advisable from the speaker's viewpoint. It can sound strong or moralizing, but is not restricted to universally agreed moral duties. Both するべき and すべき occur.

sentences.japanese: 借りたお金は、どんなに親しい友人であっても期日通りに返す（　　）だ。
sentences.english: Money that you have borrowed ought to be repaid right on schedule, no matter how close a friend they may be.
sentences.literal: Borrowed money, how-much close friend even-if schedule-according repay ought-to is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Moral principle governing personal financial integrity.

sentences.japanese: 間違いに気づいたら、すぐに訂正すべきです。
sentences.english: If you notice a mistake, you should correct it promptly.
sentences.nuanceNote: べき expresses what the speaker judges appropriate; it is stronger than a neutral prediction.

sentences.japanese: 人の秘密を勝手に話すべきではありません。
sentences.english: You should not disclose someone else's secrets without permission.
sentences.nuanceNote: べきではない advises against the action. It is different from saying the action is physically impossible.

quiz.question: ミスに気づいたら、すぐに訂正す（　　）です。
quiz.translation: If you notice a mistake, you should correct it promptly.
quiz.grammarFocus: する → すべきだ (Moral imperative)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + べきだ / べきではない (する irregular: すべきだ or するべきだ)

explanations.reason: すべきです expresses what should be done.
べく is a connective form, not the predicate before です here.
べきな is not the predicate form.
べかった is not a conjugation of べき.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 69). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜によると / 〜によれば (According To Source of Information)
meaning: According to a source of information.
connection: Source noun + によると / によれば
nuance: Names the source rather than claiming direct personal observation. It commonly accompanies そうだ, らしい, ということだ and similar reporting endings, but these are not mandatory in every report. Distinguish によって for means, cause, agency or variation.
keyTakeaway: Identify the information source; reported-style endings are common, not obligatory.

sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日の夕方から関東地方全域で大雪になるそうだ。
sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, heavy snow will reportedly blanket the entire Kanto region starting tomorrow evening.
sentences.literal: Weather forecast according-to, tomorrow evening-from Kanto entire heavy-snow become reportedly.

tokens.reading: てんきよほうによると

sentences.nuanceNote: Formal citation of meteorological bulletin.

sentences.japanese: 最近の世論調査によると、内閣支持率はやや下落したそうだ。
sentences.english: According to a recent public opinion survey, cabinet approval ratings reportedly dropped slightly.
sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + によると pairs with hearsay ending 〜そうだ to formally cite statistical data.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんの話によれば、部長は来月転勤するらしい。
sentences.english: According to what Tanaka said, the department manager will apparently transfer next month.
sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + によれば pairs with evidential conjecture 〜らしい.

quiz.question: 今朝の新聞（　　）よると、ガソリン価格が来月から再び値上がりするそうだ。
quiz.translation: According to this morning's newspaper, gasoline prices will reportedly hike again starting next month.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + によると (Citing sources)
quiz.ruleHint: Source noun + によると / によれば

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun + によると is the fixed citation pattern.
Incorrect. でよると does not exist.
Incorrect. をよると is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. へよると is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 69). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 命令・禁止・〜こと
meaning: Direct instructions and written rules.
connection: U-verb e-row; ru-verb stem+ろ; する→しろ; V dictionary+な; V dictionary/ない+こと
nuance: Imperatives and Vな prohibitions are strong. Sentence-final こと often appears in written instructions and rules. It is not the same as nominalizing a verb.
keyTakeaway: U-verb e-row; ru-verb stem+ろ; する→しろ; V dictionary+な; V dictionary/ない+こと

sentences.japanese: 試験中は辞書を使わないこと。
sentences.english: Do not use a dictionary during the exam.

sentences.japanese: 危ない！止まれ！
sentences.english: Watch out! Stop!
sentences.nuanceNote: The imperative can be appropriate in an urgent warning; in ordinary requests it may sound forceful.

sentences.japanese: ここに入るな。
sentences.english: Do not enter here.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary verb + な is a direct prohibition, not the explanatory な used before の.

sentences.japanese: 提出前に、名前を確認すること。
sentences.english: Check your name before submitting.
sentences.nuanceNote: Sentence-final こと is used for written rules/instructions. It is not a conversational request in the same register as ください.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 69). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜たらどうか
meaning: Suggest a course of action.
connection: Vた + らどうか / らどうですか
nuance: Usually advice to someone else. Tone and relationship determine whether it sounds supportive or critical.
keyTakeaway: Vた + らどうか / らどうですか

sentences.japanese: 一度、先生に相談したらどうですか。
sentences.english: Why not consult your teacher once?

sentences.japanese: 一度、先生に相談してみたらどうですか。
sentences.english: Why not try consulting your teacher once?
sentences.nuanceNote: The past-form shape is part of the suggestion construction, not a report that consultation already happened.

sentences.japanese: そんなに疲れているなら、少し休んだらどう。
sentences.english: If you are that tired, why not rest a little?
sentences.nuanceNote: Tone determines whether the suggestion sounds caring or impatient; it is not automatically polite in every relationship.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 69). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜(よ)うとする (On the Very Verge Of / In the Act of Attempting)
meaning: 1) Inception: Right at the exact moment of about to execute an action. 2) Effort: Actively attempting or striving to achieve X.
connection: V-意向形 + とする (Past: とした / としていた) | Negative: としない (Refuses to do)
nuance: Volitional + とする can mark an attempt or an imminent event. The attempt may fail, and an imminent event need not have a human agent. ようとしない describes lack of willingness or attempt; stubbornness is an interpretation from context, not a required meaning.
keyTakeaway: Volitional + とする can mark an attempt or an imminent event. The attempt may fail, and an imminent event need not have a human agent. ようとしない describes lack of willingness or attempt; stubbornness is an interpretation from context, not a required meaning.

sentences.japanese: 電車に乗ろうとした瞬間、ドアが目の前で閉まってしまった。
sentences.english: The instant I attempted to board the train, the doors shut right in front of my eyes.
sentences.literal: Train board-attempted instant, doors eyes-front-at closed-regrettably.

tokens.meaning: the moment I attempted to board
tokens.reading: のろうとしたしゅんかん

sentences.nuanceNote: Interrupted boarding action.

sentences.japanese: ドアを開けようとしましたが、鍵がかかっていました。
sentences.english: I tried to open the door, but it was locked.
sentences.nuanceNote: The volitional form plus とする indicates an attempt; it does not guarantee success.

sentences.japanese: 電車が発車しようとしています。
sentences.english: The train is about to depart.
sentences.nuanceNote: This use describes an imminent event, not a personal intention belonging to the train.

sentences.japanese: 何度頼んでも、彼は話そうとしません。
sentences.english: No matter how often I ask, he will not try to speak.
sentences.nuanceNote: ようとしない describes a lack of willingness or attempt, rather than ordinary inability.

quiz.question: うちの犬は、お風呂に（　　）とすると、必死で逃げ出そうとする。
quiz.translation: Whenever I attempt to put my dog in the bath, he desperately tries to flee.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-意向形 + とする (Attempting action)
quiz.ruleHint: V-意向形 + とする (Past: とした / としていた) | Negative: としない (Refuses to do)

explanations.reason: Correct! 入れる volitional is 入れよう + とする (Attempting to put into bath).
Incorrect. 入れる is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 入れ is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 入れた is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 50 (PDF p. 73). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ようにする (Make an Effort To / Endeavor Habitually)
meaning: Indicates that the subject makes a conscious, ongoing effort or resolves to build a habit of doing (or not doing) action X.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ようにする / ようにしている
nuance: CONSCIOUS HABITUAL EFFORT: ようにしている expresses an established personal policy: '毎朝ストレッチをするようにしている' (I make it a point to stretch every morning).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-る / V-ない + ようにする = 'Make sure to do / Endeavor to do!'.

sentences.japanese: 健康のために、夜遅くには甘いものを食べないようにしている。
sentences.english: For the sake of my health, I make it a strict rule to avoid eating sweets late at night.
sentences.literal: Health-of sake-for, night late sweets eat-not endeavor-am-doing.

tokens.word: 食べないようにしている
tokens.meaning: make a point of not eating
tokens.reading: たべないようにしている

sentences.nuanceNote: Active self-discipline regarding dietary lifestyle.

sentences.japanese: 忘れ物をしないように、出かける前に確認します。
sentences.english: I check before going out so that I do not forget anything.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative clause specifies the outcome the speaker tries to avoid.

sentences.japanese: 毎日少しでも歩くようにしています。
sentences.english: I make an effort to walk at least a little every day.
sentences.nuanceNote: ようにしている presents ongoing effort; it does not claim perfect success on every occasion.

quiz.question: 約束の時間には絶対に遅れない（　　）してください。
quiz.translation: Please make sure you do not arrive late for the promised time.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ない + ようにする (Urging effort)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ようにする / ようにしている

explanations.reason: Correct! ようにしてください is the polite formula for urging conscious adherence.
Incorrect. ためにしてください is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. ことにしてください means 'please pretend/decide'.
Incorrect. ものにしてください is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 50 (PDF p. 73). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ことにしている (Habitual Personal Rule / Self-Imposed Policy)
meaning: Indicates a conscious, self-imposed rule or habitual code of conduct that the speaker upholds consistently.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-ない形 + ことにしている
nuance: Presents a maintained personal decision or practice. Compare ようにしている (effort to behave that way) and ことになっている (an established arrangement). The contrast is one of presentation; the latter does not necessarily prove an outside authority made the decision.
keyTakeaway: Presents a maintained personal decision or practice. Compare ようにしている (effort to behave that way) and ことになっている (an established arrangement). The contrast is one of presentation; the latter does not necessarily prove an outside authority made the decision.

sentences.japanese: どんなに忙しくても、毎日必ず30分は読書をすることにしている。
sentences.english: No matter how busy I am, I make it a strict personal rule to read for at least 30 minutes every day.
sentences.literal: How-much busy even-if, every-day definitely 30-minutes reading do-rule-have.

tokens.word: 読書をすることにしている
tokens.meaning: make it a rule to read
tokens.reading: どくしょをすることにしている
tokens.romaji: dokusho o suru koto ni shite iru

sentences.nuanceNote: Disciplined intellectual daily habit.

sentences.japanese: 夜十時以降は仕事のメールを見ないことにしています。
sentences.english: I make it a rule not to check work email after ten at night.
sentences.nuanceNote: ことにしている presents a policy chosen and maintained by the speaker.

sentences.japanese: 毎月、給料の一部を貯金することにしています。
sentences.english: I make it a practice to save part of my salary every month.
sentences.nuanceNote: Compare ようにしている, which emphasizes trying to maintain the behavior rather than declaring the rule itself.

quiz.question: 環境を守るため、買い物にはマイバッグを持参する（　　）にしている。
quiz.translation: To protect the environment, I make it a policy to bring my own shopping bag when buying goods.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + ことにしている (Personal code)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない形 + ことにしている

explanations.reason: Correct! 持参することにしている expresses an intentional self-directed eco-friendly habit.
Incorrect. ものにしている does not express personal rules.
Incorrect. わけにしている is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. ところにしている is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 50 (PDF p. 73). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜つもり (Believing / Acting as If / Contrary to Reality)
meaning: Expresses that the subject acts with the internal belief or mental mindset of X, regardless of whether external reality or others agree.
connection: V-た形 / Noun + の / い-adj / な-adj + な + つもり (Noun modifier)
nuance: CONVICTION VS REALITY: Can convey a subjective illusion: '自分では若いつもりだが、階段で息が切れる' (I feel young in my own mind, but I get out of breath on stairs). Or reproaching someone: '冗談のつもりだった' (I intended it as a joke).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た / Nounの + つもり = 'In my mind / Believing that I had done so (even if reality differs)'.

sentences.japanese: 鍵を閉めたつもりだったが、帰宅したらドアが開いていてぞっとした。
sentences.english: I was under the firm impression that I had locked the door, but returning home I was terrified to find it wide open.
sentences.literal: Key locked impression-had, home-returned door open-being horrified.
sentences.nuanceNote: Chilling discovery of a mistaken assumption.

sentences.japanese: 十分説明したつもりでしたが、伝わっていませんでした。
sentences.english: I thought I had explained it adequately, but it had not got across.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたつもり expresses the speaker's belief about what they had done, not a future intention.

sentences.japanese: 先生になったつもりで、この問題を説明してください。
sentences.english: Explain this problem as if you were the teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: つもりで asks someone to adopt an imagined role for the action.

quiz.question: 自分では上手に説明した（　　）だったが、誰にも理解してもらえなかった。
quiz.translation: In my own mind I believed I had explained it clearly, but nobody understood me.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た + つもり (Mistaken subjective impression)
quiz.ruleHint: V-た形 / Noun + の / い-adj / な-adj + な + つもり (Noun modifier)

explanations.reason: Correct! 説明したつもりだった reflects internal conviction contradicted by the listeners' bewilderment.
Incorrect. はずだった means 'was supposed to' (expectation that failed to happen).
Incorrect. わけだった does not express subjective misconception.
Incorrect. ところだった means 'was on the verge of'.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 50 (PDF p. 73). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: お〜になる / ご〜になる (Honorific Respect - Elevating Others' Actions)
meaning: Transforms a regular verb into a respectful honorific (尊敬語) to elevate the actions of an esteemed superior, client, or guest.
connection: お + V-stem + になる (wago) | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + になる / なさる (kango)
nuance: Respectful language elevates the person performing an action. Whether a colleague or family member is in-group depends on whom you are addressing; speaking internally about a superior differs from representing your company to an outsider.
keyTakeaway: Respectful language elevates the person performing an action. Whether a colleague or family member is in-group depends on whom you are addressing; speaking internally about a superior differs from representing your company to an outsider.

sentences.japanese: 部長は今朝のニュースをすでにお読みになりましたか。
sentences.english: Department manager, have you already read this morning's news?
sentences.literal: Department-manager morning news already honorably-read became-question?

tokens.word: お読みになりましたか
tokens.reading: およみになりましたか

sentences.nuanceNote: Deferential query directed upward toward department head.

sentences.japanese: 先生はもうお帰りになりました。
sentences.english: The teacher has already gone home.
sentences.nuanceNote: お + verb stem + になる honors the teacher's action, not the speaker's.

sentences.japanese: お客様はロビーでお待ちになっています。
sentences.english: The guest is waiting in the lobby.
sentences.nuanceNote: The honorific form is about the person being respected, not simply anyone older than the speaker.

quiz.question: 先生、こちらの新しい資料をもうご（　　）になりましたか。
quiz.translation: Professor, have you already reviewed this new reference material?
quiz.grammarFocus: ご覧になる (Honorific vision)
quiz.ruleHint: お + V-stem + になる (wago) | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + になる / なさる (kango)

explanations.reason: Correct! ご覧になる is the honorific form of 見る ('to look/review').
Incorrect. ご見になる is ungrammatical.
拝見する is humble for an in-group person viewing something; it does not form the teacher-honorifying ご覧になる pattern.
Incorrect. ご見せになる is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 52 (PDF p. 75). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: お〜する / ご〜する (Humble Deference - Lowering One's Own Actions)
meaning: Transforms an action performed by the speaker into a humble deferential (謙譲語), lowering oneself to demonstrate respect to the recipient.
connection: お + V-stem + する / いたす | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + する / いたす
nuance: The お〜する / ご〜する pattern commonly lowers an in-group action directed toward someone respected. The respected person need not be the listener. Not every verb accepts the productive pattern, and some have special forms such as 拝見する. Distinguish humble/polite forms such as 参る, 申す and おる, which can show deference toward the listener without an honored action-recipient.
keyTakeaway: The お〜する / ご〜する pattern commonly lowers an in-group action directed toward someone respected. The respected person need not be the listener. Not every verb accepts the productive pattern, and some have special forms such as 拝見する. Distinguish humble/polite forms such as 参る, 申す and おる, which can show deference toward the listener without an honored action-recipient.

sentences.japanese: 明日の午後に、こちらから改めてお電話いたします。
sentences.english: I will personally telephone you once again tomorrow afternoon.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow afternoon, from-here again humble-phone will-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite corporate commitment to follow up by phone.

sentences.japanese: 資料は私がお届けします。
sentences.english: I will deliver the materials.
sentences.nuanceNote: お届けする humbles the speaker's action toward its recipient.

sentences.japanese: 先生に研究の結果をご報告しました。
sentences.english: I reported the research results to my teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: ご + suitable suru-noun + する. Prefix choice and whether the pattern is idiomatic must be learned with the expression.

quiz.question: 私が先生に資料をお送り（　　）。
quiz.translation: I will send the materials to my teacher.
quiz.grammarFocus: ご + Kango + ください (Polite client request)
quiz.ruleHint: お + V-stem + する / いたす | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + する / いたす

explanations.reason: お送りする is the humble construction.
お送りになる is respectful and inappropriate for the speaker's own action here.
お送りされる is not the intended humble construction.
お送りなります is not a valid form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 52 (PDF p. 75). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 謙譲語II・丁寧語
meaning: Distinguish listener-oriented modest speech from polite endings.
connection: 申す・参る・おります; です・ます・ございます
nuance: 謙譲語I respects the person an action is directed toward; 謙譲語II is modest speech toward the listener. 丁寧語 marks politeness without changing who acts.
keyTakeaway: 申す・参る・おります; です・ます・ございます

sentences.japanese: 私は駅の近くに住んでおります。
sentences.english: I live near the station. (Modest/polite)

sentences.japanese: 私は山田と申します。
sentences.english: My name is Yamada.
sentences.nuanceNote: 申す presents the speaker's saying politely toward the listener; not every humble verb needs a person as the action's destination.

sentences.japanese: 明日は九時に参ります。
sentences.english: I will come/go at nine tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: 参る is a humble/polite counterpart of 行く/来る; choose come versus go from the situation.

sentences.japanese: 受付は一階にございます。
sentences.english: The reception desk is on the first floor.
sentences.nuanceNote: ございます is a polite form of ある. It does not honor the desk as an actor.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 52 (PDF p. 75). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 助詞の整理：も・しか・くらい・まで
meaning: Identify what a particle adds to the sentence.
connection: Nも; Nしか + negative; quantityくらい; Nまで
nuance: も can mean also or as many as; くらい can give an approximate amount or a minimal example; まで can mean even. Read the predicate before deciding the sense.
keyTakeaway: Nも; Nしか + negative; quantityくらい; Nまで

sentences.japanese: 子供までそのニュースを知っています。
sentences.english: Even children know that news.

sentences.japanese: 子供も大人も参加できます。
sentences.english: Both children and adults can participate.
sentences.nuanceNote: も adds each group; it is not the only-use sense of しか.

sentences.japanese: 今日は千円しか持っていません。
sentences.english: I have only one thousand yen today.
sentences.nuanceNote: しか excludes amounts beyond this and pairs with a negative predicate.

sentences.japanese: 駅まで十分くらいかかります。
sentences.english: It takes about ten minutes to the station.
sentences.nuanceNote: くらい gives an approximate quantity here, not an extreme degree comparison.

sentences.japanese: 先生までその冗談を聞いて笑いました。
sentences.english: Even the teacher laughed at that joke.
sentences.nuanceNote: まで adds an unexpected case. It does not mark an endpoint in time here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 58 (PDF p. 81). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: について・に対して・にとって・として
meaning: Topic, target, perspective and role.
connection: Nについて / に対して / にとって / として
nuance: について identifies a topic; に対して a target or contrast; にとって an evaluating perspective; として a role. The following predicate helps decide which fits.
keyTakeaway: Nについて / に対して / にとって / として

sentences.japanese: 教師として、学生に対して公平でありたいです。
sentences.english: As a teacher, I want to be fair toward students.

sentences.japanese: 日本の教育について調べています。
sentences.english: I am researching education in Japan.
sentences.nuanceNote: について introduces the topic being investigated.

sentences.japanese: 店員は客に対して丁寧に説明しました。
sentences.english: The shop assistant explained politely to the customer.
sentences.nuanceNote: に対して marks the target of the explanation/attitude.

sentences.japanese: 私にとって、この写真は大切です。
sentences.english: This photograph is important to me.
sentences.nuanceNote: にとって identifies whose standpoint supports the evaluation.

sentences.japanese: 通訳として会議に参加しました。
sentences.english: I attended the meeting as an interpreter.
sentences.nuanceNote: として states a capacity or role, not an evaluation.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 62 (PDF p. 85). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: Core Compound Particles Matrix (p. 62)
table.subtitle: について vs に対して vs にとって vs として vs において

rows.label: 〜について (Topic / Theme)
cells: 名詞 + について (修飾: 〜についてのN)
Regarding / about: introduces the central topic of thought, speech, or inquiry.
日本の文化について研究する / 将来の進路について話し合う
Followed by verbs of inquiry/expression: 調べる, 書く, 話す, 考える. Cannot replace に対して when pointing to an opposing party.
rows.note: Formal equivalent is 〜に関（かん）して.

rows.label: 〜に対して (Target / Contrast)
cells: 名詞 + に対して (修飾: 〜に対するN)
1. Toward / facing an external target. 2. In sharp contrast between two different subjects.
お客様に対して丁寧な言葉遣いをする / 兄が活発なのに対して、弟は物静かだ
Distinguish from 反面: 反面 contrasts two aspects of the SAME subject; に対して contrasts TWO DISTINCT subjects.
rows.note: When expressing an attitude toward people, に対して is mandatory.

rows.label: 〜にとって (Evaluative Standpoint)
cells: 名詞 + にとって (修飾: 〜にとってのN)
From the standpoint / in the eyes of: establishes the subjective evaluator.
私にとって家族が一番大切だ / 留学生にとって漢字の習得は高い壁だ
Predicate MUST express subjective evaluation (大切だ, 難しい, 深刻だ). NEVER expresses personal physical action (❌ 私にとって本を買う).
rows.note: Evaluates value or difficulty from that party's stance.

rows.label: 〜として (Role / Capacity)
cells: 名詞 + として (修飾: 〜としてのN)
In the role, capacity, official status, or recognized qualification of.
留学生として日本に来ました / 彼は会社の代表として会議に出席した
Noun before として must represent an official title, category, function, or status.
rows.note: Indicates functioning within that recognized status.

rows.label: 〜において (Formal Domain / Setting)
cells: 名詞 + において (修飾: 〜におけるN)
In / at / within: specifies the formal setting, field, era, or domain.
現代社会において情報技術は不可欠だ / 開会式は第一ホールにおいて行われる
Formal written equivalent of で; heavily used in news, academic writing, and official announcements.
rows.note: Formal locus marker for occasions and fields.

title: 〜ところだった (Was on the Very Verge Of / Narrowly Escaped)
meaning: Indicates that an undesirable disaster or drastic event almost occurred, but was averted in the nick of time: 'I almost / was on the verge of...'.
connection: V-辞書形 + ところだった (often paired with もう少しで, 危うく)
nuance: NARROW ESCAPE: Almost always paired with adverbs like もう少しで (by a hair's breadth) or 危うく (narrowly): 'もう少しで終電に乗り遅れるところだった' (I almost missed the last train).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: もう少しで + V-る + ところだった = 'Narrow escape! Almost happened but thank goodness it didn't!'.

sentences.japanese: 足元が滑って、危うく階段から転がり落ちるところだった。
sentences.english: My footing slipped, and I came within a hair's breadth of tumbling down the stairs.
sentences.literal: Footing slipped, narrowly stairs-from tumble-down verge-was.

tokens.word: 転がり落ちるところだった
tokens.meaning: was on the verge of tumbling down
tokens.reading: ころがりおちるところだった

sentences.nuanceNote: Heart-stopping near-miss on a steep staircase.

sentences.japanese: もう少しで終電に乗り遅れるところだった。
sentences.english: I came within a hair's breadth of missing the last train.
sentences.nuanceNote: もう少しで + V-る + ところだった describes an undesirable event narrowly averted at the last second.

sentences.japanese: 危うく赤信号を見落とすところだったが、手前で急ブレーキを踏んだ。
sentences.english: I almost overlooked the red light, but slammed on the brakes just before the intersection.
sentences.nuanceNote: 危うく + V-る + ところだった expresses relief at averting a collision.

quiz.question: 友達が声をかけてくれなかったら、大事な約束を（　　）ところだった。
quiz.translation: If my friend hadn't called out to remind me, I would have completely forgotten my important appointment.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + ところだった (Averted outcome)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + ところだった (often paired with もう少しで, 危うく)

explanations.reason: Correct! 辞書形 忘れる + ところだった expresses an action that was narrowly averted.
忘れたところだった would mean had just forgotten; it does not express the averted event required by this context.
Incorrect. 忘れてところだった is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 忘れないところだった conveys the opposite meaning.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 66 (PDF p. 89). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: こと・の・もの
meaning: Nominalize events and distinguish things from facts.
connection: Plain clause + こと/の; concrete thing + もの
nuance: Perception constructions often use の: 走るのを見た. Fixed patterns such as ことができる require こと. Do not assume the nominalizers are interchangeable everywhere.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + こと/の; concrete thing + もの

sentences.japanese: 毎日歩くことは大切です。子供が走るのを見ました。
sentences.english: Walking every day is important. I saw a child running.

sentences.japanese: 毎日運動することは大切です。
sentences.english: Exercising every day is important.
sentences.nuanceNote: こと nominalizes the activity as an abstract topic.

sentences.japanese: 子供が公園で走っているのを見ました。
sentences.english: I saw a child running in the park.
sentences.nuanceNote: の is natural for an event directly perceived with 見る; do not substitute こと mechanically.

sentences.japanese: 何か冷たいものが飲みたいです。
sentences.english: I would like something cold to drink.
sentences.nuanceNote: もの refers to a thing; it is not interchangeable with nominalizing の/こと here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 66 (PDF p. 89). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: Nominalizers Triad Matrix: こと vs の vs もの (p. 66)
table.subtitle: Distinguishing abstract truth, sensory perception, and tangible/natural reality.

rows.label: こと (Abstract Truth / Definition)
cells: 動詞普通形 + こと / 名詞 + であること
Conceptualization, abstract facts, rules, and definition statements.
私の趣味は音楽を聴くことです / パソコンを使うことができる
Mandatory in fixed patterns: 〜ことができる, 〜ことにする / なる, 〜ことがある. Mandatory in definitional sentences (X は Y ことです).
rows.note: Use こと when treating an action as an abstract concept.

rows.label: の (Direct Sensory Perception)
cells: 動詞普通形 + の
Immediate concrete action happening right in front of the speaker's senses.
子供たちが走っているのを見た / 隣の部屋で誰かが歌っているのが聞こえる
Mandatory with sensory verbs (見る, 聞こえる, 感じる) and physical intervention verbs (手伝う, 待つ, 止める). Mandatory in cleft sentences (〜のは〜だ).
rows.note: Sensory perception of unfolding events always takes の.

rows.label: もの (Tangible Reality / Natural Essence)
cells: 普通形 + もの (な-adj な / 名詞な)
Concrete physical objects, universal human nature, or innate natural truth.
冷たいものが飲みたい / 人間は誰でも失敗するものだ
〜ものだ expresses universal general truth ('It is human nature to...'). 〜ものではない expresses strong moral warning ('You should never...').
rows.note: もの refers to real substances or general inherent truths.

title: 〜ように (So That / In Order That - Non-Volitional Objective)
meaning: Expresses an objective or intended state toward which action is directed: 'So that X may become possible / so that X doesn't happen'.
connection: V-辞書形 (Potential / Intransitive non-volitional) / V-ない + ように
nuance: VOLITIONAL CONTRAST: ように takes non-volitional verbs (見える、聞こえる、忘れない, potential verbs). In contrast, ために takes conscious volitional actions by the same subject.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ない / V-可能形 + ように = 'So that...'. Example: 忘れないようにメモする (Jot down so as not to forget).

sentences.japanese: 後ろの席の人にもよく聞こえるように、マイクの音量を上げてください。
sentences.english: Please turn up the microphone volume so that people in the back seats can hear well too.
sentences.literal: Back-of seats people-to-also well can-hear so-that, mic-of volume please-raise.

tokens.meaning: so that it can be heard

sentences.nuanceNote: Intransitive potential verb 聞こえる expresses intended auditory perception.

sentences.japanese: 日本語の新聞が読めるように、漢字を勉強しています。
sentences.english: I am studying kanji so that I can read Japanese newspapers.
sentences.nuanceNote: The goal is an ability expressed with the potential form.

sentences.japanese: 電車に遅れないように、早く家を出ました。
sentences.english: I left home early so that I would not miss the train.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vないように is natural for avoiding an unwanted result; it does not require a potential verb.

quiz.question: 忘れ（　　）ように、メモしておきます。
quiz.translation: I will make a note so that I do not forget.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ない + ように (Preventative purpose)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 (Potential / Intransitive non-volitional) / V-ない + ように

explanations.reason: Vないように gives the negative outcome to avoid.
なく cannot directly modify よう in this pattern.
ないの adds an unnecessary の.
なくて is not the required modifier.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 70 (PDF p. 93). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: ようだ・ように：比喩・目的・指示
meaning: Distinguish resemblance, a goal and an indirect instruction.
connection: Nのようだ; V dictionary/ない + ように; Vようにと言う
nuance: ように can describe resemblance, a desired outcome, or the content of an instruction. With a goal, non-volitional/potential or negative forms are common; ために often expresses a controlled purpose.
keyTakeaway: Nのようだ; V dictionary/ない + ように; Vようにと言う

sentences.japanese: 忘れないように、メモするように言われました。
sentences.english: I was told to take notes so that I would not forget.

sentences.japanese: この雲は魚のように見えます。
sentences.english: This cloud looks like a fish.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのように compares appearance; it does not express purpose.

sentences.japanese: 後ろの人にも聞こえるように、大きな声で話しました。
sentences.english: I spoke loudly so that people at the back could hear too.
sentences.nuanceNote: A non-volitional/potential outcome precedes purpose ように.

sentences.japanese: 先生は、来週までに読むように言いました。
sentences.english: The teacher told us to read it by next week.
sentences.nuanceNote: ように introduces the content of an instruction. It is not resemblance or a purpose clause here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 70 (PDF p. 93). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜わけにはいかない (Cannot Afford To / Morally or Socially Bound Not To)
meaning: Indicates that even if the speaker wants to do X, social morals, duties, or practical constraints make it utterly impermissible: 'Cannot afford to do / In all conscience I cannot'.
connection: V-辞書形 + わけにはいかない (cannot do) | V-ない形 + わけにはいかない (must do / cannot afford not to)
nuance: INTERNAL CONSCIENCE & SOCIAL CODE: Unlike physical inability (できない), わけにはいかない denotes moral, professional, or situational inhibition: '明日試験だから、ゲームをするわけにはいかない' (Since there's an exam tomorrow, I cannot afford to play games).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-る + わけにはいかない = 'Cannot do (conscience/duty forbids)'. V-ない + わけにはいかない = 'MUST do!'.

sentences.japanese: 大事な会議の当日に、ちょっと熱があるくらいで仕事を休むわけにはいかない。
sentences.english: On the day of such a crucial meeting, I simply cannot afford to take off work just for a slight fever.
sentences.literal: Crucial meeting day-on, slight fever exists just-by work take-off cannot-afford.

tokens.word: 休むわけにはいかない
tokens.reading: やすむわけにはいかない

sentences.nuanceNote: Sense of professional duty overriding personal discomfort.

sentences.japanese: 明日は大切な試験なので、今夜は遊ぶわけにはいきません。
sentences.english: I have an important exam tomorrow, so I cannot go out for fun tonight.
sentences.nuanceNote: The obstacle is what is appropriate or responsible, not physical inability.

sentences.japanese: 約束したので、行かないわけにはいきません。
sentences.english: Since I promised, I have to go.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative verb reverses the practical conclusion: not going is unacceptable.

quiz.question: 友人に秘密にしてくれと頼まれたから、誰にも話す（　　）にはいかない。
quiz.translation: Because my friend pleaded with me to keep it a secret, I cannot in all conscience tell anyone.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + わけにはいかない (Moral constraint)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + わけにはいかない (cannot do) | V-ない形 + わけにはいかない (must do / cannot afford not to)

explanations.reason: Correct! 話すわけにはいかない conveys moral obligation not to betray trust.
Incorrect. 話すはずにはいかない is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 話すことにはいかない is invalid.
Incorrect. 話すものにはいかない does not form this structure.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 74 (PDF p. 97). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: わけだ・ないわけにはいかない
meaning: A logical conclusion; being unable not to act.
connection: Plain clause + わけだ; Vない + わけにはいかない
nuance: わけだ connects facts into an explanation. The double negative ないわけにはいかない expresses an obligation, not a prohibition.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + わけだ; Vない + わけにはいかない

sentences.japanese: 約束したので、行かないわけにはいきません。
sentences.english: Since I promised, I have to go.

sentences.japanese: 毎日三時間練習しているのですか。上手なわけですね。
sentences.english: You practice three hours every day? That explains why you are good.
sentences.nuanceNote: わけだ connects new information with an understandable conclusion.

sentences.japanese: 代表に選ばれたので、出席しないわけにはいきません。
sentences.english: Since I was chosen as representative, I have to attend.
sentences.nuanceNote: ないわけにはいかない expresses an obligation. It does not mean impossible to attend.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 74 (PDF p. 97). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: The 4 わけ Quadruplets Decoded (p. 74)
table.subtitle: Logical inevitability vs total impossibility vs partial denial vs moral barrier.

rows.label: 〜わけだ (Logical Conclusion)
cells: Naturally so / No wonder: a conclusion that follows as the obvious logical result.
普通形 (な-adj な, N である) + わけだ
今日は気温が38度もある。暑いわけだ。
Connects observed facts into an understandable explanation ('That explains why!').
rows.note: Confirms why a situation is naturally understandable.

rows.label: 〜わけがない (Absolute Impossibility)
cells: There is no way on earth that...: absolute objective impossibility based on evidence.
普通形 + わけがない (= はずがない)
彼がそんな酷い嘘をつくわけがない。
Emphatic certainty that something cannot possibly be true.
rows.note: Strong denial of possibility based on reason.

rows.label: 〜わけではない (Partial Negation)
cells: It does not necessarily mean that... / I don't mean to say that...
普通形 + わけではない
日本料理が嫌いなわけではないが、納豆は苦手だ。
Softens a statement by denying total black-and-white interpretation.
rows.note: Partial negation; does not reject the entire premise.

rows.label: 〜わけにはいかない (Moral / Social Barrier)
cells: Cannot bring oneself to do / Cannot afford to do because of duty, conscience, or society.
動詞辞書形 + わけにはいかない (二重否定: 動詞ない形 + わけにはいかない = Must do)
大事な会議があるから、熱があっても休むわけにはいかない。
Physical ability exists, but social/moral constraints prevent the action.
rows.note: Conscience or social duty forbids the action.

title: ばかり：偏り・追加・直後
meaning: Only, repeatedly, not only, or just finished.
connection: Nばかり; Vてばかりいる; ばかりでなく; V dictionaryばかりだ; Vたばかりだ
nuance: Identify the form before ばかり. たばかり is subjectively recent; たところ emphasizes the immediate phase after completion. Repeated-action てばかりいる often conveys criticism.
keyTakeaway: Nばかり; Vてばかりいる; ばかりでなく; V dictionaryばかりだ; Vたばかりだ

sentences.japanese: 弟はゲームをしてばかりいます。私は帰ったばかりです。
sentences.english: My younger brother does nothing but play games. I have only just returned.

sentences.japanese: 弟は甘い物ばかり食べています。
sentences.english: My younger brother eats almost nothing but sweet things.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nばかり describes a strong bias toward one category.

sentences.japanese: 休みの日は寝てばかりいます。
sentences.english: On days off I do nothing but sleep.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vてばかりいる focuses on repeated/excessive behavior, often with criticism.

sentences.japanese: この店は安いばかりでなく、量も多いです。
sentences.english: This restaurant is not only cheap; the portions are large too.
sentences.nuanceNote: ばかりでなく adds a second favorable feature here.

sentences.japanese: 先月始めたばかりなので、まだ慣れていません。
sentences.english: I only started last month, so I am not used to it yet.
sentences.nuanceNote: たばかり can count last month as recent relative to the activity; it does not always mean a few seconds ago.

sentences.japanese: 準備は終わりました。あとは出発するばかりです。
sentences.english: The preparations are finished. All that remains is to leave.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary verb + ばかり describes a remaining action here; it is not the worsening-trend use.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 80 (PDF p. 103). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: The 〜ばかり Functional Spectrum (p. 80)
table.subtitle: From exclusive concentration to critical indulgence to recency to unidirectional change.

rows.label: N + ばかり (Exclusive Concentration)
cells: Nothing but N / Only N: focused entirely on one item to the exclusion of others.
肉ばかり食べないで、野菜も食べなさい。
Critical observation of one-sidedness.
Contrast with だけ: だけ is neutral limitation; ばかり implies excessive saturation.
rows.note: Often carries a tone of mild criticism regarding imbalance.

rows.label: V-て + ばかりいる (Habitual Indulgence)
cells: Does nothing but V all the time: habitual repetition of unproductive activity.
弟は勉強もしないで、ゲームをしてばかりいる。
Annoyance or disapproval from the speaker.
Always expresses critical reproach regarding repeated behavior.
rows.note: Indicates continuous repetition with speaker criticism.

rows.label: V-た + ばかりだ (Subjective Recency)
cells: Just finished doing: feels subjectively immediate to the speaker.
先月日本に来たばかりなので、まだ地理がよく分かりません。
Subjective feeling of recency, even if weeks have passed.
Contrast with 〜たところだ: たところだ is literal immediate temporal phase (minutes ago).
rows.note: Speaker treats the completed action as very fresh.

rows.label: V-辞書形 + ばかりだ (Unidirectional Trend)
cells: Continues steadily to worsen/progress, or everything is prepared and ready to V.
不況のせいで、会社の業績は悪化するばかりだ。
Passive acknowledgment of unfolding momentum.
Only pairs with verbs of continuous change (上がる, 下がる, 悪化する).
rows.note: Describes an ongoing change moving steadily in one direction.

rows.label: 〜ばかりか / ばかりでなく (Escalating Addition)
cells: Not only A, but on top of that B as well: escalating surprise or severity.
彼は漢字ばかりか、ひらがなさえ読めない。
Strong emphatic addition.
Clause B introduces something even more surprising or severe.
rows.note: Formal equivalent of 〜だけでなく.

title: 〜ことになっている (Customary Rule, Schedule, or Standing Regulation)
meaning: Indicates a pre-established rule, institutional regulation, law, or standing appointment that governs behavior: 'It is a rule that / It is scheduled that'.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ことになっている
nuance: Reports an established rule, plan or arrangement. It can concern a private appointment as well as institutional rules. Compare ことにしている, which emphasizes the actor's chosen policy. ことになっている does not always mean that the speaker had no part in making the arrangement.
keyTakeaway: Reports an established rule, plan or arrangement. It can concern a private appointment as well as institutional rules. Compare ことにしている, which emphasizes the actor's chosen policy. ことになっている does not always mean that the speaker had no part in making the arrangement.

sentences.japanese: 法律により、二十歳未満の飲酒と喫煙は禁止されることになっています。
sentences.english: By law, drinking and smoking under twenty years of age is strictly prohibited.
sentences.literal: Law-by, 20-under drinking smoking prohibited become-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standing statutory legal requirement.

sentences.japanese: この学校では、上履きを履くことになっています。
sentences.english: At this school, students are required to wear indoor shoes.
sentences.nuanceNote: ことになっている reports an established rule or arrangement rather than the speaker's personal policy.

sentences.japanese: 会議は十時に始まることになっています。
sentences.english: The meeting is scheduled to begin at ten.
sentences.nuanceNote: The arrangement can be a schedule, not only a prohibition or institutional rule.

quiz.question: この寮では、夜十一時以降は静かに（　　）ことになっている。
quiz.translation: In this dormitory, it is a standing rule to remain quiet after 11:00 PM.
quiz.grammarFocus: Standing rule formula 〜ことになっている
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ことになっている

explanations.reason: Correct! V-辞書形 静かにする connects to ことになっている.
Incorrect. して is te-form.
Incorrect. した is past form.
Incorrect. し is bare stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 84 (PDF p. 107). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: する・なる：変化・習慣・決定
meaning: Distinguish making a change from a change happening.
connection: Adjく/に + する/なる; Vことにする/なる; Vようにする/なる
nuance: する emphasizes a deliberate choice or effort. なる describes a resulting change or arrangement. ようになっている can describe how a system is designed.
keyTakeaway: Adjく/に + する/なる; Vことにする/なる; Vようにする/なる

sentences.japanese: 毎日練習して、日本語で話せるようになりました。
sentences.english: By practicing every day, I became able to speak in Japanese.

sentences.japanese: 部屋を明るくしました。窓を開けると、もっと明るくなりました。
sentences.english: I made the room brighter. When I opened the window, it became brighter still.
sentences.useLabel: Deliberate change versus change in state
sentences.nuanceNote: する focuses on making the change; なる presents the resulting change.

sentences.japanese: 私は参加することにしました。会議は金曜に行うことになりました。
sentences.english: I decided to participate. It has been arranged that the meeting will be held on Friday.
sentences.nuanceNote: ことにする emphasizes a decision; ことになる presents the settled outcome without necessarily identifying the decision-maker.

sentences.japanese: 練習して、泳げるようになりました。
sentences.english: After practicing, I became able to swim.
sentences.nuanceNote: ようになる describes a change in ability/habit, not simply deciding to do it.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 84 (PDF p. 107). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: The Decision & Custom Grid: する vs なる (p. 84)
table.subtitle: Personal volition vs external outcome vs maintained habit vs institutional regulation.

rows.label: 〜ことにする (Personal Decision)
cells: Personal volition / deliberate conscious choice made by the speaker.
One-off new resolution.
健康のために、今日からお酒をやめることにした。
Announcing a personal decision.
rows.note: Reflects the speaker's own will.

rows.label: 〜ことになる (External Outcome)
cells: External circumstances, collective decision, or objective outcome without individual focus.
Settled outcome / development.
来月、大阪の本社へ転勤することになりました。
Polite reporting of business/life developments where personal agency is restrained.
rows.note: Presents an arrangement as a settled situation.

rows.label: 〜ことにしている (Maintained Habit)
cells: Personal self-discipline / self-imposed standing policy.
Ongoing maintained routine.
どんなに忙しくても、毎日30分は本を読むことにしている。
Describing personal health, lifestyle, or study discipline.
rows.note: Speaker's own persistent rule.

rows.label: 〜ことになっている (Standing Regulation)
cells: Standing law, institutional regulation, societal rule, or fixed schedule.
Established system / rule.
法律により、二十歳未満の飲酒は禁止されていることになっている。
Explaining societal laws, school rules, and official schedules.
rows.note: Societal or institutional standing rule.

title: 条件形の特別な用法
meaning: Discovery, narrative sequence and adding characteristics.
connection: Vと…た; Vたら…た; Nも…ばNも…
nuance: Past と/たら may describe an actual discovery rather than a hypothetical condition. も…ば…も adds two features; it need not express an if-then relation.
keyTakeaway: Vと…た; Vたら…た; Nも…ばNも…

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けると、猫がいました。この店は安くもあれば、おいしくもあります。
sentences.english: When I opened the window, there was a cat. This restaurant is both inexpensive and tasty.

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けると、庭に猫がいました。
sentences.english: When I opened the window, there was a cat in the garden.
sentences.nuanceNote: Narrative と can describe an actual past discovery, not only a natural law.

sentences.japanese: 駅に着いたら、電車はもう出ていました。
sentences.english: When I reached the station, the train had already left.
sentences.nuanceNote: たら locates an actual discovery after arriving; the train's departure happened earlier.

sentences.japanese: この店は料理もおいしければ、サービスもいいです。
sentences.english: This restaurant has both good food and good service.
sentences.nuanceNote: も…ば…も lists coexisting features rather than setting an if-then condition.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 88 (PDF p. 111). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 副詞と文末の呼応
meaning: Match adverbs to the meaning of the ending.
connection: 決して + negative; まるで + ようだ; たとえ + ても; 必ずしも + negative
nuance: Look beyond the blank. 必ずしも否定 means not necessarily, whereas 決して否定 is emphatic rejection. まさか often signals disbelief.
keyTakeaway: 決して + negative; まるで + ようだ; たとえ + ても; 必ずしも + negative

sentences.japanese: 高い物が必ずしも丈夫だとは限りません。
sentences.english: Expensive things are not necessarily durable.

sentences.japanese: 有名な店が必ずしもおいしいとは限りません。
sentences.english: A famous restaurant is not necessarily good.
sentences.nuanceNote: 必ずしも combines with a negative scope, not a universal positive assertion.

sentences.japanese: このことは決して忘れません。
sentences.english: I will never forget this.
sentences.nuanceNote: 決して strengthens the negative predicate.

sentences.japanese: まるで夢を見ているようです。
sentences.english: It feels as though I am dreaming.
sentences.nuanceNote: まるで pairs naturally with an expression of resemblance such as ようだ.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 92 (PDF p. 115). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: Adverb & Sentence-Ending Collocations (呼応表現) (p. 92)
table.subtitle: The golden pair triggers that determine the grammatical ending before reading the sentence.

rows.label: 決して (けっして)
cells: 〜ない / 否定形
Resolute total refusal: 'Never, under any circumstance'.
約束は決して破りません。
Trap: Pairs strictly with negative predicates.
rows.note: Strong determination never to do.

rows.label: まったく
cells: 〜ない / 否定形
Complete absence: 'Not in the slightest / Not at all'.
彼の説明は難しくて、まったく分からなかった。
Can also mean 'truly/completely' in affirmative with surprise (まったく驚いた).
rows.note: Emphasizes complete lack or total state.

rows.label: 必ずしも (かならずしも)
cells: 〜わけではない / 〜とは限らない
Partial exception: 'Not necessarily true in every case'.
有名大学を卒業した人が、必ずしも優秀だとは限らない。
Trap: Almost always resolves in 〜とは限らない or 〜わけではない.
rows.note: Denies absolute universality.

rows.label: まるで
cells: 〜ようだ / 〜みたいだ
Vivid figurative simile: 'Just as if / Exactly like'.
あの雲はまるで白い城のようだ。
Trap: Signals a metaphorical comparison.
rows.note: Introduces a vivid simile.

rows.label: たとえ
cells: 〜ても / 〜でも
Extreme hypothetical concession: 'Even if / No matter if'.
たとえ親に反対されても、自分の夢を諦めない。
Trap: Pairs with 〜ても to concede an extreme situation.
rows.note: Concessive hypothesis marker.

rows.label: どうしても
cells: 〜たい / 〜てしまう / 否定形
Inescapable yearning or unavoidable impossibility: 'By all means / Simply cannot'.
どうしても日本で働きたい。 / どうしても鍵が見つからない。
Expresses powerful internal urge or insurmountable barrier.
rows.note: Pairs with strong volition or impossibility.

rows.label: まさか
cells: 〜ないだろう / 〜とは思わなかった
Utter disbelief: 'It couldn't possibly be... / Never in my wildest dreams'.
まさか彼が試験に落ちるとは思わなかった。
Trap: Expresses shock that an unthinkable event occurred.
rows.note: Signals incredulity or surprise.

title: 〜っぽい (Prone to Negative Behavior / Resembling Quality: -ish / -y)
meaning: Having a perceived quality, resemblance or tendency; often informal and sometimes negative.
connection: Selected nouns / verb stems + っぽい
nuance: っぽい describes a resemblance, quality or tendency and behaves as an い-adjective. It occurs with particular nouns and verb stems, not freely with every adjective.
keyTakeaway: っぽい describes a resemblance, quality or tendency and behaves as an い-adjective. It occurs with particular nouns and verb stems, not freely with every adjective.

sentences.japanese: 彼は些細なことで怒りっぽい性格なので、みんな話しかけにくそうにしている。
sentences.english: Because he has a quick-tempered personality who gets angry over trivial matters, everyone seems hesitant to talk to him.
sentences.literal: He trivial-things-over angry-prone personality since, everyone speak-hard looking-is.

tokens.reading: おこりっぽいせいかく

sentences.nuanceNote: 怒る (stem 怒り) + っぽい describes chronic short temper.

sentences.japanese: この服は少し子供っぽいです。
sentences.english: These clothes look a little childish.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nっぽい means having a perceived quality. The evaluation often depends on context.

sentences.japanese: 最近、忘れっぽくなりました。
sentences.english: Recently I have become forgetful.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + っぽい forms an adjective for a tendency; its attachment is lexical, not freely available with every verb.

quiz.question: いい歳をした大人が、そんな（　　）っぽい嘘をつくのは恥ずかしいですよ。
quiz.translation: It is shameful for a grown adult to tell such a childish lie.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + っぽい (Superficial resemblance / immaturity)
quiz.ruleHint: Selected nouns / verb stems + っぽい

explanations.reason: Correct! 子供っぽい means 'childish / immature'.
Incorrect. 大人っぽい means mature-looking.
Incorrect. 先生っぽい means teacher-like.
Incorrect. 若者っぽい means youth-like.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 96 (PDF p. 119). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜だらけ (Covered in Mess, Flaws, or Filth: Riddled With / Full Of)
meaning: Covered entirely with an undesirable substance or riddled with flaws: 'covered in mud, full of errors, riddled with debts'.
connection: Noun + だらけ (泥だらけ, 間違いだらけ, ゴミだらけ, 借金だらけ)
nuance: だらけ means full of or covered with many examples of something, commonly unwelcome things such as mistakes or mud. Its negative association is a tendency, not a logical ban on every positive noun.
keyTakeaway: だらけ means full of or covered with many examples of something, commonly unwelcome things such as mistakes or mud. Its negative association is a tendency, not a logical ban on every positive noun.

sentences.japanese: 急いで書いた彼のレポートは、誤字や文法の間違いだらけだった。
sentences.english: His report, which was written in a rush, was riddled with typos and grammatical errors.
sentences.literal: Hurriedly wrote his report, typos grammar mistakes-riddled was.

tokens.reading: まちがいだらけだった

sentences.nuanceNote: Negative appraisal of messy draft.

sentences.japanese: 転んで、服が泥だらけになりました。
sentences.english: I fell and my clothes became covered in mud.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nだらけ commonly describes an undesirable substance or condition spread throughout.

sentences.japanese: この文章は間違いだらけです。
sentences.english: This passage is full of mistakes.
sentences.useLabel: Many defects in an abstract thing
sentences.nuanceNote: だらけ also applies to flaws, not just physical dirt.

quiz.question: 作文が間違い（　　）です。
quiz.translation: The composition is full of mistakes.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + だらけ (Covered in mess)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + だらけ (泥だらけ, 間違いだらけ, ゴミだらけ, 借金だらけ)

explanations.reason: Noun + だらけ means full of.
だらく is not this suffix.
だらかな is not this suffix.
だらくて is not this suffix.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 96 (PDF p. 119). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜らしい (Evidential Hearsay vs Typical Archetype)
meaning: Two primary senses: (1) Hearsay/conjecture based on external reports ('apparently'); (2) Exemplifying the quintessence of a quality ('truly typical of / behaving like a real...').
connection: Sense 1 (Conjecture): 普通形 (Noun / な-adj bare) + らしい | Sense 2 (Typicality): Noun + らしい
nuance: らしい has an inference/report sense and a typical-quality sense. In 春らしい, it means characteristic of spring. っぽい describes a perceived resemblance or tendency, often informally; it is not inherently shallow or fake. Determine the sense of らしい from what precedes it and the context.
keyTakeaway: Identify the sense: apparent/report-based inference, or a quality typical of a noun.

sentences.japanese: 桜が咲いてポカポカ暖かくなり、ようやく春らしい季節になった。
sentences.english: With cherry blossoms blooming and pleasantly warm weather, it has finally become a truly spring-like season.
sentences.literal: Cherry-blossoms bloomed pleasantly warm became, at-last spring-like season became.
sentences.nuanceNote: Embodying the ideal aesthetic qualities of springtime.

sentences.japanese: 彼は来月引っ越すらしいです。
sentences.english: Apparently he is moving next month.
sentences.nuanceNote: Plain clause + らしい expresses an inference or information received indirectly.

sentences.japanese: 今日は春らしい暖かい日です。
sentences.english: Today is a warm, springlike day.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nらしい means characteristic of that noun; it is not hearsay about spring.

quiz.question: 負けて悔しいのは分かるが、プロの選手（　　）最後まで堂々と振る舞うべきだ。
quiz.translation: I understand you are frustrated by the loss, but as a professional athlete you ought to carry yourself with dignity until the end.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + らしく (Archetypical conduct)
quiz.ruleHint: Sense 1 (Conjecture): 普通形 (Noun / な-adj bare) + らしい | Sense 2 (Typicality): Noun + らしい

explanations.reason: Correct! 選手らしく means 'in a manner befitting a true athlete'.
Incorrect. 選手そうに is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 選手みたいで implies superficial resemblance rather than true professional conduct.
Incorrect. 選手がちに is meaningless.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 96 (PDF p. 119). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜気味 (Slight Negative Tinge / Feeling Somewhat...)
meaning: Indicates a subtle, mild onset of an undesirable physical, mental, or situational condition: 'a touch of / feeling slightly...'.
connection: V-stem + 気味 (ぎみ) | Noun + 気味 (風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 太り気味, 遅れ気味)
nuance: 気味 describes a slight tendency or degree of a condition, often unwelcome: 風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 緊張気味. It need not mean the beginning of an illness; it can describe an ongoing mild condition. Attachment is conventional rather than freely possible with every noun or stem.
keyTakeaway: 気味 describes a slight tendency or degree of a condition, often unwelcome: 風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 緊張気味. It need not mean the beginning of an illness; it can describe an ongoing mild condition. Attachment is conventional rather than freely possible with every noun or stem.

sentences.japanese: 最近残業続きで疲れ気味なので、今週末は家でゆっくり休みたい。
sentences.english: Because I've been feeling somewhat worn out from consecutive overtime lately, I want to rest peacefully at home this weekend.
sentences.literal: Recently overtime-continuation-due-to fatigue-touch-being, this-weekend home peacefully want-to-rest.
sentences.nuanceNote: Mild exhaustion prompting weekend recuperation.

sentences.japanese: 朝から喉が痛くて、少し風邪気味です。
sentences.english: My throat has been hurting since morning, and I have a slight touch of a cold.
