sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + 気味 describes nascent physical symptoms before a full-blown illness.

sentences.japanese: 悪天候のため、電車の運行が全体的に遅れ気味になっている。
sentences.english: Due to adverse weather, train operations are slightly lagging behind schedule overall.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb stem + 気味 indicates a slight unfavorable operational deviation.

quiz.question: 朝から喉が痛くて少し（　　）気味なので、早めに薬を飲んで寝ます。
quiz.translation: My throat has been hurting since morning and I have a touch of a cold, so I will take medicine early and go to sleep.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + 気味 (Nascent symptom)
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem + 気味 (ぎみ) | Noun + 気味 (風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 太り気味, 遅れ気味)

explanations.reason: Correct! 風邪気味 (かぜぎみ) is the classic idiom for having a mild touch of a cold.
Incorrect. 病気気味 is not standard Japanese.
Incorrect. 熱気味 is unnatural (one says 微熱がある).
Incorrect. 痛い気味 is ungrammatical (adjectives do not attach directly to 気味).

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 96 (PDF p. 119). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜がち (Prone To / Habitual Unfortunate Tendency)
meaning: Indicates a recurring, unwanted tendency to happen frequently or slip into an undesirable state: 'tending to / prone to / easily falling into...'.
connection: V-stem + がち | Noun + がち (留守がち, 曇りがち, 遠慮がち, 忘れがち)
nuance: がち describes a recurring tendency, often unwelcome. It attaches to selected nouns and verb stems and forms combinations such as 病気がちだ and 忘れがちなこと. 気味 describes a slight degree/state and is not restricted to physical symptoms. The two can overlap in some contexts; do not treat every similar-looking alternative as ungrammatical.
keyTakeaway: がち describes a recurring tendency, often unwelcome. It attaches to selected nouns and verb stems and forms combinations such as 病気がちだ and 忘れがちなこと. 気味 describes a slight degree/state and is not restricted to physical symptoms. The two can overlap in some contexts; do not treat every similar-looking alternative as ungrammatical.

sentences.japanese: スマートフォンに夢中になると、ついつい夜更かしをしがちだ。
sentences.english: When absorbed in one's smartphone, one is terribly prone to inadvertently staying up late.
sentences.literal: Smartphone absorbed become, inadvertently staying-up-late prone-to-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: Common behavioral vulnerability in modern life.

sentences.japanese: 忙しいと、朝食を抜きがちです。
sentences.english: When I am busy, I tend to skip breakfast.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + がち describes a recurring tendency, often considered undesirable.

sentences.japanese: 子供のころは病気がちでした。
sentences.english: I was often ill as a child.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nがち occurs with established combinations such as 病気がち; do not attach it to every noun indiscriminately.

quiz.question: 最近、仕事が忙しくて、約束を忘れ（　　）です。
quiz.translation: Recently I have been busy with work and tend to forget appointments.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + がち (Frequent behavioral tendency)
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem + がち | Noun + がち (留守がち, 曇りがち, 遠慮がち, 忘れがち)

explanations.reason: V-stem + がちです describes a tendency.
がちな modifies a following noun.
がちに is adverbial, not the predicate before です.
がちの does not form this predicate.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 96 (PDF p. 119). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 複合動詞・接尾辞
meaning: Expand a verb or noun's meaning with a suffix.
connection: V-stem + 始める/続ける/終わる/出す/切る; N + らしい/っぽい
nuance: Suffixes differ in meaning and attachment. 出す can describe a sudden onset; 始める is a general start. らしい can mean typical of; っぽい often marks a resemblance or tendency.
keyTakeaway: V-stem + 始める/続ける/終わる/出す/切る; N + らしい/っぽい

sentences.japanese: 雨が降り出しましたが、最後まで走り切りました。
sentences.english: It suddenly started raining, but I ran all the way to the end.

sentences.japanese: 雨が降り始めて、一時間ほど降り続きました。
sentences.english: It started raining and continued for about an hour.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + 始める and 続ける distinguish starting from continuing.

sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが急に泣き出しました。
sentences.english: The baby suddenly started crying.
sentences.nuanceNote: 出す often highlights a sudden onset; 始める is a more general start.

sentences.japanese: 長い小説をやっと読み終わりました。
sentences.english: I finally finished reading the long novel.
sentences.nuanceNote: 終わる marks completion of the activity.

sentences.japanese: 一人で全部食べ切りました。
sentences.english: I ate it all by myself.
sentences.nuanceNote: 切る emphasizes completing the action fully or exhausting its object.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 96 (PDF p. 119). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: Suffix Transformation Matrix: っぽい vs だらけ vs 気味 vs がち (p. 96)
table.subtitle: Resemblance vs surface saturation vs physical tinge vs unfortunate habit.

rows.label: 〜っぽい (Resemblance / Cheapened Quality)
cells: 名詞 / 動詞ます語幹 / い形容詞語幹
Resembling a quality, often with a childish, negative, or cheapened tone: '-ish, -like'.
子供っぽい (childish), 怒りっぽい (quick-tempered), 安っぽい (cheap-looking), 白っぽい (whitish)
Cannot be used for dignified praise (use 〜らしい instead).
rows.note: Negative or informal resemblance.

rows.label: 〜だらけ (Surface Saturation)
cells: 名詞 (always negative or messy entities)
Completely covered, riddled with, or full of undesirable things across an entire surface.
間違いだらけ (riddled with errors), 泥だらけ (covered in mud), 借金だらけ (deep in debt)
Exclusive to negative, dirty, or flawed conditions.
rows.note: Physical or metaphorical mess across the whole surface.

rows.label: 〜気味 (ぎみ) (Slight Negative Tinge)
cells: 名詞 / 動詞ます語幹
A slight, emerging physical, mental, or bodily symptom: 'A touch of..., feeling somewhat...'.
風邪気味 (a touch of a cold), 疲れ気味 (somewhat tired), 緊張気味 (a bit nervous)
Describes an incipient, mild physical or psychological feeling.
rows.note: Slight internal feeling or symptom.

rows.label: 〜がち (Unfortunate Tendency)
cells: 名詞 / 動詞ます語幹
Unfortunate recurrent tendency or habit: 'Prone to doing..., frequently happens'.
病気がち (frequently falling ill), 遠慮しがち (tending to hold back), 留守にしがち (often away)
Describes a persistent negative pattern over time.
rows.note: Frequent regrettable occurrence.

title: 〜かける・〜通す・〜づらい
meaning: An unfinished action, persistence and difficulty.
connection: Vます-stem + かける / 通す / づらい
nuance: かける means an action is started or partly done; 通す means continuing through to the end; づらい often conveys personal difficulty or discomfort.
keyTakeaway: Vます-stem + かける / 通す / づらい

sentences.japanese: 読みかけの本を最後まで読み通しました。
sentences.english: I read the partly finished book all the way to the end.

sentences.japanese: 机の上に飲みかけのお茶があります。
sentences.english: There is some partly drunk tea on the desk.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + かけ describes something started but unfinished.

sentences.japanese: 最後まで自分の意見を言い通しました。
sentences.english: I maintained my opinion all the way to the end.
sentences.nuanceNote: 通す emphasizes persisting through the whole course, rather than merely reaching an endpoint.

sentences.japanese: このことは家族にも話しづらいです。
sentences.english: This is difficult to tell even my family.
sentences.nuanceNote: づらい often highlights personal discomfort or difficulty; compare neutral difficulty with にくい.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 96 (PDF p. 119). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文の組み立て：引用
meaning: Keep the quoted clause together.
connection: [Quoted clause] と + 言う/思う/聞く
nuance: Find the quoting predicate, then locate the clause ending immediately before と. A noun predicate may need だ inside the quotation. Do not attach particles solely by English order.
keyTakeaway: [Quoted clause] と + 言う/思う/聞く

sentences.japanese: 友達は明日休むと言っていました。
sentences.english: My friend said they would take tomorrow off.

sentences.japanese: 先生は「明日は休みです」と言いました。
sentences.english: The teacher said, “Tomorrow is a day off.”
sentences.nuanceNote: と closes the quoted message and attaches it to 言う; the quoted sentence can retain polite style.

sentences.japanese: 先生に、明日は休みかどうか聞きました。
sentences.english: I asked the teacher whether tomorrow was a day off.
sentences.nuanceNote: かどうか marks a yes/no question embedded as the content of 聞く. Do not assemble it as a quotation asserting the answer.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 104 (PDF p. 127). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文の組み立て：名詞修飾
meaning: Identify which noun a clause modifies.
connection: [Plain modifying clause] + head noun + particle
nuance: Find the head noun first, then determine its role in the main clause. The modifying clause is a unit, even if it contains its own subject and objects.
keyTakeaway: [Plain modifying clause] + head noun + particle

sentences.japanese: 昨日駅で会った人に、今日電話しました。
sentences.english: Today I called the person I met at the station yesterday.

sentences.japanese: 昨日駅で会った人から、メールが来ました。
sentences.english: I received an email from the person I met at the station yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: 昨日駅で会った modifies 人. The following から marks that whole noun phrase as the source.

sentences.japanese: 妹が作ったケーキを、みんなで食べました。
sentences.english: We all ate the cake my younger sister made.
sentences.nuanceNote: 妹が belongs inside the modifier; ケーキを is the object of the main predicate 食べました.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 106 (PDF p. 129). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文の組み立て：という・といった
meaning: Link content or representative examples to a noun.
connection: [Name/content]というN; [examples]といったN
nuance: という may label a thing or state the content of a report. といった gives representative examples. Preserve the noun following the whole modifier.
keyTakeaway: [Name/content]というN; [examples]といったN

sentences.japanese: 電車が遅れるという知らせを聞きました。
sentences.english: I heard a report that the train would be delayed.

sentences.japanese: 試験の日が変わったという知らせを聞きました。
sentences.english: I heard the news that the exam date had changed.
sentences.nuanceNote: という links a proposition to a noun describing its content; 知らせ is the main noun before を.

sentences.japanese: 京都や奈良といった町を訪ねました。
sentences.english: I visited cities such as Kyoto and Nara.
sentences.nuanceNote: といった presents examples of the following category. The list need not be exhaustive.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 108 (PDF p. 131). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文の組み立て：決まった形
meaning: Reconstruct fixed combinations before choosing word order.
connection: 例えば: Vば + V dictionaryほど; Nさえ + Vば
nuance: Build grammatical chunks before arranging the entire sentence. After placing them, read the sentence to check the intended meaning and the star position.
keyTakeaway: 例えば: Vば + V dictionaryほど; Nさえ + Vば

sentences.japanese: 練習すればするほど、楽しくなります。
sentences.english: The more I practice, the more enjoyable it becomes.

sentences.japanese: 一度読んだだけでは、全部理解できません。
sentences.english: I cannot understand everything after reading it only once.
sentences.nuanceNote: だけでは belongs together before the negative conclusion. Ordering fragments requires the complete construction.

sentences.japanese: 日本語を勉強し始めたばかりの学生です。
sentences.english: This is a student who has only just started studying Japanese.
sentences.nuanceNote: 勉強し始めたばかり modifies 学生 through の; retain the verb-suffix chain in order.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 110 (PDF p. 133). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：文頭と文末の対応
meaning: Match the topic at the start to a suitable ending.
connection: 理由は…からだ; 大切なのは…ことだ
nuance: Read past long modifiers to identify the topic-predicate relation. A reason topic should receive a reason, not an unrelated action.
keyTakeaway: 理由は…からだ; 大切なのは…ことだ

sentences.japanese: 私が早く帰る理由は、家で用事があるからです。
sentences.english: The reason I am going home early is that I have something to do at home.

sentences.japanese: 私がこの町を選んだ理由は、交通が便利だからです。
sentences.english: The reason I chose this town is that its transport is convenient.
sentences.nuanceNote: The topic 理由は needs a reason predicate; the intervening clause must not make you lose track of that structure.

sentences.japanese: この町に住みたいです。なぜなら、職場に近いからです。
sentences.english: I want to live in this town because it is close to my workplace.
sentences.useLabel: A cause introduced by なぜなら
sentences.nuanceNote: なぜなら introduces the explanation; からです completes the expected reason construction.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 116 (PDF p. 139). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：時制・ている
meaning: Keep the timeline and state consistent.
connection: Event time; reference time; Vている / Vていた
nuance: Distinguish an action in progress from its resulting state. A clause inside a past narrative may use non-past relative to the narrative's reference point.
keyTakeaway: Event time; reference time; Vている / Vていた

sentences.japanese: 駅に着いた時、雨が降っていました。
sentences.english: It was raining when I arrived at the station.

sentences.japanese: 駅に着いたとき、雨が降っていました。
sentences.english: It was raining when I reached the station.
sentences.nuanceNote: ていました presents the ongoing situation at the past arrival time.

sentences.japanese: 駅に着いたとき、店はもう閉まっていました。
sentences.english: When I reached the station, the shop had already closed.
sentences.nuanceNote: The closing happened earlier; ていました describes the resulting closed state, not ongoing closing.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 118 (PDF p. 141). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：自動詞・他動詞
meaning: Track the affected object and the agent.
connection: Thing が + intransitive; agent が thing を + transitive
nuance: Do not invent an agent for an intransitive sentence. Conversely, an action with an object needs the corresponding transitive construction.
keyTakeaway: Thing が + intransitive; agent が thing を + transitive

sentences.japanese: 窓が開いていました。私が閉めました。
sentences.english: The window was open. I closed it.

sentences.japanese: 窓が開いていました。寒かったので、私が閉めました。
sentences.english: The window was open. It was cold, so I closed it.
sentences.nuanceNote: 開く is intransitive; 閉める is transitive. The second sentence omits the understood object 窓を.

sentences.japanese: 私がコップを割ってしまいました。割れたコップは捨てました。
sentences.english: I accidentally broke a glass. I threw away the broken glass.
sentences.nuanceNote: 割る takes the object; 割れた modifies the resulting broken item. Follow the same participant across sentences.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 122 (PDF p. 145). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：てくる・ていく
meaning: Maintain a consistent spatial or temporal viewpoint.
connection: Vてくる: toward the reference point; Vていく: away/onward
nuance: The reference point can be now or a narrated scene. てきた can describe development up to now; ていく can describe future continuation.
keyTakeaway: Vてくる: toward the reference point; Vていく: away/onward

sentences.japanese: 日本語に慣れてきました。これからも勉強していきます。
sentences.english: I have become more accustomed to Japanese. I will keep studying from now on.

sentences.japanese: 友達がこちらへ歩いてきました。
sentences.english: My friend walked toward me.
sentences.nuanceNote: くる views the movement toward the speaker's reference point.

sentences.japanese: 日本語が少しずつ分かってきました。これからも勉強していきます。
sentences.english: I have gradually come to understand Japanese. I will keep studying from now on.
sentences.nuanceNote: てきた connects development to now; ていく projects continuation away from now into the future.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 124 (PDF p. 147). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N3: Spatiotemporal Direction Matrix: てくる vs ていく (p. 124)
table.subtitle: Spatial vectors, temporal evolution, and psychological emergence.

rows.label: Physical Space (空間的移動)
cells: Moving toward the speaker's current physical location.
Moving away from the speaker into distance.
黒い雲がこちらへ近づいてきた (Clouds approached us) vs 飛行機が遠くへ飛んでいった (Plane flew away).
Speaker is the spatial anchor point (原点).
rows.note: Spatial vector toward vs away from speaker.

rows.label: Time Dimension (時間的推移)
cells: Development from the past up to the present moment.
Progression from the present moment onward into the future.
日本で三年勉強してきた (Have studied up to now) vs これからも努力を続けていく (Will continue onward into future).
Present moment is the pivot point.
rows.note: Historical accumulation up to now vs future trajectory.

rows.label: Physiological / Emergence (生起・変化)
cells: Spontaneous internal sensation emerging into conscious perception.
Fading away, disappearing, or settling into extinction.
寒くなってきた / お腹が空いてきた (Felt cold / hunger emerge) vs 音が消えていった (Sound faded away).
Perception emerging inward vs dissolving outward.
rows.note: Internal emergence vs outward dissolution.

title: 文章：受身・使役・使役受身
meaning: Keep track of who acts, causes and experiences.
connection: 読む / 読まれる / 読ませる / 読ませられる
nuance: Mark each participant before selecting a voice. Being praised and being made to praise someone assign very different roles.
keyTakeaway: 読む / 読まれる / 読ませる / 読ませられる

sentences.japanese: 私は先生に褒められました。
sentences.english: I was praised by my teacher.

sentences.japanese: 弟に大切な本を汚されて、困りました。
sentences.english: My younger brother got my important book dirty, which caused me trouble.
sentences.nuanceNote: The omitted subject is the affected speaker; に marks the person who dirtied the book.

sentences.japanese: 先生は学生に作文を書かせました。学生は作文を書かされました。
sentences.english: The teacher made the students write an essay. The students were made to write it.
sentences.nuanceNote: The same event is viewed from the causer and then from those made to act. Particle roles and the subject change.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 128 (PDF p. 151). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：授受の視点
meaning: Keep the giver/receiver perspective consistent.
connection: Aが私にVてくれる; 私がAにVてもらう
nuance: The subject differs between giving and receiving frames. Follow the paragraph's continuing topic rather than translating each verb in isolation.
keyTakeaway: Aが私にVてくれる; 私がAにVてもらう

sentences.japanese: 友達が道を教えてくれました。おかげで迷わずに着きました。
sentences.english: A friend gave me directions. Thanks to that, I arrived without getting lost.

sentences.japanese: 友達が道を教えてくれました。それで、迷わずに着きました。
sentences.english: A friend showed me the way, so I arrived without getting lost.
sentences.nuanceNote: くれる presents the friend's action as a benefit toward the speaker's side.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に道を教えてもらいました。
sentences.english: I had a friend show me the way.
sentences.nuanceNote: もらう makes the receiver the subject; に identifies the person giving the help.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 130 (PDF p. 153). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：指示表現
meaning: Resolve what こ・そ・あ refers to.
connection: この/その/あのN; これ/それ/あれ
nuance: Look for an antecedent in the nearby text. それ may refer to an entire previous event, not only the nearest noun. あれ can refer to shared remembered experience.
keyTakeaway: この/その/あのN; これ/それ/あれ

sentences.japanese: 新しい辞書を買いました。それはとても使いやすいです。
sentences.english: I bought a new dictionary. It is very easy to use.

sentences.japanese: 新しい机を買いました。その机は窓のそばに置きました。
sentences.english: I bought a new desk. I put it beside the window.
sentences.nuanceNote: その机 refers back to the previously introduced desk; the second sentence omits the subject 私.

sentences.japanese: 電車が遅れました。それで、会議に間に合いませんでした。
sentences.english: The train was delayed. Because of that, I did not make it to the meeting on time.
sentences.nuanceNote: それ refers to the preceding situation as a cause, not merely to the noun 電車.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 134 (PDF p. 157). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：は・が
meaning: Follow established topics and identify new subjects.
connection: Topic は; identifying/descriptive subject が
nuance: The distinction depends on discourse, not a fixed rule that は always means contrast or が always means new information. Notice question-answer focus and subordinate clauses.
keyTakeaway: Topic は; identifying/descriptive subject が

sentences.japanese: 庭に猫がいました。その猫は白かったです。
sentences.english: There was a cat in the garden. The cat was white.

sentences.japanese: 庭に猫がいます。その猫は毎朝ここに来ます。
sentences.english: There is a cat in the garden. That cat comes here every morning.
sentences.useLabel: Introduce a subject, then continue its topic
sentences.nuanceNote: が introduces the cat in the existence statement; は then presents it as the continuing topic.

sentences.japanese: 誰が説明しますか。私が説明します。
sentences.english: Who will explain? I will.
sentences.nuanceNote: が identifies the requested person. This focus differs from introducing a general topic with は.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 159). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：接続表現
meaning: Identify the logical link between sentences.
connection: だから: result; しかし: contrast; つまり: restatement; 例えば: example
nuance: Choose a connector from the relation between complete propositions. Matching a single keyword is not sufficient.
keyTakeaway: だから: result; しかし: contrast; つまり: restatement; 例えば: example

sentences.japanese: 雨が強くなりました。そのため、試合は中止になりました。
sentences.english: The rain became heavier. As a result, the match was canceled.

sentences.japanese: 雨が強くなりました。それでも、試合は続きました。
sentences.english: The rain got heavier. Even so, the match continued.
sentences.nuanceNote: それでも presents continuation despite a circumstance that could have stopped it.

sentences.japanese: この部屋には誰もいません。つまり、今は使われていません。
sentences.english: There is nobody in this room. In other words, it is not being used now.
sentences.nuanceNote: つまり reformulates the point; choose it from the logical relation, not from a shared word.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 140 (PDF p. 163). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：文体の統一
meaning: Keep narration and quoted speech in appropriate registers.
connection: Polite です/ます; plain だ/である; quotations may differ
nuance: A paragraph normally maintains a consistent narrative style. Direct quotations may legitimately use another register; do not mechanically change every plain form.
keyTakeaway: Polite です/ます; plain だ/である; quotations may differ

sentences.japanese: この町は静かです。交通も便利です。
sentences.english: This town is quiet. Transportation is convenient too.

sentences.japanese: この町は静かです。公園も多く、住みやすいです。
sentences.english: This town is quiet. It also has many parks and is easy to live in.
sentences.nuanceNote: The surrounding narrative maintains polite endings while an internal connective clause need not end in です.

sentences.japanese: 彼は「明日は行かない」と言いました。私は驚きました。
sentences.english: He said, “I am not going tomorrow.” I was surprised.
sentences.useLabel: A quotation can have a different style
sentences.nuanceNote: Plain speech inside a direct quote is compatible with polite surrounding narration. Do not mechanically change quoted speech.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 142 (PDF p. 165). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に際して / 〜にあたって (Upon the Occasion Of / At the Inception Of)
meaning: Formal expression used when initiating an important event, official occasion, or milestone: "On the occasion of / Prior to commencing X".
connection: V-辞書形 + に際して / にあたって | Noun + に際して / にあたって
nuance: Formal written and spoken expression used for significant occasions, official ceremonies, starting contracts, overseas travel, or inaugural greetings. It sets a formal, forward-looking tone. It is not used for everyday routine actions like waking up or eating lunch.
keyTakeaway: V-る / Noun + に際して・にあたって = Formal expression for significant occasions or inaugural milestones.

sentences.japanese: 新会社の設立にあたって、出資者と関係各位に心より感謝の意を表します。
sentences.english: Upon the establishment of our new company, I express my heartfelt gratitude to the investors and all parties concerned.
sentences.literal: New-company establishment upon, investors and related-parties-to heart-from gratitude express.

tokens.word: 新会社の設立にあたって
tokens.reading: しんがいしゃのせつりつにあたって

sentences.nuanceNote: Solemn inaugural corporate speech.

sentences.japanese: 入学に際して、必要な書類を提出してください。
sentences.english: Please submit the required documents on entering the school.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nに際して marks a formal/significant occasion; it is not a general replacement for every とき.

sentences.japanese: 新しい事業を始めるにあたって、専門家に相談しました。
sentences.english: Before embarking on a new business, I consulted a specialist.
sentences.nuanceNote: V dictionary + にあたって frames preparation for an undertaking. It is common with forward-looking occasions.

quiz.question: 留学（　　）あたって、現地での生活費や保険について詳しく調べた。
quiz.translation: Prior to studying abroad, I thoroughly researched living expenses and health insurance in the destination country.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + にあたって milestone preparation
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + に際して / にあたって | Noun + に際して / にあたって

explanations.reason: Correct! 留学にあたって expresses careful preparatory measures for a major life event.
Incorrect. 留学をあたって is an invalid particle combination.
Incorrect. 留学へあたって is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 留学であたって does not exist.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 8 (PDF p. 18). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜（か）と思うと / 〜（か）と思ったら (Just as I Thought X, Y Suddenly Burst Forth)
meaning: No sooner had condition X occurred than unexpected event Y abruptly and surprisingly burst forth: 'Hardly had... when suddenly...'.
connection: V-た + （か）と思うと / （か）と思ったら
nuance: SUDDEN REVERSAL: Clause B describes an instantaneous, jarring surprise or sudden shift. CANNOT be the speaker's own planned action or volition!
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た + かと思ったら = Just when I thought X, BAM, sudden surprise Y happened!

sentences.japanese: 空が急に暗くなったかと思うと、激しい雷雨が降り出した。
sentences.english: No sooner had the sky suddenly turned dark than a violent thunderstorm began pouring down.
sentences.literal: Sky suddenly dark-became thought-when, violent thunderstorm began-falling.

tokens.word: 暗くなったかと思うと
tokens.reading: くらくなったかとおもうと
tokens.romaji: kuraku natta ka to omou to

sentences.nuanceNote: Jarring meteorological onset.

sentences.japanese: 空が暗くなったかと思うと、激しい雨が降り始めました。
sentences.english: The sky had barely darkened when heavy rain began.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker observes a rapid transition, rather than stating a planned action triggered by a condition.

sentences.japanese: 子供は泣いたかと思ったら、もう笑っていました。
sentences.english: The child had barely started crying before they were laughing again.
sentences.nuanceNote: The change can be a striking contrast in behavior; the expression need not report a literal intervening thought.

quiz.question: 赤ちゃんは今泣いていた（　　）思うと、もうすやすや眠っている。
quiz.translation: Just when I thought the baby was crying right now, he is already sleeping peacefully.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜かと思うと sudden transition
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + （か）と思うと / （か）と思ったら

explanations.reason: Correct! 泣いていたかと思うと expresses lightning-fast reversal of baby's state.
Incorrect. なと is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. にと is invalid.
Incorrect. へと indicates directional transformation.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 8 (PDF p. 18). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜か〜ないかのうちに (On the Very Verge Of / Before Even Finishing)
meaning: Action Y takes place virtually simultaneously with action X, so fast that one can barely tell if X even finished: 'No sooner had... than...'.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-た + か + V-ない + かのうちに
nuance: PHYSICAL FRACTION OF A SECOND: The bell hasn't even finished vibrating before the students dash out (ベルが鳴り終わるか終わらないかのうちに飛び出した).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-る + か + V-ない + かのうちに = Before X even finished, Y happened!

sentences.japanese: 授業終了のチャイムが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。
sentences.english: No sooner had the end-of-class chime begun ringing than the students dashed out of the classroom.
sentences.literal: Class-end chime ring or ring-not within, students classroom dashed-out.

tokens.word: 鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに
tokens.reading: なるかならないかのうちに
tokens.romaji: naru ka naranai ka no uchi ni

sentences.nuanceNote: Instantaneous burst of action at the bell.

sentences.japanese: ベルが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、学生たちが立ち上がりました。
sentences.english: The students stood up almost before the bell had rung.
sentences.nuanceNote: The repeated verb frames the event at the boundary of completion.

sentences.japanese: 家に着くか着かないかのうちに、雨が降り出しました。
sentences.english: It began raining just as I was arriving home.
sentences.nuanceNote: This is an immediate temporal sequence, not a deliberate future request.

quiz.question: 布団に横に（　　）か横にならないかのうちに、深い眠りに落ちてしまった。
quiz.translation: No sooner had I lain down on the futon than I fell into a deep sleep.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-るか〜ないかのうちに simultaneous timing
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-た + か + V-ない + かのうちに

explanations.reason: Correct! 辞書形 横になるか + 横にならないかのうちに is the canonical pair.
Incorrect. なって is te-form.
Incorrect. なり is masu-stem.
Incorrect. なら is conditional.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 8 (PDF p. 18). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜たとたん（に） (The Very Instant That / Concurrently Burst Forth)
meaning: The precise split-second an action finishes, an unexpected, instantaneous event occurs without warning: 'No sooner had... than / The moment that...'.
connection: V-た形 + とたん（に）
nuance: UNFORESEEN SURPRISE: Clause Y must be an instantaneous reaction outside the speaker's conscious control. You CANNOT use speaker's planned will or intention in clause Y (❌ 窓を開けたとたん、掃除した).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た + とたんに = 'The instant X happened, unexpected surprise Y broke out!'.

sentences.japanese: ドアを開けたとたんに、強烈な冷たい風が部屋の中に吹き込んできた。
sentences.english: The very instant I opened the door, a fierce freezing blast of wind swept into the room.
sentences.literal: Door opened instant-at, fierce cold wind room-of inside-into blew.
sentences.nuanceNote: Sudden physical reaction upon opening door.

sentences.japanese: 立ち上がったとたん、めまいがしました。
sentences.english: The moment I stood up, I felt dizzy.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたとたん links an immediate occurrence that was not presented as the speaker's planned next action.

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けたとたん、強い風が入ってきました。
sentences.english: The instant I opened the window, a strong wind blew in.
sentences.nuanceNote: The first action is completed at the point the second event occurs.

quiz.question: 疲れてベッドに横になった（　　）、あっという間に眠りに落ちてしまった。
quiz.translation: The moment I lay down on the bed from sheer exhaustion, I fell into a deep sleep in an instant.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た + とたん (Instantaneous reaction)
quiz.ruleHint: V-た形 + とたん（に）

explanations.reason: Correct! 横になったとたん expresses falling asleep instantaneous upon lying down.
Incorrect. 横になった最中 is ungrammatical (最中 requires ongoing action: 横になっている最中).
Incorrect. 横になったばかり denotes recent completion, not instantaneous reaction.
Incorrect. 横になった一方 is meaningless here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 8 (PDF p. 18). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜際に
meaning: On the occasion of doing something.
connection: V dictionary/た + 際に; Nの際に
nuance: More formal than とき. Common in instructions and notices. The form before 際 depends on whether the event is prospective or completed.
keyTakeaway: V dictionary/た + 際に; Nの際に

sentences.japanese: 申請する際に、身分証を持参してください。
sentences.english: Please bring identification when applying.

sentences.japanese: お申し込みの際に、身分証明書をご提示ください。
sentences.english: Please present identification when applying.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nの際に is formal wording for an occasion and can introduce an instruction.

sentences.japanese: 京都を訪れた際に、先生にお会いしました。
sentences.english: When I visited Kyoto, I met my teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vた際に describes a past occasion; 際に is not limited to future beginnings.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 8 (PDF p. 18). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜最中だ / 〜最中に (In the Very Thick Of / Climax of Activity)
meaning: Right in the middle of an ongoing activity.
connection: V-ている + 最中に / 最中だ | Noun + の + 最中に / 最中だ
nuance: 最中 means right in the middle of an activity. An unexpected interruption often follows 最中に, but interruption is a common context, not an obligatory part of its meaning.
keyTakeaway: 最中 means right in the middle of an activity. An unexpected interruption often follows 最中に, but interruption is a common context, not an obligatory part of its meaning.

sentences.japanese: 重要なプレゼンテーションを行っている最中に、停電でプロジェクターが消えてしまった。
sentences.english: Right in the middle of delivering an important presentation, the projector shut off due to a power outage.
sentences.literal: Important presentation conducting middle-in, blackout-by projector vanished-regrettably.

tokens.meaning: right in the middle of conducting
tokens.reading: おこなっているさいちゅうに

sentences.nuanceNote: Severe external disruption during presentation.

sentences.japanese: 会議をしている最中に、停電しました。
sentences.english: There was a power cut right in the middle of the meeting.
sentences.nuanceNote: An interruption is common after 最中に; the ongoing activity uses ている.

sentences.japanese: 今は準備の最中です。
sentences.english: We are in the middle of preparations now.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nの最中だ simply states an ongoing phase; it does not require an unexpected bad event.

quiz.question: 食事の最中（　　）、電話が鳴りました。
quiz.translation: The phone rang in the middle of the meal.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + の + 最中に disruptive interruption
quiz.ruleHint: V-ている + 最中に / 最中だ | Noun + の + 最中に / 最中だ

explanations.reason: 最中に locates the event during the activity.
を does not mark this time relation.
の needs a following noun.
と does not link this time relation.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 12 (PDF p. 22). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ばかりだ / 〜一方だ (Continual Single-Directional Trend: Keep On -ing)
meaning: A change continues in one direction.
connection: V dictionary + 一方だ / ばかりだ
nuance: Use with a predicate that describes change, such as 増える, 減る or 悪くなる. It does not necessarily mean that the rate accelerates. 一方だ can describe favorable or unfavorable trends; ばかりだ often presents an unwelcome trend. Other constructions with 一方 or ばかり have other meanings, so do not apply this restriction to every occurrence of the word.
keyTakeaway: Continuing in one direction does not mean accelerating.

sentences.japanese: 少子高齢化が進み、地方都市の人口は減少する一方だ。
sentences.english: With birth rates declining and population aging, the populations of regional cities keep on dwindling relentlessly.
sentences.literal: Declining-birth aging advance, regional-city population decrease one-direction-is.

tokens.reading: げんしょうするいっぽうだ

sentences.nuanceNote: Relentless demographic decline.

sentences.japanese: 修理をしないので、状態は悪くなるばかりです。
sentences.english: Because it is not being repaired, its condition keeps getting worse.
sentences.nuanceNote: ばかりだ presents a one-direction trend, often evaluated negatively.

sentences.japanese: 利用者は増える一方です。
sentences.english: The number of users keeps increasing.
sentences.nuanceNote: 一方だ does not itself state whether the growth is good or bad, or whether its rate is accelerating.

quiz.question: 不景気の影響で、会社の業績は悪化する（　　）だ。
quiz.translation: Under the impact of the recession, company performance is only worsening further and further.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + ばかりだ continual deterioration
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary + 一方だ / ばかりだ

explanations.reason: Correct! 悪化するばかりだ expresses continuous negative downward spiral.
Incorrect. ところだ indicates temporal phase.
Incorrect. わけだ indicates logical consequence.
Incorrect. ことだ indicates advice or exclamation.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 12 (PDF p. 22). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜つつある (Currently in Continuous Transition / Underway)
meaning: Indicates that an evolutionary process or dynamic transformation is steadily progressing in real time: 'is in the ongoing process of -ing'.
connection: V-stem (masu-stem) + つつある
nuance: つつある presents an ongoing change or development in a relatively formal register. It is common with gradual changes and is not the normal choice for an ordinary action merely in progress.
keyTakeaway: つつある presents an ongoing change or development in a relatively formal register. It is common with gradual changes and is not the normal choice for an ordinary action merely in progress.

sentences.japanese: 医療技術の急速な進歩により、かつての難病も克服されつつある。
sentences.english: Owing to rapid advances in medical technology, formerly intractable illnesses are steadily being overcome.
sentences.literal: Medical technology rapid progress due-to, former intractable-illnesses overcome-being-underway.

tokens.meaning: is in the process of being overcome
tokens.reading: こくふくされつつある

sentences.nuanceNote: Formal scientific commentary on healthcare progression.

sentences.japanese: 町の景色は少しずつ変わりつつあります。
sentences.english: The townscape is gradually changing.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + つつある presents a process of change underway, often in formal writing.

sentences.japanese: 景気は回復しつつあります。
sentences.english: The economy is in the process of recovering.
sentences.nuanceNote: The construction highlights transition; it is not the ordinary way to say a person is eating right now.

quiz.question: 地球温暖化の影響で、北極の氷が年々解け（　　）。
quiz.translation: Due to the impacts of global warming, the Arctic ice is steadily melting year by year.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + つつある (Ongoing macro trend)
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (masu-stem) + つつある

explanations.reason: Correct! 解けつつある describes the ongoing gradual environmental transformation.
Incorrect. つつあることだ is structurally incoherent.
Incorrect. つつあるまい is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. つつあるべきだ does not make sense here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 12 (PDF p. 22). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜うちに・〜ようとしている
meaning: While a condition lasts; just about to change.
connection: V dictionary/ない/ている + うちに; volitional + としている
nuance: うちに can signal a chance before a condition changes. ようとしている can describe an imminent change, even without a human intention.
keyTakeaway: V dictionary/ない/ている + うちに; volitional + としている

sentences.japanese: 日が暮れようとしています。明るいうちに帰りましょう。
sentences.english: The sun is about to set. Let us return while it is light.

sentences.japanese: 暗くならないうちに、帰りましょう。
sentences.english: Let's go home before it gets dark.
sentences.nuanceNote: ないうちに sets a limited opportunity before the state changes.

sentences.japanese: 長い冬が終わろうとしています。
sentences.english: The long winter is about to end.
sentences.nuanceNote: Volitional + としている can describe an event on the verge of occurring, without a human agent intending it.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 12 (PDF p. 22). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜つつ・〜つつも
meaning: Simultaneous action or acting despite awareness.
connection: Vます-stem + つつ / つつも
nuance: The simultaneous use is relatively formal and shares a subject. Concessive つつ often contrasts what someone knows or thinks with what they do.
keyTakeaway: Vます-stem + つつ / つつも

sentences.japanese: 悪いと知りつつ、約束を破ってしまいました。
sentences.english: Although I knew it was wrong, I broke my promise.

sentences.japanese: 資料を確認しつつ、説明を聞きました。
sentences.english: I listened to the explanation while checking the documents.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stemつつ can link simultaneous activities by the same actor, in a relatively formal style.

sentences.japanese: 悪いと知りつつも、約束を破ってしまいました。
sentences.english: Although I knew it was wrong, I broke the promise.
sentences.nuanceNote: つつも expresses a conflict between awareness and action, not simultaneity alone.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 12 (PDF p. 22). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てはじめて (Only After Experiencing X Did Y Truly Dawn Upon Me)
meaning: Expresses that only after an event occurred or only upon personally experiencing X did one truly recognize, understand, or realize situation Y.
connection: V-て形 + はじめて
nuance: EPIPHANY THROUGH FIRST EXPERIENCE: 'You don't appreciate health until you get sick': 病気になってはじめて健康のありがたさを知った (Only after falling ill did I appreciate the blessing of health).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + はじめて = 'Only after X happened did I finally open my eyes to Y!'.

sentences.japanese: 一人暮らしを始めてはじめて、親が毎日家事をしてくれていたありがたさに気づいた。
sentences.english: Only after beginning to live alone did I truly realize the immense gratitude I owe my parents for doing chores daily.
sentences.literal: Living-alone started only-after, parents daily chores did gratitude realized.
sentences.nuanceNote: Young adult coming of age realization.

sentences.japanese: 一人で暮らしてはじめて、家事の大変さが分かりました。
sentences.english: Only after living alone did I understand how hard housework is.
sentences.nuanceNote: The experience enables a realization not previously attained.

sentences.japanese: 実際に使ってはじめて、この道具の便利さが分かります。
sentences.english: Only by actually using it can you appreciate how useful this tool is.
sentences.nuanceNote: The first action is necessary for the later understanding; this is not simply two events in sequence.

quiz.question: 実際に海外で生活し（　　）はじめて、自国の文化の特徴を客観的に見直すことができた。
quiz.translation: Only after actually living abroad was I able to re-examine the characteristics of my own country's culture objectively.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + はじめて (Epiphany through experience)
quiz.ruleHint: V-て形 + はじめて

explanations.reason: Correct! 生活してみてはじめて (or 生活してはじめて) forms 'only after living abroad'.
Incorrect. 生活したらはじめて is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 生活してもはじめて is invalid.
Incorrect. 生活しつつはじめて is grammatically impossible.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 26). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜上（で） (Upon Thorough Completion of Prerequisite X / In Doing X)
meaning: Two functions: (1) After completing prerequisite inspection/consultation X, proceed to Y ('After... / Upon...'); (2) In the context/domain of doing X ('When it comes to...').
connection: Prerequisite Sense: V-た形 + 上で | Noun + の上で | Context Sense: V-辞書形 + 上で
nuance: DELIBERATE PREREQUISITE: Requires deliberate investigation, agreement, or thought: '家族と相談した上で、決断します' (After consulting with family, I will make my decision).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た / Nounの + 上で = 'Only after thorough check X is complete will next action happen!'.

sentences.japanese: 契約書の内容をよくご確認いただいた上で、こちらにご署名をお願いいたします。
sentences.english: After having thoroughly verified the contents of the contract, please furnish your signature here.
sentences.literal: Contract-of contents well verify-receive after-upon, here signature please-do.

tokens.word: ご確認いただいた上で
tokens.reading: ごかくにんいただいたうえで

sentences.nuanceNote: Formal business contractual execution.

sentences.japanese: 内容をよく確認した上で、署名してください。
sentences.english: Please sign after checking the contents carefully.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vた上で treats the completed action as a prerequisite for the next step.

sentences.japanese: 仕事を選ぶ上で、何を大切にしていますか。
sentences.english: What do you consider important when choosing a job?
sentences.nuanceNote: V dictionary上で identifies the activity or standpoint within which a consideration matters; it does not mean after choosing.

quiz.question: 担当者と詳しく話し合っ（　　）上で、今後のスケジュールを決定いたします。
quiz.translation: After discussing the details with the person in charge, we will determine our future schedule.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た + 上で (Prerequisite step)
quiz.ruleHint: Prerequisite Sense: V-た形 + 上で | Noun + の上で | Context Sense: V-辞書形 + 上で

explanations.reason: Correct! V-た + 上で expresses 'after having held discussions'.
Incorrect. 話し合って上で is ungrammatical (must be 話し合った上で).
Incorrect. 話し合う上で means 'in the process of discussing', which clashes with determining future schedule afterward.
Incorrect. 話し合っても上で is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 26). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜次第：時間
meaning: As soon as a prerequisite is completed.
connection: Vます-stem + 次第
nuance: Common in plans, announcements and requests. It normally introduces an intended subsequent action, rather than narrating an accidental past sequence.
keyTakeaway: Vます-stem + 次第

sentences.japanese: 結果が分かり次第、ご連絡します。
sentences.english: I will contact you as soon as I know the result.

sentences.japanese: 日程が決まり次第、ご連絡します。
sentences.english: I will contact you as soon as the schedule is decided.
sentences.useLabel: Planned action immediately after a trigger
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem次第 introduces the future trigger for a planned response.

sentences.japanese: 準備ができ次第、出発してください。
sentences.english: Please leave as soon as the preparations are complete.
sentences.nuanceNote: The final clause can be a request; distinguish temporal 次第 from N次第 meaning depending on.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 26). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜て以来・〜てこのかた
meaning: A state continuing since an event.
connection: Vて + 以来 / このかた; N以来
nuance: The initial event is a starting boundary and the following state continues through the relevant period. Do not use it merely for one unrelated event afterward.
keyTakeaway: Vて + 以来 / このかた; N以来

sentences.japanese: 引っ越して以来、毎朝歩いています。
sentences.english: Since moving, I have been walking every morning.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ来て以来、毎日日記を書いています。
sentences.english: I have kept a diary every day since coming to Japan.
sentences.nuanceNote: て以来 presents continuity over the period after the starting event.

sentences.japanese: 引っ越してこのかた、前の友達には会っていません。
sentences.english: Since moving, I have not seen my old friends.
sentences.useLabel: Sustained state since a major change
sentences.nuanceNote: てこのかた is a relatively formal expression emphasizing the period since the event.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 26). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てからでないと
meaning: Not possible until an action is completed.
connection: Vて + からでないと / からでなければ
nuance: Usually followed by an inability or negative consequence. It makes the first action a prerequisite.
keyTakeaway: Vて + からでないと / からでなければ

sentences.japanese: 説明を聞いてからでないと、決められません。
sentences.english: I cannot decide until I have heard the explanation.

sentences.japanese: 実物を見てからでないと、買うかどうか決められません。
sentences.english: I cannot decide whether to buy it until I see the actual item.
sentences.nuanceNote: The consequence is negative in meaning before the prerequisite is satisfied.

sentences.japanese: 許可をもらってからでなければ、使用は無理です。
sentences.english: Using it is impossible until permission has been obtained.
sentences.nuanceNote: 無理 provides the negative meaning; the grammar does not require a literal ない ending.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 26). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜をはじめ（として） (Starting with Representative Prime Example X)
meaning: Singles out prime representative example X first, followed by numerous other members of the same category: 'Starting with X, as well as many others'.
connection: Noun + をはじめ（として） / をはじめとする + Noun
nuance: CHIEF REPRESENTATIVE: Entity X is the most prominent, flagship, or famous example (e.g. 'Starting with Tokyo, cities across Japan...').
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Noun + をはじめとして = Prime flagship example first, plus the rest!

sentences.japanese: 富士山をはじめ、日本には四季折々の美しい景観が数多く存在する。
sentences.english: Starting with Mt. Fuji, there exist numerous breathtaking landscapes reflecting the four seasons in Japan.
sentences.literal: Mt-Fuji starting-with, Japan-in four-seasons beautiful landscapes many exist.
sentences.nuanceNote: Flagship natural landmark leading into nationwide landscapes.

sentences.japanese: 校長先生をはじめ、多くの先生が出席しました。
sentences.english: Many teachers attended, including the principal.
sentences.useLabel: Representative example in a wider group
sentences.nuanceNote: The principal is a prominent representative, not necessarily the first person in chronological order.

sentences.japanese: 京都をはじめとする古い町を訪ねました。
sentences.english: I visited old towns including Kyoto.
sentences.nuanceNote: をはじめとする modifies the following noun phrase.

quiz.question: 社長（　　）社員全員が一丸となって、新事業の成功に取り組んだ。
quiz.translation: Starting with the company president, all employees united as one and tackled the success of the new business.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + をはじめ representative leader
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + をはじめ（として） / をはじめとする + Noun

explanations.reason: Correct! 社長をはじめ marks the president as the leading representative of the entire company.
Incorrect. をめぐって means concerning a dispute.
Incorrect. をもとに means based on data/material.
Incorrect. にそって means conforming to rules.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 20 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜からして (Judging Even from One Clue: Starting from the Very...)
meaning: Singles out one basic, representative clue or initial detail X to make an assessment about the whole: "Judging even from the very X...". Often used for critical assessments, but can also be used in positive appraisals.
connection: Noun + からして
nuance: Highlights an initial or prominent feature X as sufficient evidence to evaluate the entire whole. While frequently used to point out initial shortcomings (タイトルからして怪しい), it is also used for strong positive impressions (さすが一流店だ、盛り付けの美しさからして違う).
keyTakeaway: Noun + からして = "Judging even from this one initial detail, the whole thing is..." (used for both negative critiques and positive praise).

sentences.japanese: 彼の態度は、挨拶の言葉遣いからして社会人としてなっていない。
sentences.english: His attitude, judging even from his very choice of words in greetings, is completely unacceptable as a working adult.
sentences.literal: His attitude, greeting's word-choice from-even working-adult-as unacceptable.

tokens.reading: ことばづかいからして

sentences.nuanceNote: Basic flaw indicating systemic unprofessionalism.

sentences.japanese: この店は入口からして、とても豪華です。
sentences.english: Even the entrance to this shop is very luxurious.
sentences.nuanceNote: からして singles out an initial/basic feature suggesting what the whole is like.

sentences.japanese: 話し方からして、かなり緊張しているようです。
sentences.english: Judging from the way they speak, they seem quite nervous.
sentences.nuanceNote: The feature is used as a basis for inference; do not translate it as a starting time.

quiz.question: この店の料理は、盛り付けの美しさ（　　）して一流の気品が漂っている。
quiz.translation: This restaurant's cuisine, judging even from the sheer beauty of its presentation, radiates first-class elegance.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + からして indicative clue
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + からして

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜からして singles out presentation as an immediate indicative proof of top quality.
Incorrect. までして indicates extreme drastic measure ('even going so far as to...').
Incorrect. よりして is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. ほどして is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 20 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜にわたって / 〜にわたり (Spanning Across Extensive Time or Space)
meaning: Indicates that a state, event, or activity extends over a wide geographical area, a long span of time, or multiple times/fields: "Spanning across / Extending over X".
connection: Noun (Time Span / Space Expanse / Number of Sessions) + にわたって / にわたり
nuance: Connects to expressions of broad time, space, frequency, or field: 数十キロにわたって (stretching across dozens of km), 三年間にわたって (spanning three years), 全五回にわたり (held over 5 sessions). It emphasizes breadth and comprehensive scope, not that an activity is literally uninterrupted without sleep or pause.
keyTakeaway: [Range / Time span / Area] + にわたって = Extending across or spanning a broad scale.

sentences.japanese: 台風の影響で、この地域は三日間にわたって停電が続いた。
sentences.english: Under the influence of the typhoon, power outages persisted across this region spanning three full days.
sentences.literal: Typhoon influence-by, this region 3-days-spanning blackout continued.

tokens.reading: みっかかんにわたって

sentences.nuanceNote: Extensive temporal blackout span.

sentences.japanese: 工事は三か月にわたって続きました。
sentences.english: The construction continued over three months.
sentences.nuanceNote: にわたって emphasizes the extent of the period, rather than naming a starting point.

sentences.japanese: 大雨の被害は県全体にわたっています。
sentences.english: The damage from heavy rain extends across the whole prefecture.
sentences.nuanceNote: The scope can be spatial rather than temporal.

quiz.question: 高速道路は事故のため、十キロ（　　）わたって渋滞している。
quiz.translation: Due to an accident, the expressway is congested spanning across ten kilometers.
quiz.grammarFocus: Spatial span 〜にわたって
quiz.ruleHint: Noun (Time Span / Space Expanse / Number of Sessions) + にわたって / にわたり

explanations.reason: Correct! 十キロにわたって indicates the continuous 10km spatial span of the traffic jam.
Incorrect. をわたって is ungrammatical with this construction.
Incorrect. へわたって does not exist.
Incorrect. でわたって is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 20 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜を通じて・〜を通して
meaning: Throughout a period or through an intermediary.
connection: N + を通じて / を通して
nuance: A time noun gives throughout; a person, activity or organization can be a medium. Direct tools normally take で.
keyTakeaway: N + を通じて / を通して

sentences.japanese: 一年を通じて、この町は暖かいです。
sentences.english: This town is warm throughout the year.

sentences.japanese: この地域は一年を通じて温暖です。
sentences.english: This region is mild throughout the year.
sentences.nuanceNote: を通じて describes a condition spanning a whole period.

sentences.japanese: 友人を通して、その仕事を知りました。
sentences.english: I learned about the job through a friend.
sentences.nuanceNote: を通して names an intermediary, not the duration of the event.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 20 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜限り・〜だけ：最大範囲
meaning: The full extent of what is available or possible.
connection: V dictionary/possible + 限り; V possible + だけ
nuance: できる限り and できるだけ both express doing as much as possible. This maximum-range meaning differs from restrictive に限り and conditional 限りは.
keyTakeaway: V dictionary/possible + 限り; V possible + だけ

sentences.japanese: 分かる限りのことを説明しました。
sentences.english: I explained everything I knew.

sentences.japanese: できる限り、手伝います。
sentences.english: I will help as much as I can.
sentences.nuanceNote: 限り expresses the maximum extent within the speaker's ability.

sentences.japanese: 今日は食べられるだけ食べてください。
sentences.english: Please eat as much as you can today.
sentences.nuanceNote: Potential verb + だけ sets the possible extent. It is not merely only eat rather than drink.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 20 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜限りでは (As Far As Scope of Information Reaches: Insofar As)
meaning: Restricts a judgment strictly to the boundary of personal knowledge, research, memory, or reports: 'As far as my knowledge/investigation goes...'.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-た + 限りでは | Noun + の + 限りでは (Pairs with informational verbs: 知る, 見る, 聞く, 調べた)
nuance: EPISTEMIC HUMILITY: Protects the speaker against being wrong outside their range: '私が知っている限りでは問題ありません' (As far as I know, there are no issues).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [知る / 聞く / 調べる] + 限りでは = 'As far as my information reaches...'.

sentences.japanese: 私が調べた限りでは、この地域に同業他社の店舗はまだ存在しません。
sentences.english: As far as my investigation reaches, no competitor stores exist in this region yet.
sentences.literal: I investigated extent-in, this region competitor stores yet exist-not.

tokens.meaning: as far as I have researched

sentences.nuanceNote: Scoping market research claim.

sentences.japanese: 私が知っている限りでは、その店は日曜も開いています。
sentences.english: As far as I know, that shop is open on Sundays too.
sentences.nuanceNote: The statement is limited to the speaker's information, not guaranteed beyond it.

sentences.japanese: 調べた限りでは、問題は見つかりませんでした。
sentences.english: As far as my investigation went, no problem was found.
sentences.nuanceNote: The phrase qualifies the evidence base; it does not prove that no problem exists anywhere.

quiz.question: 私が調べた（　　）では、今回の事件で怪我人は出ていないようだ。
quiz.translation: As far as the police announcement indicates, no injuries appear to have occurred in this incident.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た / V-る + 限りでは (Scope of information)
quiz.ruleHint: V-る / V-た / V-ている + 限りでは: Insofar as / As far as the scope of information reaches

explanations.reason: Correct! 調べた限りでは (as far as my investigation reaches) sets the epistemic boundary of knowledge.
Incorrect. 調べただけでは means "merely by investigating (it is insufficient to...)", which does not fit the affirmative evidential clause.
Incorrect. 調べたほどでは is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 調べたわけでは is typically followed by ない (わけではない) for partial denial.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 34). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に限り・〜に限って
meaning: A restriction, special case or emphatic exception.
connection: N + に限り / に限って
nuance: に限り is common in formal eligibility notices. に限って can also limit a case, or express unlucky timing and confident exceptions. Do not restrict it to only the emotional uses.
keyTakeaway: N + に限り / に限って

sentences.japanese: 本日に限り、入場は無料です。急ぐ日に限って電車が遅れます。
sentences.english: Admission is free today only. The train is late precisely on days when I am in a hurry.

sentences.japanese: 会員に限り、入場料が無料です。
sentences.english: Admission is free for members only.
sentences.nuanceNote: に限り restricts eligibility; it does not mean members are the best choice.

sentences.japanese: 急いでいる日に限って、電車が遅れます。
sentences.english: The train is delayed on the very days when I am in a hurry.
sentences.nuanceNote: に限って singles out an inconvenient occasion, often with frustration.

sentences.japanese: あの人に限って、約束を忘れるはずがありません。
sentences.english: That person of all people surely would not forget a promise.
sentences.nuanceNote: に限って identifies someone the speaker trusts to be an exception; it is different from an eligibility restriction.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 34). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜限りは・〜限りでは
meaning: While a condition holds; within the scope of knowledge.
connection: Plain clause + 限りは; information clause + 限りでは
nuance: Conditional 限りは means as long as. 限りでは restricts the evidence or knowledge underlying a statement, not its duration.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + 限りは; information clause + 限りでは

sentences.japanese: 私が知っている限りでは、問題はありません。
sentences.english: As far as I know, there is no problem.

sentences.japanese: ここに住んでいる限りは、町の規則を守らなければなりません。
sentences.english: As long as you live here, you must follow the town's rules.
sentences.nuanceNote: 限りは states the continuing condition under which the conclusion holds.

sentences.japanese: 私が聞いた限りでは、計画に変更はありません。
sentences.english: As far as I have heard, there is no change to the plan.
sentences.nuanceNote: 限りでは restricts the information supporting the claim, not the period during which a duty holds.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 34). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜のみならず (Not Only X, but Also Y - Formal & Broad)
meaning: Formal written equivalent of 〜だけでなく. Asserts that the scope of a phenomenon is not confined to X, but also encompasses Y.
connection: Noun + のみならず | 普通形 (な-adj + である, Noun + である) + のみならず
nuance: BROAD HORIZON: Emphasizes that an impact ripples far beyond the immediate subject: '国内のみならず、全世界で' (Not only domestically, but across the entire globe).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Noun / Clause + のみならず = 'Not only X, but also Y!'. Formal written prose.

sentences.japanese: このアニメは日本国内のみならず、欧米やアジアのファンにも熱狂的に愛されている。
sentences.english: This anime is passionately loved not only within Japan, but also by fans across Europe, America, and Asia.
sentences.literal: This anime Japan domestic not-only, West and Asia fans-by-also enthusiastically loved-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Describing global cultural resonance.

sentences.japanese: この研究は国内のみならず、海外でも注目されています。
sentences.english: This research is attracting attention not only domestically but overseas too.
sentences.nuanceNote: のみならず is a formal additive expression; も commonly marks the added scope.

sentences.japanese: 彼は知識が豊富であるのみならず、説明も上手です。
sentences.english: He is not only knowledgeable but also good at explaining.
sentences.nuanceNote: A formal predicate can precede のみならず; the second clause adds another quality.

quiz.question: 彼は英語（　　）ならず、中国語とスペイン語も極めて流暢に操る。
quiz.translation: Not only English, he also commands Chinese and Spanish with extreme fluency.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + のみならず (Expansive scope)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + のみならず | 普通形 (な-adj + である, Noun + である) + のみならず

explanations.reason: Correct! 英語のみならず forms the classical 'not only X, but Y as well' collocation.
Incorrect. 英語だけならず is ungrammatical (must be だけでなく).
Incorrect. 英語ばかりならず is invalid (must be ばかりでなく).
Incorrect. 英語ほどならず does not exist.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 30 (PDF p. 40). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ばかりか (Not Merely X, but Beyond That Even Y!)
meaning: Indicates that something does not stop at degree X, but extends unexpectedly to an even more astonishing, serious, or extreme degree Y.
connection: 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + である) + ばかりか (often paired with 〜さえ / 〜まで)
nuance: ESCALATION BEYOND EXPECTATION: Can be positive or negative, but conveys astonishment: '友達ばかりか、家族まで彼を疑った' (Not merely his friends, but even his own family doubted him).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: 普通形 + ばかりか... さえ = 'Not just X, but going so far as extreme Y!'.

sentences.japanese: 彼は約束の時間に遅刻したばかりか、謝罪の一言さえ口にしなかった。
sentences.english: He not only showed up late for the promised time, but he didn't even utter a single word of apology.
sentences.literal: He promised-time late-was not-merely, apology single-word even mouth-to not-did.
sentences.nuanceNote: Indignation at unrepentant bad manners.

sentences.japanese: この店は安いばかりか、配達まで無料です。
sentences.english: This shop is not only cheap; even delivery is free.
sentences.nuanceNote: ばかりか adds a further point, often stronger or more surprising than the first.

sentences.japanese: 彼は謝らないばかりか、私を責めました。
sentences.english: He not only failed to apologize; he blamed me.
sentences.nuanceNote: The added point can intensify an unfavorable evaluation.

quiz.question: 彼女は親切に道を教えてくれた（　　）か、目的地まで一緒に案内してくれた。
quiz.translation: Not only did she kindly give me directions, she even guided me all the way to my destination.
quiz.grammarFocus: 普通形 + ばかりか (Unexpected escalation)
quiz.ruleHint: 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + である) + ばかりか (often paired with 〜さえ / 〜まで)

explanations.reason: Correct! 教えてくれたばかりか expresses unexpected escalation of generosity.
Incorrect. 教えてくれただけか is a question ('only taught?').
Incorrect. 教えてくれたほどか is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 教えてくれたくらいか does not form this structure.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 30 (PDF p. 40). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に限らず・〜はもとより・〜上に
meaning: Not limited to; not only the obvious case; in addition.
connection: Nに限らず; Nはもとより; plain clause + 上に
nuance: に限らず extends the range. はもとより treats the first item as obvious. 上に adds another feature in the same evaluative direction; Nの/である、な-adjectiveな/である.
keyTakeaway: Nに限らず; Nはもとより; plain clause + 上に

sentences.japanese: この店は安い上に、駅にも近いです。
sentences.english: This shop is inexpensive and, in addition, close to the station.

sentences.japanese: この講座は学生に限らず、社会人も参加できます。
sentences.english: This course is open not only to students but also to working adults.
sentences.nuanceNote: に限らず expands the scope beyond the first group.

sentences.japanese: 日本語はもとより、英語でも説明できます。
sentences.english: They can explain in English as well as, of course, Japanese.
sentences.useLabel: The first point is taken for granted
sentences.nuanceNote: はもとより treats the first case as already expected and adds another.

sentences.japanese: この部屋は広い上に、駅にも近いです。
sentences.english: This room is spacious and is also near the station.
sentences.nuanceNote: 上に adds another circumstance supporting the same overall evaluation; it is not temporal 上で.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 30 (PDF p. 40). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜をめぐって / 〜をめぐる (Centering Around a Dispute, Controversy, or Conflict)
meaning: Indicates the contentious issue, disputed prize, or topic around which opposing parties argue, battle, or negotiate: 'Over / Regarding / Concerning [conflict]'.
connection: Noun + をめぐって (Adverbial) | Noun + をめぐる + Noun (Attributive)
nuance: をめぐって identifies an issue around which activity develops, often discussion, dispute or competition. It is not interchangeable with neutral について in every context, but it does not require hostile conflict.
keyTakeaway: をめぐって identifies an issue around which activity develops, often discussion, dispute or competition. It is not interchangeable with neutral について in every context, but it does not require hostile conflict.

sentences.japanese: 莫大な遺産の相続をめぐって、親族の間で激しい裁判闘争が続いている。
sentences.english: Centering around the inheritance of a vast fortune, a fierce legal battle continues among relatives.
sentences.literal: Vast estate inheritance over, relatives-between fierce court-battle continuing.
sentences.nuanceNote: Legal dispute centered on disputed wealth.

sentences.japanese: 新しい道路の建設をめぐって、住民の意見が分かれています。
sentences.english: Residents are divided over construction of the new road.
sentences.nuanceNote: をめぐって frames the issue around which debate or differing positions develop.

sentences.japanese: 土地の利用をめぐる話し合いが続いています。
sentences.english: Discussions over land use are continuing.
sentences.nuanceNote: をめぐる modifies the following noun; the pattern is not restricted to angry arguments.

quiz.question: 新空港の建設予定地を（　　）て、住民と行政の間で激しい議論が交わされた。
quiz.translation: Over the planned construction site of the new airport, fierce debates were exchanged between residents and the government.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + をめぐって contentious controversy
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + をめぐって (Adverbial) | Noun + をめぐる + Noun (Attributive)

explanations.reason: Correct! 予定地をめぐって captures the contentious conflict between citizens and government.
Incorrect. もとづいて means based on evidence.
Incorrect. こたえて means responding to expectations.
Incorrect. つうじて means through the medium of.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 34 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜にこたえて / 〜にこたえる (In Response to Expectations, Requests, or Demands)
meaning: Taking concrete action to meet, fulfill, or respond positively to expectations, public demands, cheer, or customer feedback.
connection: Noun + にこたえて (Adverbial) | Noun + にこたえる + Noun (Attributive)
nuance: FAVORABLE RESPONSE TO CHEERS / DEMANDS: Fixed pairings: 期待にこたえて (meeting expectations), 要望にこたえて (responding to requests), アンコールにこたえて (responding to encore).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [期待 / 要望 / 声援] にこたえて = Fulfilling expectations or demands!

sentences.japanese: お客様からの熱いご要望にこたえて、人気商品の再販売を決定いたしました。
sentences.english: In response to passionate requests from our customers, we have decided to resume sales of our popular item.
sentences.literal: Customers passionate requests in-response-to, popular-item re-sale decided.

tokens.reading: ごようぼうにこたえて

sentences.nuanceNote: Corporate commercial response to customer feedback.

sentences.japanese: 利用者の要望にこたえて、営業時間を延ばしました。
sentences.english: In response to users' requests, we extended the opening hours.
sentences.nuanceNote: にこたえて means acting to meet a request or expectation, not merely answering a question verbally.

sentences.japanese: 両親の期待にこたえられるよう、努力しています。
sentences.english: I am working hard so that I can live up to my parents' expectations.
sentences.nuanceNote: The potential form describes being able to meet the expectation.

quiz.question: ファンの温かい応援に（　　）て、選手は見事な逆転勝利を収めた。
quiz.translation: In response to the warm cheers of the fans, the athlete achieved a spectacular comeback victory.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + にこたえて responsive action
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + にこたえて (Adverbial) | Noun + にこたえる + Noun (Attributive)

explanations.reason: Correct! 応援にこたえて expresses rising to the occasion driven by fan support.
Incorrect. そって means following along rules.
Incorrect. めぐって means over a dispute.
Incorrect. たいして means toward an object or in contrast.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 34 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜にかけては (When It Comes to Skill / Domain: Unrivaled Superiority)
meaning: Be particularly good at something; as regards a particular skill or field.
connection: N + にかけては
nuance: Usually introduces a positive assessment of ability in a particular field. It often emphasizes confidence or comparative strength, but does not by itself prove that someone is the best in the world. Contrast neutral について, which simply marks a topic, and にとって, which marks an evaluating viewpoint.
keyTakeaway: Name a field, then evaluate strength in it.

sentences.japanese: 数学の難問を解くことにかけては、学年で彼の右に出る者はいない。
sentences.english: When it comes to solving difficult mathematics problems, there is nobody in the entire grade who can surpass him.
sentences.literal: Math difficult-problems solve domain-in, grade-in his right-side exceed person none.
sentences.nuanceNote: Supreme academic domain superiority.

sentences.japanese: 料理にかけては、姉のほうが得意です。
sentences.english: When it comes to cooking, my older sister is better at it.
sentences.nuanceNote: にかけては highlights a field of strength; it does not by itself mean best in the world.

sentences.japanese: 正確さにかけては、この方法が優れています。
sentences.english: In terms of accuracy, this method is superior.
sentences.nuanceNote: The following predicate evaluates a particular strength rather than just naming a neutral topic.

quiz.question: パソコンの修理（　　）かけては、社内で田中さんの知識が一番豊富です。
quiz.translation: When it comes to computer repair, Tanaka-san's knowledge is the most extensive in the company.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + にかけては specialized expertise
quiz.ruleHint: N + にかけては

explanations.reason: Correct! 修理にかけては specifies the specialized domain where Tanaka-san excels supreme.
Incorrect. をかけて means risking one's life (命をかけて).
Incorrect. へ is directional.
Incorrect. で is locational.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 34 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に関して / 〜に関する (Concerning / Pertaining To Formal Matters)
meaning: Formal, academic equivalent of 〜について. Pertaining to, dealing with, or relating to a broad thematic domain or investigation.
connection: Noun + に関して / に関しては | Noun + に関する + Noun
nuance: に関して / に関する is a relatively formal concerning or regarding. It does not necessarily promise broader coverage than について.
keyTakeaway: に関して / に関する is a relatively formal concerning or regarding. It does not necessarily promise broader coverage than について.

sentences.japanese: AIの倫理的な利用に関する国際シンポジウムが、来月東京で開催される。
sentences.english: An international symposium concerning the ethical utilization of AI will be held in Tokyo next month.
sentences.literal: AI ethical usage concerning international-symposium, next-month Tokyo-in held-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: High-level academic conference announcement.

sentences.japanese: 環境問題に関して、意見を交換しました。
sentences.english: We exchanged opinions concerning environmental issues.
sentences.nuanceNote: に関して is a relatively formal topic marker.

sentences.japanese: 奨学金に関する資料を読みました。
sentences.english: I read materials concerning scholarships.
sentences.nuanceNote: に関する is the noun-modifying form; に関して is not substituted directly before 資料.

quiz.question: 環境問題（　　）関する新しい法案が、国会で可決された。
quiz.translation: A new legislative bill concerning environmental issues was passed by the Diet.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + に関する + Noun (Thematic modifier)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + に関して / に関しては | Noun + に関する + Noun

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun + に関する is the standard adnominal modifier.
Incorrect. を関する is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. へ関する is invalid.
Incorrect. で関する does not exist.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 34 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に対して
meaning: Direct an action or attitude toward a target.
connection: Nに対して; Nに対するN
nuance: The contrast sense compares two items; the target sense identifies whom an action, response or attitude is directed toward. It is different from perspective にとって.
keyTakeaway: Nに対して; Nに対するN

sentences.japanese: 質問に対して、丁寧な回答をいただきました。
sentences.english: I received a careful answer to my question.

sentences.japanese: 政府に対して、不満を持つ人が増えています。
sentences.english: More people are dissatisfied with the government.
sentences.nuanceNote: に対して identifies the target of dissatisfaction.

sentences.japanese: 学生に対する説明が不足していました。
sentences.english: The explanation given to students was insufficient.
sentences.nuanceNote: に対する modifies 説明; preserve the target relationship when changing the grammatical form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 34 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に基づいて / 〜をもとに (Founded Upon / Grounded on Reliable Data)
meaning: に基づいて: based on a foundation or grounds. をもとに: using something as a basis or material.
connection: Nに基づいて / Nに基づくN; Nをもとに / NをもとにしたN
nuance: に基づいて presents the basis for a decision, action or account, often evidence, rules, experience or principles. It is not limited to laws/science and does not guarantee literal compliance with every detail. をもとに can introduce source material used to develop something, such as an account or design. The meanings overlap; creative freedom versus strict compliance is a useful tendency, not an absolute boundary.
keyTakeaway: 基づく emphasizes grounds; をもとに emphasizes a source/basis. Context determines the contrast.

sentences.japanese: 最新の科学的知見に基づいて、防災計画の抜本的な見直しが行われた。
sentences.english: A radical overhaul of the disaster prevention plan was carried out based upon the latest scientific insights.
sentences.literal: Latest scientific insights based-upon, disaster-prevention plan radical overhaul conducted.
sentences.nuanceNote: Policy revisions grounded on rigorous research.

sentences.japanese: 調査の結果に基づいて、計画を見直しました。
sentences.english: We revised the plan based on the survey results.
sentences.nuanceNote: に基づいて identifies the grounds for the revision.

sentences.japanese: この映画は実際の出来事をもとに作られました。
sentences.english: This film was made based on actual events.
sentences.nuanceNote: をもとに identifies source material; it does not guarantee that every detail is reproduced literally.

quiz.question: この小説は、歴史的な事実（　　）基づいて執筆された大作である。
quiz.translation: This novel is a monumental work authored based upon historical facts.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + に基づいて (Factual foundation)
quiz.ruleHint: Nに基づいて / Nに基づくN; Nをもとに / NをもとにしたN

explanations.reason: Correct! 事実に基づいて is the established formula for factual foundations.
Incorrect. 事実を基づいて is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 事実で基づいて is invalid.
Incorrect. 事実へ基づいて is meaningless.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 48). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に沿って / 〜に沿った (In Line With Guidelines / Aligning Faithfully)
meaning: Follow a route, plan, policy or guiding line.
connection: Nに沿って / Nに沿うN / Nに沿ったN
nuance: Can be physical (川に沿って歩く) or abstract (方針に沿って進める). It presents something as following a guiding line, not necessarily as following every detail with no deviation. Distinguish に基づいて, which identifies a basis or grounds.
keyTakeaway: 沿う = follow along; the guiding line can be physical or abstract.

sentences.japanese: 基本方針に沿って策定された計画に従い、着実に業務を推進してください。
sentences.english: Please steadily advance operations following the plan formulated in line with our fundamental policy.
sentences.literal: Basic-policy along formulated plan follow, steadily operations advance please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Managerial directive on operational fidelity.

sentences.japanese: 川に沿って、細い道が続いています。
sentences.english: A narrow road runs along the river.
sentences.nuanceNote: 沿う can describe following a physical line, not just an abstract policy.

sentences.japanese: 計画に沿って、作業を進めます。
sentences.english: We will proceed with the work according to the plan.
sentences.nuanceNote: に沿って presents the plan as a guiding line for the work.

quiz.question: お客様のご要望（　　）沿った最適なプランをご提案させていただきます。
quiz.translation: We will humbly propose the optimal plan strictly tailored in line with our customer's requests.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + に沿った + Noun (Faithful alignment)
quiz.ruleHint: Nに沿って / Nに沿うN / Nに沿ったN

explanations.reason: Correct! ご要望に沿った (in line with customer requests) is standard commercial Japanese.
Incorrect. ご要望を沿った is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. ご要望で沿った is invalid.
Incorrect. ご要望へ沿った does not exist.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 48). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜のもとで・〜のもとに
meaning: Under supervision or a stated condition/principle.
connection: Nのもとで / Nのもとに
nuance: のもとで often identifies a guiding person or environment. のもとに often frames conditions, agreements or principles. They overlap in some contexts.
keyTakeaway: Nのもとで / Nのもとに

sentences.japanese: 先生の指導のもとで、研究を進めています。
sentences.english: I am conducting research under my teacher's guidance.

sentences.japanese: 有名な先生のもとで、研究を続けました。
sentences.english: I continued my research under a well-known teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: のもとで identifies the guidance or environment under which an activity occurs.

sentences.japanese: 安全第一という方針のもとに、作業を進めます。
sentences.english: We will proceed under a policy of safety first.
sentences.nuanceNote: のもとに identifies the principle or condition governing the activity.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 48). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜向け
meaning: Designed or intended for a group.
connection: N向けのN; N向けに; N向けだ
nuance: Contrast 向き, which means suitable for. A beginner-oriented book is designed for beginners; suitability alone does not establish the intended audience.
keyTakeaway: N向けのN; N向けに; N向けだ

sentences.japanese: これは初心者向けの説明です。
sentences.english: This explanation is intended for beginners.

sentences.japanese: これは初心者向けの教科書です。
sentences.english: This is a textbook intended for beginners.
sentences.nuanceNote: 向け describes the target audience for which something is designed, not a guarantee that every beginner finds it suitable.

sentences.japanese: 外国人向けに、やさしい日本語で案内を書きました。
sentences.english: I wrote the information in simple Japanese for foreign readers.
sentences.nuanceNote: 向けに modifies the action; 向けの modifies a noun.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 38 (PDF p. 48). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜につれて / 〜にしたがって (As X Progresses, Y Proportionally Evolves)
meaning: As condition A naturally moves or progresses along a timeline or scale, condition B simultaneously evolves in step: 'As X changes, Y evolves alongside'.
connection: V-辞書形 (Change verb) + につれて | Noun (Change noun) + につれて
nuance: NATURAL DRIFT: Connects to verbs of ongoing spontaneous progression: 年を取るにつれて (As we grow older), 経済が発展するにつれて (As the economy develops).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Change Verb] につれて = In lockstep with the progress of X, Y evolves naturally!

sentences.japanese: 台風が北上して近づくにつれて、風と雨が次第に激しくなってきた。
sentences.english: As the typhoon moved north and approached, the wind and rain gradually became violent.
sentences.literal: Typhoon northward-moving approach as, wind and rain gradually violent became.
sentences.nuanceNote: Simultaneous escalation of storm intensity with geographical proximity.

sentences.japanese: 年を取るにつれて、考え方が変わりました。
sentences.english: My way of thinking changed as I grew older.
sentences.nuanceNote: につれて links a progression with another developing change.

sentences.japanese: 山を登るにしたがって、空気が冷たくなりました。
sentences.english: The air became colder as we climbed the mountain.
sentences.nuanceNote: にしたがって links the progressing climb to the changing temperature; it does not assert an exact mathematical rate.

quiz.question: 日本での生活が長く（　　）につれて、日本の文化を深く理解できるようになった。
quiz.translation: As my life in Japan became longer, I became able to deeply understand Japanese culture.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + につれて proportional evolution
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 (Change verb) + につれて | Noun (Change noun) + につれて
