sentences.english: The success was due to nothing other than everyone's cooperation.
sentences.nuanceNote: からにほかならない emphasizes the essential reason.

sentences.japanese: 電車がないので、歩くしかありません。
sentences.english: There is no train, so we have no choice but to walk.
sentences.nuanceNote: V dictionaryしかない states that no alternative remains in the situation.

sentences.japanese: 分からないことは、質問すべきです。
sentences.english: You should ask about what you do not understand.
sentences.nuanceNote: べき expresses what the speaker considers appropriate, not physical necessity.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 104 (PDF p. 114). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ことだ (Direct Practical Advice: You Should / Best Course Is To)
meaning: Offers direct, emphatic advice or an admonition to someone facing a dilemma: 'The best thing to do is / You should definitely...'.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-ない形 + ことだ
nuance: SENIOR-TO-JUNIOR ADMONITION: Given by an elder, coach, teacher, or friend who knows the correct solution: '日本語を上達させたければ、毎日声を出して読むことだ' (If you want to master Japanese, the thing to do is read aloud every day). Never use upwards to a boss.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-る / V-ない + ことだ = 'Here is the golden rule you should follow!'.

sentences.japanese: 健康を維持したいなら、暴飲暴食を慎み、規則正しい生活を送ることだ。
sentences.english: If you wish to maintain your health, the best thing to do is refrain from binge eating and drinking, and lead a regulated lifestyle.
sentences.literal: Health maintain want-if, binge-eating-drinking refrain, regulated life send thing-is.

tokens.meaning: the thing to do is to lead

sentences.nuanceNote: Sage wellness advice on lifestyle discipline.

sentences.japanese: 上達したければ、毎日少しずつ練習することです。
sentences.english: If you want to improve, you should practice a little every day.
sentences.nuanceNote: Sentence-final ことだ gives advice about what to do; it may sound authoritative.

sentences.japanese: 体を壊したくなければ、無理な残業はしないことです。
sentences.english: If you don't want to ruin your health, you shouldn't do unreasonable overtime.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-ない + ことだ provides direct, firm advice on what action to avoid.

quiz.question: 健康のためには、よく寝る（　　）だ。
quiz.translation: For your health, you should sleep well.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + ことだ (Practical wisdom advice)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない形 + ことだ

explanations.reason: V dictionary + ことだ gives advice.
ものに does not form this ending.
はずに does not form this ending.
ところに does not form this ending.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 108 (PDF p. 118). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜まい / 〜まいか (Resolute Negative Will / Negative Conjecture)
meaning: Negative intention (will not) or negative conjecture (probably will not).
connection: V dictionary + まい; ru-verbs also stem + まい; するまい / すまい / しまい; 来るまい / 来まい
nuance: This relatively formal form can state a decision not to do something or a belief that something will not occur. Determine the sense from the subject and context. A first-person agent often supports intention; it is not automatically a promise never to act again. ではあるまいか instead suggests a possibility: could it not be…?
keyTakeaway: まい is negative intention or conjecture; ではあるまいか is a different rhetorical pattern.

sentences.japanese: あんな不愉快な思いをするくらいなら、あの店には二度と行くまい。
sentences.english: If I have to endure such an unpleasant experience, I vow never to set foot in that shop ever again.
sentences.literal: That unpleasant experience suffer rather-than, that shop-to twice go-never-will.
sentences.nuanceNote: Steadfast personal vow after terrible customer service.

sentences.japanese: 同じ失敗は繰り返すまいと思いました。
sentences.english: I resolved not to repeat the same mistake.
sentences.nuanceNote: A first-person agent and intention context support the negative-will reading.

sentences.japanese: この時間では、もう誰も来るまい。
sentences.english: At this hour, probably nobody else will come.
sentences.nuanceNote: まい is a formal negative conjecture here, not the speaker deciding not to come.

quiz.question: 二度と失敗する（　　）と誓いました。
quiz.translation: I vowed never to fail again.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + まい (Steadfast negative determination)
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary + まい; ru-verbs also stem + まい; するまい / すまい / しまい; 来るまい / 来まい

explanations.reason: するまい expresses negative resolve.
するず is not a negative form.
するぬで is not the required construction.
するなく is not a negative form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 108 (PDF p. 118). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ようではないか・〜ことはない
meaning: Invite joint action; say there is no need.
connection: Volitional + ではないか; V dictionary + ことはない
nuance: ようではないか is a formal appeal to act together. ことはない often reassures someone that an action is unnecessary; distinguish experiential たことがない.
keyTakeaway: Volitional + ではないか; V dictionary + ことはない

sentences.japanese: 一緒に考えようではありませんか。急ぐことはありません。
sentences.english: Let us think about it together. There is no need to hurry.

sentences.japanese: もう一度、みんなで考えようではありませんか。
sentences.english: Let us all think about it once more.
sentences.nuanceNote: Volitional + ではないか makes a formal appeal to joint action.

sentences.japanese: そんなに心配することはありません。
sentences.english: There is no need to worry so much.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary verb + ことはない reassures that the action is unnecessary; it differs from experiential Vたことがない.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 108 (PDF p. 118). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: ものだ・ものではない・まい・ものか
meaning: Norms, prohibitions, negative intention and rejection.
connection: V dictionary/ない + ものだ; V dictionary + ものではない; V+まい; plain+ものか
nuance: ものだ can state a norm as well as a general truth or recollection. まい is a formal negative intention or conjecture. ものか emotionally rejects a possibility or intention.
keyTakeaway: V dictionary/ない + ものだ; V dictionary + ものではない; V+まい; plain+ものか

sentences.japanese: 人の失敗を笑うものではありません。
sentences.english: One should not laugh at other people's mistakes.

sentences.japanese: 人には親切にするものです。
sentences.english: One should be kind to others.
sentences.nuanceNote: ものだ presents a behavior as a general norm, not just a description of one person's action.

sentences.japanese: もう負けるまいと思った。こんなことで諦めるものか。
sentences.english: I resolved not to lose again. There is no way I will give up over this.
sentences.nuanceNote: まい states negative intention; ものか adds an emphatic emotional rejection.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 108 (PDF p. 118). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てはいられない / 〜てられない (Cannot Afford to Keep Doing / Compelled to Act)
meaning: Expresses that due to time pressure, changing circumstances, age, or emotional urgency, the speaker cannot remain in an ongoing state or continue an action: "Cannot afford to keep doing / Can't just sit around doing X".
connection: V-て + はいられない (Spoken: 〜てられない)
nuance: Indicates that one cannot afford to remain idle, passive, or continuing a casual behavior because circumstances require a shift or action. It can describe a pressing crisis (避難しなければ), but also ordinary life milestones (もう30歳だから親に甘えてばかりはいられない) or imminent deadlines (試験前だから遊んではいられない).
keyTakeaway: V-て + はいられない = Cannot afford to continue the current state or posture; circumstances compel a change or action.

sentences.japanese: 試験まであと一週間しかないのだから、遊んではいられない。
sentences.english: Since there is only one week left until the exam, I cannot afford to be playing around.
sentences.literal: Exam-until only 1-week have-not since, playing-around afford-cannot.

tokens.reading: あそんではいられない

sentences.nuanceNote: Urgent study pressure eliminating leisure.

sentences.japanese: もうすぐ試験が始まるから、いつまでものんびりしてはいられない。
sentences.english: The exam will begin soon, so I cannot afford to be idling around forever.
sentences.nuanceNote: Time pressure prevents continuing in a relaxed state.

sentences.japanese: 社会人になったのだから、親に甘えてばかりはいられない。
sentences.english: Now that I am a working adult, I can't keep depending on my parents.
sentences.nuanceNote: Growing up means one cannot continue childhood dependence.

quiz.question: こんな重大な危機に直面して、ただ黙って（　　）はいられない。
quiz.translation: Facing such a critical crisis, I cannot afford to just keep silent and do nothing.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + はいられない urgent compulsion
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + はいられない (Spoken: 〜てられない)

explanations.reason: Correct! 黙って見ている (silently watching) becomes 黙って見てはいられない ('cannot just look on').
Incorrect. 見はいられない is ungrammatical without て.
Incorrect. 見るはいられない is invalid.
Incorrect. 見た is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 112 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ずにいられない / 〜ないではいられない (Cannot Help But Do / Irresistible Urge)
meaning: An internal psychological urge or emotional impulse is so intensely overwhelming that the speaker is irresistibly compelled to do X: 'Cannot help but do / Cannot suppress doing'.
connection: V-ない form (drop ない) + ずにいられない (する irregular: せずにいられない) / ないではいられない
nuance: UNCONTROLLABLE EMOTIONAL IMPULSE: Laughing, crying, saying something, or helping: '彼の面白い顔を見たら、笑わずにはいられなかった' (Seeing his funny face, I couldn't help but burst into laughter).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ず + にはいられない = 'I simply couldn't stop myself from doing it!'. する becomes せず.

sentences.japanese: あまりの理不尽な対応に、一言抗議せずにはいられなかった。
sentences.english: Confronted with such an overly unreasonable response, I couldn't help but voice a word of protest.
sentences.literal: Overly unreasonable response-to, one-word protest without could-not-stay.

tokens.word: 抗議せずにはいられなかった
tokens.reading: こうぎせずにはいられなかった

sentences.nuanceNote: Irrepressible moral protest against injustice.

sentences.japanese: その話を聞くと、笑わずにはいられません。
sentences.english: When I hear that story, I cannot help laughing.
sentences.nuanceNote: The impulse makes suppressing the action difficult; it is not an external rule forcing it.

sentences.japanese: 困っている人を見ると、何かしないではいられません。
sentences.english: When I see someone in trouble, I cannot help doing something.
sentences.nuanceNote: ないではいられない is the ordinary negative-form alternative. The ず variant of する is せずにはいられない.

quiz.question: 悲しい結末の映画を見て、涙を（　　）ずにはいられなかった。
quiz.translation: Watching the movie with its tragic ending, I couldn't help but shed tears.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ず + にはいられない irresistible emotional impulse
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない form (drop ない) + ずにいられない (する irregular: せずにいられない) / ないではいられない

explanations.reason: Correct! 流す negative stem 流さ + ずにいられない forms 流さずにはいられなかった ('couldn't help shedding tears').
Incorrect. 流し is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 流す is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 流せ is imperative/potential stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 112 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ざるを得ない (Inevitably Compelled to Do Against One's Wish)
meaning: Indicates that despite personal reluctance or aversion, objective circumstances, rules, or harsh realities leave no alternative: 'Cannot help but / Am compelled to / Forced to...'.
connection: V-ない形 (drop ない) + ざるを得ない (する irregular: せざるを得ない)
nuance: UNWILLING RESIGNATION: You do not want to do it, but circumstances leave zero escape: 'これだけ証拠が揃っては、罪を認めざるを得ない' (Confronted with this much evidence, one cannot help but confess to the crime).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ない stem + ざるを得ない (する→せざるを得ない) = 'I really don't want to, but I have NO OTHER CHOICE!'.

sentences.japanese: 台風で全便が欠航となったため、旅行の予定を延期せざるを得なかった。
sentences.english: Because all flights were cancelled due to the typhoon, we had no choice but to postpone our travel schedule.
sentences.literal: Typhoon-by all-flights cancelled became because, travel-of schedule postpone compelled-was.

tokens.word: 延期せざるを得なかった
tokens.meaning: had no choice but to postpone
tokens.reading: えんきせざるをえなかった

sentences.nuanceNote: Reluctant acceptance of uncontrollable force majeure.

sentences.japanese: 台風のため、旅行を中止せざるを得ませんでした。
sentences.english: Because of the typhoon, we had no choice but to cancel the trip.
sentences.nuanceNote: する changes to せざる; the compulsion comes from circumstances rather than an irresistible emotion.

sentences.japanese: 費用が高すぎるので、計画を見直さざるを得ません。
sentences.english: The cost is too high, so we have no choice but to revise the plan.
sentences.nuanceNote: The expression presents a decision as unavoidable, often contrary to the preferred course.

quiz.question: 会社の業績が著しく悪化したため、不採算部門の閉鎖を決断（　　）ざるを得ない。
quiz.translation: Because the company's financial performance deteriorated drastically, management is compelled to decide on closing unprofitable divisions.
quiz.grammarFocus: する → せざるを得ない (Compelled reluctant action)
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない形 (drop ない) + ざるを得ない (する irregular: せざるを得ない)

explanations.reason: Correct! する becomes せざるを得ない (irregular suru conjugation).
Incorrect. しざるを得ない is a classic learner trap (ungrammatical!).
Incorrect. さざるを得ない does not exist.
Incorrect. すざるを得ない is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 112 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てたまらない / 〜てしかたがない (Intolerably / Irresistibly Overwhelming)
meaning: An internal psychological emotion, physical sensation, or urge is so powerful that the speaker cannot endure or suppress it: 'Dying to / Unbearably / Cannot help but feel'.
connection: V-て形 / い-adj-くて / な-adj-で + たまらない / しょうがない
nuance: INTOLERABLE INTENSITY: '会いたくてたまらない' (Dying to meet you), '寒くてたまらない' (Unbearably cold), '心配でたまらない' (Worried sick). First-person sensations.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: て-form + たまらない = 'Unbearably intense! I can't hold it back!'. (心配でたまらない = Worried sick).

sentences.japanese: 一人で海外に留学している娘の安否が、心配でたまらない。
sentences.english: I am worried sick about the safety and well-being of my daughter studying abroad all on her own.
sentences.literal: Alone overseas studying daughter-of safety, worried-sick intolerably.

tokens.reading: しんぱいでたまらない

sentences.nuanceNote: Parental visceral concern for a distant child.

sentences.japanese: 暑くてたまりません。
sentences.english: It is unbearably hot.
sentences.nuanceNote: い-adjectiveくて attaches before たまらない to express an intense sensation.

sentences.japanese: 旅行が楽しみでしかたがありません。
sentences.english: I am tremendously excited about the trip.
sentences.nuanceNote: な-adjectiveで precedes the expression; strong intensity need not be negative or painful.

quiz.question: 徹夜でレポートを書き上げて、今は眠くて（　　）。
quiz.translation: Having finished writing the report overnight without sleep, I am dying of sleepiness right now.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adj-くて + たまらない (Unbearable physical state)
quiz.ruleHint: V-て形 / い-adj-くて / な-adj-で + たまらない / しょうがない

explanations.reason: Correct! 眠くてたまらない expresses visceral, unbearable physiological fatigue.
Incorrect. 眠くてならない is unnatural (ならない is for spontaneous mental states like 思えてならない).
Incorrect. 眠くていられない is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 眠くてやまない is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 112 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てならない・〜ないわけにはいかない
meaning: An involuntary feeling; an unavoidable obligation.
connection: Vて/adjくて/な-adjectiveで + ならない; Vない + わけにはいかない
nuance: てならない often conveys a spontaneously arising emotion or conviction. The double negative expresses that not doing the action is unacceptable.
keyTakeaway: Vて/adjくて/な-adjectiveで + ならない; Vない + わけにはいかない

sentences.japanese: 結果が気になってなりません。約束したので行かないわけにはいきません。
sentences.english: I cannot stop thinking about the result. Since I promised, I have to go.

sentences.japanese: 家族のことが心配でなりません。
sentences.english: I cannot stop worrying about my family.
sentences.nuanceNote: て/でならない commonly expresses a feeling or thought arising insistently, rather than an external prohibition.

sentences.japanese: 約束したので、行かないわけにはいきません。
sentences.english: Since I promised, I have to go.
sentences.nuanceNote: The double negative says that refraining from the action is unacceptable; it does not mean I cannot go.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 112 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜たいものだ・〜ないものか
meaning: A strong wish, often not easily achieved.
connection: Vたい / Vてほしい + ものだ; Vない + ものか/ものだろうか
nuance: たいものだ can express a longstanding wish. ないものか searches for a way to realize something difficult; it is not a normal negative factual question.
keyTakeaway: Vたい / Vてほしい + ものだ; Vない + ものか/ものだろうか

sentences.japanese: いつか世界を旅したいものです。もっと安くできないものでしょうか。
sentences.english: I would love to travel the world someday. Could there be a way to make this cheaper?

sentences.japanese: いつかこの町に住んでみたいものです。
sentences.english: I would love to live in this town someday.
sentences.nuanceNote: たいものだ adds a reflective or strong wish, rather than merely announcing an immediate plan.

sentences.japanese: もう少し静かにしてほしいものです。
sentences.english: I really wish they would be a little quieter.
sentences.nuanceNote: てほしいものだ expresses a strong wish about another person's behavior and can sound critical.

sentences.japanese: もっと簡単にできないものでしょうか。
sentences.english: Could there be a simpler way to do it?
sentences.useLabel: Search for a way to achieve a wish
sentences.nuanceNote: ないものか searches for a hoped-for possibility; it is not an ordinary factual negative question.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 116 (PDF p. 126). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: ものだ・ものがある・ことだ・ことか
meaning: Recollection, an affecting quality and exclamation.
connection: Vたものだ; plain + ものがある; adjective + ことだ; どれほど…ことか
nuance: たものだ recalls a repeated past experience. ものがある says something has a quality that affects the observer. Exclamatory ことだ differs from the advice pattern Vことだ.
keyTakeaway: Vたものだ; plain + ものがある; adjective + ことだ; どれほど…ことか

sentences.japanese: この話には考えさせられるものがあります。
sentences.english: There is something thought-provoking about this story.

sentences.japanese: 学生のころは、よく夜遅くまで話したものです。
sentences.english: When we were students, we often talked until late at night.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたものだ recalls a repeated past experience.

sentences.japanese: 彼女の話には、人を元気にするものがあります。
sentences.english: There is something in her story that cheers people up.
sentences.nuanceNote: ものがある identifies a quality that makes an impression; it does not refer to a concrete object hidden in the story.

sentences.japanese: あのとき、どれほど心配したことか。
sentences.english: How worried I was at that time!
sentences.nuanceNote: ことか is exclamatory after a degree expression, not a request for a numerical answer.

sentences.japanese: 遠いところをわざわざお越しいただき、本当にありがたいことです。
sentences.english: To have you come all this way from afar, how truly thankful I am!
sentences.nuanceNote: Adjective + ことだ expresses deep, sincere personal emotion or exclamation, distinct from the practical advice pattern V-ことだ.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 116 (PDF p. 126). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜において・〜に先立って
meaning: A formal setting or an action before a significant event.
connection: Nにおいて / におけるN; N/V dictionary + に先立って
nuance: において is formal place, time or domain. に先立って puts preparations before an event. The source verb can help recall the meaning.
keyTakeaway: Nにおいて / におけるN; N/V dictionary + に先立って

sentences.japanese: 会議に先立って、資料を配ります。
sentences.english: We will distribute the materials before the meeting.

sentences.japanese: 現代社会において、情報セキュリティの確保は極めて重要である。
sentences.english: In modern society, ensuring information security is extremely important.
sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + において marks formal sphere, domain, or era.

sentences.japanese: 国際会議における合意に基づき、新たな規制が導入された。
sentences.english: Based on the agreement at the international conference, new regulations were introduced.
sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + における + Noun acts as an attributive modifier for formal location or occasion.

sentences.japanese: 新工場の稼働に先立ち、近隣住民への説明会を開いた。
sentences.english: Prior to commencing operations at the new factory, an explanatory meeting for local residents was held.
sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + に先立ち / に先立って describes deliberate preparatory actions before a major milestone.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 122 (PDF p. 132). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N2: Inception & Turning Point Matrix (p. 122)
table.subtitle: に際して vs にあたって vs に先立って vs を契機に / を機に

rows.label: 〜に際して (Momentous Occasion)
cells: Formal written / public announcements.
On the occasion of / When embarking upon: used for special, momentous, non-routine events.
動詞辞書形 / 名詞 + に際して
新しいプロジェクトの開始に際して、チーム全員に注意事項が伝えられた。
rows.note: Formal announcement for special occasions.

rows.label: 〜にあたって (Forward-Looking Juncture)
cells: Formal speeches, ceremonies, welcoming addresses.
At this crucial juncture of starting / As we embark upon: forward-looking positive resolve.
動詞辞書形 / 名詞 + にあたって
新生活を始めるにあたって、目標を明確に定めた。
rows.note: Clause B always contains positive resolve, preparation, or greetings.

rows.label: 〜に先立って (Preparatory Action)
cells: Formal business, research, public events.
In advance of / Prior to embarking on: Action A is a prerequisite step carried out before B.
名詞 / 動詞辞書形 + に先立って (修飾: 〜に先立つN)
映画の一般公開に先立って、関係者向けの特別試写会が行われた。
rows.note: Deliberate prerequisite step prior to main event.

rows.label: 〜を契機に / 〜を機に (Catalyst for Transformation)
cells: Written narrative, expository analysis, historical reflection.
Triggered by / Taking X as the decisive catalyst for permanent transformation.
名詞 + を契機に / を機に
大病を患ったことを契機に、健康的な生活習慣を徹底するようになった。
rows.note: X serves as a historic milestone initiating lasting change.

title: 〜とはいいながら・〜からすると
meaning: Concession; judging from a standpoint.
connection: Plain/N + とはいいながら; Nからすると / からいうと
nuance: とはいいながら acknowledges a label but qualifies the reality. からすると identifies the basis for a judgment or the viewpoint being adopted.
keyTakeaway: Plain/N + とはいいながら; Nからすると / からいうと

sentences.japanese: 値段からすると、十分によい品です。
sentences.english: Judging from the price, it is a perfectly good product.

sentences.japanese: まだ春浅いとはいいながら、日差しには温もりが感じられる。
sentences.english: Although it is still early spring, warmth can be felt in the sunlight.
sentences.nuanceNote: とはいいながら concedes a named condition while qualifying what actually holds.

sentences.japanese: 実用性の面からいうと、こちらのデザインのほうが優れている。
sentences.english: From the standpoint of practicality, this design is superior.
sentences.nuanceNote: からいうと / からすると specifies the criterion or perspective adopted for evaluation.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 124 (PDF p. 134). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N2: Evidential Evaluation from Nouns Matrix (p. 124)
table.subtitle: からすると vs から見ると vs からいえば vs からして

rows.label: 〜からすると / からすれば
cells: Inferred from outward signs, symptoms, or standing in someone else's shoes.
Judging by the evidence ('Judging by the footsteps, father is home') or from someone's feelings.
足音からすると、父が帰ってきたようだ。 / 親からすれば、子供は何歳になっても心配だ。
Forms deductions from sensory clues or empathetic perspective.
rows.note: Evaluation based on clues or someone's perspective.

rows.label: 〜から見ると / から見れば
cells: Evaluating external appearance, architectural design, or external third-party viewpoint.
Viewed from the perspective of an external observer.
外国人旅行者から見ると、日本の治安の良さは驚嘆に値するだろう。
Used when evaluating how something appears to an observer.
rows.note: Third-party observation angle.

rows.label: 〜からいえば / からいって
cells: Evaluating from one specific isolated dimension (quality, cost, skill, legal terms).
Speaking strictly in terms of dimension X...
味からいえば文句なしの名店だが、値段からいえば庶民的とは言えない。
Limits evaluation strictly to the specified criterion.
rows.note: Speaking strictly from one specific criterion.

rows.label: 〜からして
cells: Singling out one prominent representative clue to prove the whole condition is true.
Judging even from this one single extreme detail, you can easily tell the rest...
あの店は看板からして怪しい。 / タイトルからして難解そうな論文だ。
Picks one extreme sample to deduce the nature of the whole entity.
rows.note: One prominent clue indicates the whole nature.

title: 古い形：ず・ざる・べし・まい・つつ・せよ（古典文法の残存形式）
meaning: Systematic review of classical grammatical forms surviving in modern Japanese: negative ず/ざる, obligation べし (べき), negative intention/conjecture まい/ではあるまいか, simultaneous/progressive/concessive つつ/つつある/つつも, and conditional/imperative せよ (にせよ).
connection: V-未然形 + ず/ざる; V-dict + べき/べからず; V-dict + まい / ではあるまいか; V-stem + つつ/つつある/つつも; N/Plain + にせよ
nuance: SKM N2 p. 126 Form Review C systematically contrasts classical forms across modern grammar: (1) ず/ざる: archaic negative marker surviving in ずじまいだ (Ch. 20), ずにはいられない (Ch. 25), ざるを得ない (Ch. 25), にもかかわらず (Ch. 14), を問わず (Ch. 11), and simple negative connector ずに. (2) べし: classical modal surviving as べきだ / べきではない (Ch. 23) expressing natural obligation or moral duty. (3) まい: classical negative auxiliary expressing negative determination ('will not') and negative conjecture ('probably will not'), as well as rhetorical conjecture ではあるまいか. (4) つつ: classical continuative auxiliary expressing simultaneous action equivalent to ながら, progressive change with つつある ('in the process of changing'), and concessive contrast with つつも ('although/while'). (5) せよ: classical imperative of する surviving in concessive conditions such as にせよ / にせよ〜にせよ ('even granting / regardless of whether').
keyTakeaway: V-未然形 + ず/ざる; V-dict + べき/べからず; V-dict + まい / ではあるまいか; V-stem + つつ/つつある/つつも; N/Plain + にせよ

sentences.japanese: 確認せずに送ることはできません。
sentences.english: I cannot send it without checking.

sentences.japanese: これだけの動かぬ証拠を突きつけられては、自らの過ちを認めざるを得ない。
sentences.english: Confronted with this much irrefutable evidence, I have no choice but to admit my own mistake.
sentences.useLabel: Archaic negative in fixed idiom (ざる)
sentences.nuanceNote: ざる survives in modern Japanese within the fixed modal construction ざるを得ない ('cannot avoid doing / compelled to do').

sentences.japanese: 二度とあのような浅はかで愚かな過ちは繰り返すまいと、心に固く誓った。
sentences.english: I firmly vowed in my heart never again to repeat such a shallow and foolish mistake.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-辞書形 + まい expresses the speaker's firm negative intention or determination ('will definitely not do').

sentences.japanese: 西の空の雲行きから判断すると、今夜は雨が降るまい。
sentences.english: Judging from the clouds in the western sky, it probably will not rain tonight.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-辞書形 + まい expresses the speaker's negative conjecture or strong deduction ('probably will not happen').

sentences.japanese: 現状のまま問題を先送りにすれば、事態はさらに深刻化するのではあるまいか。
sentences.english: If we simply postpone the problem as things currently stand, won't the situation become even more critical?
sentences.useLabel: Negative rhetorical conjecture with ではあるまいか
sentences.nuanceNote: ではあるまいか functions as a formal rhetorical question expressing tentative opinion or cautious conjecture.

sentences.japanese: 最新の配布資料に素早く目を通しつつ、会議の開始を待った。
sentences.english: While quickly looking through the newly distributed handouts, I waited for the meeting to begin.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + つつ expresses formal simultaneous action in written and professional contexts equivalent to ながら.

sentences.japanese: 先端医療技術の長年の研究により、難病の治癒率は年々着実に向上しつつある。
sentences.english: Through years of research in advanced medical technology, the cure rate for intractable diseases is steadily improving year by year.
sentences.useLabel: Progressive developing change with つつある
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + つつある expresses an ongoing, developing change or transition currently in progress.

sentences.japanese: 将来の進路について深く悩みつつも、毎日の勉強と研究を地道に続けている。
sentences.english: While agonizing deeply over my future path, I steadily continue my daily studies and research.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + つつも sets up an ongoing concessive tension ('although / even while recognizing...').

sentences.japanese: どのような個人的な理由があるにせよ、事前の連絡なき無断欠席は決して認められない。
sentences.english: Whatever personal reasons one might have, unannounced absence without prior notice is strictly unacceptable.
sentences.useLabel: Concessive condition with せよ (にせよ)
sentences.nuanceNote: にせよ derives from classical imperative せよ and establishes a concessive condition ('even granting / regardless of').

sentences.japanese: 市民の安全を守るため、行政として今できる限りの防災対策を講じるべきだ。
sentences.english: In order to protect citizen safety, the municipal government ought to implement every possible disaster prevention measure right now.
sentences.useLabel: Formal obligation and duty with べき (べし)
sentences.nuanceNote: べき derives from classical べし and expresses moral duty, natural obligation, or logical necessity.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 126 (PDF p. 136). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N2: Classical Remnants & Archaic Literary Forms (p. 126)
table.subtitle: Classical grammar surviving in formal written Japanese and idioms.

rows.label: Classical Negation: ず / ざる
cells: V-未然形 + ず (せず) / ざる + N
〜ないで / 〜ない (修飾: 〜ないN)
ず: adverbial negative ("without doing"). ざる: noun-attributive negative ("that does not..."). Examples: 絶えず (constantly), 意図せざる結果 (unintended consequence), 知らざる一面 (unknown side).
rows.note: Special: する becomes せず (adverbial) / せざる (attributive).

rows.label: Classical Obligation: べし / べく
cells: V-辞書形 + べし / べき / べく
〜なければならない / 〜する目的で
べし: natural solemn duty or inevitable consequence. べき: moral obligation ("ought to"). べく: formal in-order-to purpose marker (成功すべく努力する).
rows.note: Common phrase: あるべからざる (that should never exist).

rows.label: Classical Negative Conjecture: まい
cells: V-辞書形 (一段: 辞書/未然) + まい
〜ないだろう / 絶対〜しない
1. Negative conjecture: "surely will not" (今夜は雨が降るまい). 2. Strong negative resolve: "will never do again" (二度と行くまい). 3. Rhetorical: ではあるまいか (is it not perhaps...?).
rows.note: Group 2 / Irregular: するまい/すまい, くるまい/こまい.

rows.label: Classical Simultaneous & Progress: つつ
cells: V-stem + つつ / つつある
〜ながら / 〜ている (進行中)
1. つつ: concurrent contrastive action ("while knowing full well...": 悪いと知りつつ). 2. つつある: ongoing progressive change ("is steadily in the process of...": 事態は悪化しつつある).
rows.note: つつある only pairs with verbs of continuous change (発展, 増加, 回復).

rows.label: Classical Imperative: よ / せよ
cells: V-未然/連用 + せよ / れよ
〜しなさい / 〜しろ
Written imperative used in exam instructions, technical documents, and public slogans. Examples: 次の問に答えよ (Answer the following question), 行動せよ (Take action).
rows.note: する becomes せよ; 来る becomes 来い (こい) / 来たれ.

title: 〜ことなく・〜ことに・〜ことは〜が
meaning: Without doing; emotional comment; qualified admission.
connection: V dictionary + ことなく; emotion adjective/Vた + ことに; repeated predicate + ことは…が
nuance: ことなく is relatively formal without. 残念なことに introduces the speaker's evaluation. ことは…が concedes the first clause before a reservation.
keyTakeaway: V dictionary + ことなく; emotion adjective/Vた + ことに; repeated predicate + ことは…が

sentences.japanese: 残念なことに、彼とは話すことなく別れました。
sentences.english: Unfortunately, we parted without speaking.

sentences.japanese: この本は読んだことは読んだが、内容があまり理解できなかった。
sentences.english: I did indeed read this book, but I could not understand much of the content.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-たことはV-たが concedes the action occurred before stating a reservation.

sentences.japanese: 嬉しいことに、第一志望の大学から合格通知が届いた。
sentences.english: Delightfully, an acceptance letter arrived from my top-choice university.
sentences.nuanceNote: Adjective/V-た + ことに introduces the speaker's emotional reaction to the reported fact.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 128 (PDF p. 138). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N2: The Advanced こと Constructions Matrix (p. 128)
table.subtitle: ことなく vs ことに(は) vs ことは〜が vs ということだ

rows.label: 〜ことなく (Formal Continuous Negative)
cells: Formal written negative: 'Without doing X even once / Without ceasing'.
動詞辞書形 + ことなく
彼は困難に直面しても、一度も弱音を吐くことなく前進を続けた。
High formal equivalent of 〜ないで; elevated literary and essay register.
rows.note: Formal without doing even once.

rows.label: 〜ことに(は) (Speaker's Emotional Preamble)
cells: Speaker's emotional preamble: 'To my great emotion / What is remarkable is that...'.
感情形容詞 / 動詞た形 + ことに
嬉しいことに、全員が無事に試験に合格した。 / 残念なことに、旅行は雨で中止になった。
Fronts the speaker's emotional reaction before stating the factual event.
rows.note: Emotional preamble before reporting facts.

rows.label: 〜ことは〜が (Concessive Qualification)
cells: Concessive qualification: 'It is true that X, but nevertheless Y'.
動詞辞書形 + ことは + 同動詞 + が / 形容詞 + ことは + 形容詞 + が
読めることは読めるが、専門用語が多すぎて意味は分からない。
Concedes truth of point A before introducing reservations in B.
rows.note: Concedes the first point before qualifying.

rows.label: 〜ということだ / 〜とのことだ (Authoritative Hearsay)
cells: Official hearsay quotation ('Reportedly / According to statements'), or summarizing explanation.
普通形 + ということだ / とのことだ
気象庁の発表によると、台風は今夜上陸する見込みだとのことだ。
Frequently paired with information sources (〜によると, 〜の話では).
rows.note: High formal hearsay reporting.

title: 〜ということだ・〜とのことだ
meaning: Relay a message or draw an interpretation.
connection: Plain clause + ということだ / とのことだ
nuance: とのことだ commonly relays information. ということだ can also summarize what a situation means. Identify the function from context.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + ということだ / とのことだ

sentences.japanese: 担当者は明日戻るとのことです。
sentences.english: I was told the person in charge returns tomorrow.

sentences.japanese: 連絡がないということは、今回の交渉は不成立に終わったということだ。
sentences.english: The fact that there is no contact means that this negotiation ended without an agreement.
sentences.nuanceNote: AということはBということだ draws a logical interpretation of what a situation signifies.

sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、午後から沿岸部で強い雨が降るということです。
sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, heavy rain will reportedly fall in coastal areas from this afternoon.
sentences.useLabel: Formal relay of news or reports
sentences.nuanceNote: Clause + ということです formally relays reported information or official forecasts.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 128 (PDF p. 138). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: わけだ・ところから・ことから
meaning: A logical explanation or evidence for a conclusion.
connection: Plain clause + わけだ / ところから / ことから
nuance: わけだ presents a conclusion as understandable. ところから and ことから connect an observed fact to a judgment or origin. They are not physical place markers in this use.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + わけだ / ところから / ことから

sentences.japanese: 声が似ていることから、兄弟だと思いました。
sentences.english: Because their voices were similar, I thought they were brothers.

sentences.japanese: 夜通し起きて作業をしていたのか。道理で眠そうな顔をしているわけだ。
sentences.english: You were up working all night? No wonder you look so sleepy.
sentences.nuanceNote: わけだ concludes that an observed state is entirely natural given the discovered explanation.

sentences.japanese: 富士山がよく見えるところから、この坂は「富士見坂」と名付けられた。
sentences.english: Because Mount Fuji is clearly visible from here, this slope was named Fujimizaka.
sentences.useLabel: Origin of a name or judgment
sentences.nuanceNote: ところから identifies an observable physical origin or trigger for a name.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 132 (PDF p. 142). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜だの〜だの・〜のみ
meaning: List examples informally; restrict formally.
connection: N/plain form + だの; N + のみ
nuance: だの often lists complaints or a mixed set of examples. のみ means only in a relatively formal/written register. It is not the same as the additive のみならず.
keyTakeaway: N/plain form + だの; N + のみ

sentences.japanese: 参加できるのは予約した方のみです。
sentences.english: Only people with reservations may participate.

sentences.japanese: 彼は忙しいだの疲れただのと文句ばかり言って、少しも手伝おうとしない。
sentences.english: He keeps complaining that he is busy or tired, and makes no effort to help.
sentences.nuanceNote: AだのBだの lists examples with an informal, often critical tone.

sentences.japanese: 当施設の利用は登録会員のみに限定されており、一般の入場はできません。
sentences.english: Use of this facility is strictly limited to registered members only; general admission is not permitted.
sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + のみ formally restricts scope to 'only' without additive nuance.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 134 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文末制約・人称・評価
meaning: Check how a grammar form constrains the rest of a sentence.
connection: Check intention, speaker viewpoint and positive/negative evaluation
nuance: 次第 often pairs with a planned action. たとたん typically reports an unexpected event. Personal feelings and observed feelings require different framing. These are construction-specific tendencies; avoid applying a single rule to every meaning of a form.
keyTakeaway: Check intention, speaker viewpoint and positive/negative evaluation

sentences.japanese: 準備ができ次第、出発しましょう。
sentences.english: Let us leave as soon as the preparations are complete.

sentences.japanese: 疲れてベッドに横になったとたんに、あっという間に眠りに落ちた。
sentences.english: The moment I lay down on the bed from exhaustion, I fell fast asleep in an instant.
sentences.nuanceNote: たとたん typically pairs with an immediate, non-volitional event in clause two.

sentences.japanese: 一人で遠い国に暮らしていると、家族の声が無性に聞きたくてたまらない。
sentences.english: Living alone in a distant country, I am dying to hear my family's voices.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜てたまらない expresses uncontrollable first-person sensations or desires.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 146). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N2: Sentence-Ending Constraints & Epistemic Stance Matrix (p. 136)
table.subtitle: Moral obligation vs strong negative resolve vs conviction vs speaker evaluation.

rows.label: 〜べきだ / べきではない
cells: General moral duty or common-sense obligation ('Ought to do / Should not do').
動詞辞書形 + べき (する → すべき / するべき)
人から親切にされたら、感謝の気持ちを伝えるべきだ。
Expresses universal social ethics, NOT arbitrary personal orders to a superior.
rows.note: Universal moral obligation.

rows.label: 〜まい (Negative Resolve / Conjecture)
cells: 1. Strong negative resolve ('Will never do again') 2. Negative conjecture ('Surely will not').
動詞辞書形 (一段: 辞書/未然) + まい (する → するまい/すまい)
二度とあのような愚かな過ちは繰り返すまいと誓った。
First-person for resolve; third-person takes 〜まいと思っている.
rows.note: Resolute refusal or negative conjecture.

rows.label: 〜に相違ない (にそういない)
cells: High certainty conviction based on authoritative evidence ('There is no doubt that...').
普通形 (な-adj である, 名詞である) + に相違ない
確固たる証拠が見つかった以上、犯人は彼であることに相違ない。
Formal written equivalent of に違いない; based on logical deduction.
rows.note: Authoritative conviction based on evidence.

rows.label: 〜にすぎない
cells: Limiting minimization ('Merely / Nothing more than / Just').
普通形 / 名詞 + にすぎない
私は会社の方針に従って業務を遂行したにすぎません。
Speaker deliberately downsizes the status, scale, or praise of X.
rows.note: Downsizes importance or scale.

rows.label: 〜にほかならない
cells: Definitive sole reason or essence ('Nothing other than / Precisely because').
名詞 + にほかならない
彼が難関試験に合格できたのは、日々の地道な努力の結果にほかならない。
Eliminates all other alternative causes; identifies the absolute core truth.
rows.note: Asserts the singular core reason.

rows.label: 〜かねない vs 〜かねる
cells: かねない: Negative danger ('Could happen / Risk of...'). かねる: Polite refusal ('Unable to do').
動詞ます語幹 + かねない / かねる
過度の過労は重大な病気を引き起こしかねない。 / そのご依頼には応じかねます。
かねない warns of dangerous consequences; かねる is formal customer-facing refusal.
rows.note: Danger warning vs polite refusal.

title: 〜っこない (No Way in Hell / Absolutely Out of the Question)
meaning: Emphatically denies any possibility of an action happening: 'There is absolutely no way / Impossible for someone to...'.
connection: V-stem (masu-stem) + っこない
nuance: CONVERSATIONAL CATEGORICAL REJECTION: Used in passionate speech to dismiss an absurd premise: 'こんな分厚い本、一日で読めっこないよ' (There is no way in hell anyone could read such a thick book in one day!).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Verb-stem + っこない = 'ZERO CHANCE! Categorically impossible!'.

sentences.japanese: プロの選手相手に、初心者の私たちが勝ちっこないよ。
sentences.english: There's no way in hell we beginners could ever defeat professional athletes!
sentences.literal: Pro athletes opponent-as, beginner us win-no-way.
sentences.nuanceNote: Blunt colloquial dismissal of an unrealistic match outcome.

sentences.japanese: あんなに頑固な部長が、私たちの要求を簡単に受け入れっこないよ。
sentences.english: There is no way in hell such a stubborn manager would easily accept our demands.
sentences.nuanceNote: Colloquial categorical rejection of an improbable premise.

sentences.japanese: たった二日間でこの分厚い報告書を全部翻訳できっこない。
sentences.english: There is no way anyone could translate this entire thick report in just two days.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb-stem + っこない emphasizes absolute practical impossibility.

quiz.question: 地図も持たずに初めての山に入ったら、道に迷い（　　）よ。
quiz.translation: If you enter an unfamiliar mountain without even a map, you are bound to get lost!
quiz.grammarFocus: Trap Check: っこない (Zero chance) vs かねない (Danger of happening)
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (masu-stem) + っこない

explanations.reason: Incorrect. 迷いっこない would mean 'there is no way you could get lost', which is false.
Correct! 迷いかねない warns of the very real danger: 'you are liable to get lost'. Note: For っこない, a sentence would be: 道が分かりっこない (No way you could know the path!).
Incorrect. きりない does not attach to verb stems.
Incorrect. がちない is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 140 (PDF p. 150). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文の組み立て：決まった形
meaning: Resolve the complete sentence, not only the starred slot.
connection: Pair fixed forms, then identify the main predicate
nuance: First link forms that constrain one another, such as ないことには…ない. Check how each chunk attaches on both sides. A locally plausible pair can still fail in the complete sentence.
keyTakeaway: Pair fixed forms, then identify the main predicate

sentences.japanese: 実際に使ってみないことには、便利かどうか分かりません。
sentences.english: Unless I actually try using it, I cannot tell whether it is useful.

sentences.japanese: 必要な書類を揃えないことには、申請を受け付けることはできません。
sentences.english: Unless you gather all the required documents, we cannot accept your application.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜ないことには pairs with a negative result clause 〜ない.

sentences.japanese: 今夜から明日の明け方にかけて、激しい雷雨になる見込みです。
sentences.english: From tonight through tomorrow dawn, severe thunderstorms are expected.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜から〜にかけて pairs starting boundary and ending approximate horizon.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 140 (PDF p. 150). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文の組み立て：名詞を説明する形式
meaning: Distinguish adverbial and noun-modifying forms.
connection: に関して→に関するN; に応じて→に応じたN; をめぐって→をめぐるN
nuance: A following noun may require an attributive form. Locate the noun being modified before arranging surrounding phrases.
keyTakeaway: に関して→に関するN; に応じて→に応じたN; をめぐって→をめぐるN

sentences.japanese: 経験に応じた仕事を選びます。
sentences.english: I will choose work suited to my experience.

sentences.japanese: 国民の信頼に応える政治を行うことが、今最も求められている。
sentences.english: Conducting politics that responds to the trust of the citizens is what is most demanded now.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜に応える directly modifies the abstract noun 政治 within the subject clause.

sentences.japanese: 環境問題に関する国際的な関心は、年々高まりを見せている。
sentences.english: International interest concerning environmental issues is showing an increase year by year.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜に関する attaches to Noun to modify the following noun phrase 関心.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 142 (PDF p. 152). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文の組み立て：「ない」の範囲
meaning: Track the scope of negation.
connection: わけがない / わけではない / わけにはいかない
nuance: These look similar but deny different things: possibility, a conclusion, or permission/acceptability. A second negative can reverse the apparent meaning.
keyTakeaway: わけがない / わけではない / わけにはいかない

sentences.japanese: 全部分からないわけではありません。
sentences.english: It is not that I understand none of it.

sentences.japanese: この提案に賛成できないわけではないが、予算の配分には再考の余地がある。
sentences.english: It is not that I cannot agree to this proposal, but there is room to reconsider the budget allocation.
sentences.nuanceNote: わけではない restricts negation so that the proposition is not categorically denied.

sentences.japanese: 彼ほどの能力があれば、この難問を解決できないこともないだろう。
sentences.english: With abilities like his, it is not impossible that he could solve this difficult problem.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜ないこともない uses double negation to assert a modest possibility.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 146 (PDF p. 156). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N2: Double Negatives & Compelled Action Matrix (p. 146)
table.subtitle: ないではいられない vs ずにはいられない vs なくはない vs ないわけにはいかない

rows.label: 〜ないではいられない / 〜ずにはいられない
cells: Irrepressible emotional urge: cannot help but feel / compelled to do by internal urge.
動詞ない形 + ではいられない / 動詞未然形 + ずにはいられない (する → せずにはいられない)
悲惨な事故のニュースを聞いて、涙を流さずにはいられなかった。
Driven by uncontrollable spontaneous emotion from inside.
rows.note: Internal irrepressible urge.

rows.label: 〜ないわけにはいかない
cells: Mandatory social responsibility or ethical duty: cannot afford not to do.
動詞ない形 + わけにはいかない
恩師に頼まれた以上、この仕事を引き受けないわけにはいかない。
Driven by external duty, social conscience, or obligation.
rows.note: External moral/social obligation.

rows.label: 〜なくはない / 〜なくもない
cells: Cautious double negative understatement: 'It is not entirely impossible that...'.
動詞ない形 + くはない / 形容詞く + はない
相手の言い分も理解できなくはないが、全面的に賛同はできない。
Understatement used to soften disagreement or show reluctant admission.
rows.note: Reluctant admission or softened understatement.

rows.label: 〜ないものでもない
cells: Tentative willingness under hypothetical conditions: 'Not entirely out of the question'.
動詞ない形 + ものでもない
今すぐ条件を見直していただけるなら、交渉に応じないものでもない。
Modest theoretical possibility under suitable terms.
rows.note: Hesitant potential concession.

title: 文章：文の始めと終わり
meaning: Match a long sentence's topic and predicate.
connection: 問題は…ことだ; なぜなら…からだ
nuance: Strip away modifiers temporarily and check the core clause. Then restore them and ensure they attach to the intended nouns.
keyTakeaway: 問題は…ことだ; なぜなら…からだ

sentences.japanese: 問題は、時間が足りないことです。
sentences.english: The problem is that there is not enough time.

sentences.japanese: たとえ困難な道であっても、最後まで全力を尽くすつもりです。
sentences.english: Even if it is a difficult road, I intend to give it my all until the very end.
sentences.nuanceNote: Opening たとえ correlates with closing volitional/commitment expression.

sentences.japanese: もし彼が関与していたとしたら、事態は極めて深刻だと言わざるを得ない。
sentences.english: If he were indeed involved, we would have no choice but to say the situation is extremely serious.
sentences.nuanceNote: Opening もし〜としたら correlates with closing evaluative conclusion.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 150 (PDF p. 160). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：時制
meaning: Maintain the time of events and observations.
connection: Past/non-past relative to the narrator and embedded clause
nuance: An embedded event can be future relative to a past decision. Determine the time relation before selecting an ending.
keyTakeaway: Past/non-past relative to the narrator and embedded clause

sentences.japanese: 昨日、来年日本へ行くことを決めました。
sentences.english: Yesterday I decided to go to Japan next year.

sentences.japanese: 食事をする前に手を洗い、食事が終わった後で薬を飲んだ。
sentences.english: I washed my hands before eating, and took my medicine after the meal finished.
sentences.nuanceNote: Tense before 前 is non-past (する); tense after 終わった reflects completed sequence.

sentences.japanese: 昨日見た映画は、昔読んだ小説を映画化したものだった。
sentences.english: The movie I watched yesterday was an adaptation of a novel I had read long ago.
sentences.nuanceNote: Relative past tenses (見た、読んだ) maintain coherent retrospective framing.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 154 (PDF p. 164). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：条件
meaning: Distinguish a hypothetical condition from an actual sequence.
connection: なら: premise; たら: condition/after; と: regular result/discovery; ば: condition
nuance: Read the following sentence to decide whether an event actually occurred. Volition restrictions depend on the construction, predicate type and subject relation.
keyTakeaway: なら: premise; たら: condition/after; と: regular result/discovery; ば: condition

sentences.japanese: 店に行ったら、休みでした。
sentences.english: When I went to the shop, it was closed.

sentences.japanese: 春になると、公園の桜が一斉に咲き乱れる。
sentences.english: When spring arrives, cherry blossoms in the park burst into bloom all at once.
sentences.nuanceNote: Conditional と marks invariant seasonal consequence without speaker volition in the clause.

sentences.japanese: 分からないことがあれば、遠慮せずにいつでも質問してください。
sentences.english: If there is anything you do not understand, please ask anytime without hesitation.
sentences.nuanceNote: Conditional たら smoothly accommodates advice and polite directives.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 158 (PDF p. 168). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：動詞・自他の視点
meaning: Keep participants consistent across sentences.
connection: Agent/object roles; transitive versus intransitive
nuance: A paragraph can omit repeated subjects. Recover them from context instead of automatically assigning each action to the most recent noun.
keyTakeaway: Agent/object roles; transitive versus intransitive

sentences.japanese: ドアが閉まりました。係員がもう一度開けました。
sentences.english: The door closed. An attendant opened it again.

sentences.japanese: 強い風でドアが閉まり、室内の書類が散らかった。
sentences.english: The door shut in the strong wind, and documents in the room got scattered.
sentences.nuanceNote: Intransitive 閉まる focuses on the spontaneous event rather than an intentional actor.

sentences.japanese: 冷気が入らないように、窓をしっかり閉めておいた。
sentences.english: So that cold air would not enter, I shut the window firmly in advance.
sentences.nuanceNote: Transitive 閉める focuses on purposeful human intervention.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 162 (PDF p. 172). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：てくる・ていく
meaning: Follow direction relative to a continuing reference point.
connection: Spatial approach/departure; temporal development
nuance: Identify whose location or time is central. A switch between くる and いく may indicate a deliberate viewpoint change, not interchangeable wording.
keyTakeaway: Spatial approach/departure; temporal development

sentences.japanese: 人口は減ってきました。今後も減っていくでしょう。
sentences.english: The population has been falling. It will probably continue to fall.

sentences.japanese: これまで多くの困難を乗り越えてきた。
sentences.english: We have overcome many hardships up to this point.
sentences.useLabel: Development reaching the present with てくる
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜てくる traces progressive development from the past approaching the current moment.

sentences.japanese: この技術は今後さらに発展していくだろう。
sentences.english: This technology will likely continue to develop further into the future.
sentences.useLabel: Evolution heading into the future with ていく
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜ていく projects continuous development moving forward from the present.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 166 (PDF p. 176). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：受身・使役・使役受身
meaning: Track the experiencer and causer through a passage.
connection: Affected subject in passive; causer in causative; compelled actor in causative-passive
nuance: Write a quick who-did-what paraphrase before choosing a form. Pay attention to whether に marks an agent, recipient or person made to act.
keyTakeaway: Affected subject in passive; causer in causative; compelled actor in causative-passive

sentences.japanese: 私は部長に資料を作らされました。
sentences.english: I was made to prepare the materials by my manager.

sentences.japanese: 満員電車で隣の人に足を踏まれて痛かった。
sentences.english: I had my foot stepped on by the person next to me on the crowded train, and it hurt.
sentences.nuanceNote: Indirect adversity passive marks the affected person as subject and actor with に.

sentences.japanese: 親は子供に好きな習い事を自由にやらせてくれた。
sentences.english: The parents generously let their child freely pursue whatever extracurricular lessons they wanted.
sentences.nuanceNote: Causative with てくれる expresses gracious permission granted to an actor.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 170 (PDF p. 180). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ていただく / 〜くださる (Benefactive Exchanges in Formal Business Register)
meaning: Polite business equivalents of favor receipt and bestowment: 〜ていただく (humbly receive an action from an esteemed party); 〜くださる (an esteemed party graciously performs an action for us).
connection: V-て形 + いただく / いただきます | V-て形 + くださる / くださいます
nuance: BUSINESS PROTOCOL: In professional correspondence: 'ご検討いただけますと幸いです' (We would be honored if you would kindly consider this).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + いただく = 'We humbly receive your gracious deed'. V-て + くださる = 'You graciously do for us'.

sentences.japanese: 多忙な時期にもかかわらず、貴重なお時間を割いていただき心より御礼申し上げます。
sentences.english: Despite it being a hectic period, I express my heartfelt thanks for you generously taking your precious time for us.
sentences.literal: Hectic period despite, precious time sparing-receive-humbly heart-from thanks express.

tokens.meaning: humbly receiving your sparing of time

sentences.nuanceNote: Formal business correspondence expressing profound appreciation.

sentences.japanese: お忙しいところ恐縮ですが、企画書をご確認いただけますでしょうか。
sentences.english: I apologize for troubling you when busy, but could you kindly review the proposal?
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb-て + いただく politely solicits a superior's or client's favorable action.

sentences.japanese: 社長自ら私たちの研究室まで足を運んでくださった。
sentences.english: The company president graciously took the trouble to visit our laboratory in person.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb-て + くださる honors an action performed by an esteemed superior for our group.

quiz.question: 先生に作文を見て（　　）。
quiz.translation: I had my teacher look over my composition.
quiz.grammarFocus: お + stem + いただく (Deferential client request)
quiz.ruleHint: V-て形 + いただく / いただきます | V-て形 + くださる / くださいます

explanations.reason: いただく makes the speaker the receiver, with teacher marked に.
The teacher would be the subject in the くださる frame.
あげる reverses the intended benefit direction.
やる reverses the intended benefit direction and is unsuitable here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 174 (PDF p. 184). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：あげる・くれる・もらう
meaning: Preserve the passage's beneficiary viewpoint.
connection: Giver perspective versus receiver perspective
nuance: Check the subject and particles together. Polite forms do not change the underlying direction of the favor.
keyTakeaway: Giver perspective versus receiver perspective

sentences.japanese: 先生に説明していただき、よく分かりました。
sentences.english: After receiving an explanation from my teacher, I understood well.

sentences.japanese: 友人が困っていたので、私のノートを貸してあげた。
sentences.english: Because my friend was having trouble, I lent them my notebook.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜てあげる indicates doing a favor outwards for a peer.

sentences.japanese: 先輩が仕事の進め方を丁寧に教えてくれた。
sentences.english: My senior colleague kindly taught me how to proceed with the work.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜てくれる marks an action performed by another for the benefit of the speaker.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 174 (PDF p. 184). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：こ・そ・あ
meaning: Identify the antecedent and textual distance.
connection: Reference to things, events or previous claims
nuance: A demonstrative may summarize a whole proposition. Test each possible referent by substituting it back into the sentence.
keyTakeaway: Reference to things, events or previous claims

sentences.japanese: 毎日少しずつ練習しました。それが自信につながりました。
sentences.english: I practiced a little every day. That led to confidence.

sentences.japanese: 若者の読書離れが進んでいる。この問題には早急な対策が必要だ。
sentences.english: Young people reading fewer books is progressing. Urgent countermeasures are required for this problem.
sentences.nuanceNote: Demonstrative この summarizes the previously introduced socioeconomic phenomenon.

sentences.japanese: あのときの苦しい経験があったからこそ、今の成功がある。
sentences.english: It is precisely because of that painful experience back then that we have today's success.
sentences.nuanceNote: Demonstrative あの recalls an experience vividly shared in psychological memory.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 178 (PDF p. 188). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：は・が
meaning: Separate the continuing topic from the focused subject.
connection: Topic, contrast, exhaustive identification and subordinate subjects
nuance: Use the question the sentence answers to find its focus. は can contrast; が can identify who or what. Neither has a single English translation.
keyTakeaway: Topic, contrast, exhaustive identification and subordinate subjects

sentences.japanese: 私が担当します。この仕事は経験があります。
sentences.english: I will handle it. I have experience with this work.

sentences.japanese: 兄は外で遊ぶのが好きだが、弟は家で読書をするのが好きだ。
sentences.english: My older brother likes playing outside, but my younger brother likes reading at home.
sentences.nuanceNote: は marks contrast between parallel topics.

sentences.japanese: 外で激しい雨が降り始めたので、窓を閉めた。
sentences.english: Because heavy rain began falling outside, I shut the window.
sentences.nuanceNote: が in subordinate clauses neutrally marks the subject of natural phenomena.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 182 (PDF p. 192). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：接続表現（談話の展開と論理の整理）
meaning: System of discourse connectors governing addition (しかも・そのうえ・さらに), contrast (それに対して・一方), alternatives (あるいは・それとも), logical development & result (そのため・したがって・そこで・すると・このように・こうして), rationale (なぜなら・というのは), adversative persistence (だが・ところが・それなのに・それでも), reformulation & analogy (つまり・要するに・いわば・すなわち), qualification & exception (ただし・ただ・もっとも・なお), and topic transition (さて・ところで).
connection: Sentence 1。 + Connector + 、Sentence 2。 (Discourse linking expressions across sentence boundaries)
nuance: SKM N2 pp. 186-187 functional distinctions: Addition: しかも adds same evaluation; そのうえ/さらに adds higher degree. Contrast: それに対して/一方 contrasts two subjects. Alternatives: あるいは gives declarative alternatives; それとも introduces question choices. Consequence: そのため states factual results; したがって draws formal conclusions; そこで introduces intentional reactions; すると introduces triggered events/discoveries; このように/こうして summarizes unfolding outcomes. Rationale: なぜなら/というのは introduces reasons. Adversative: だが is formal contrast; ところが introduces unexpected contrary outcomes; それなのに expresses complaint/regret; それでも indicates action persists despite facts. Reformulation: つまり rephrases; 要するに summarizes; いわば makes figurative analogies; すなわち states exact identities. Qualification: ただし sets strict conditions/exceptions; ただ/もっとも preemptively qualifies assumptions; なお adds supplementary notices. Discourse transition: さて transitions forward to the main agenda; ところで diverts to an unrelated topic.
keyTakeaway: Sentence 1。 + Connector + 、Sentence 2。 (Discourse linking expressions across sentence boundaries)

sentences.japanese: 美術館の休館日は毎週月曜日です。ただし、祝日と重なる場合は開館いたします。
sentences.english: The museum's regular closing day is every Monday. However, when it coincides with a public holiday, it remains open.

sentences.japanese: このアパートは駅から徒歩3分でとても便利だ。しかも、家賃が相場よりずっと安い。
sentences.english: This apartment is just a 3-minute walk from the station and very convenient. Moreover, the rent is much lower than the market rate.
sentences.nuanceNote: しかも adds another supportive point of the same evaluation or greater intensity.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんの家で美味しい夕食をごちそうになった。そのうえ、珍しいお土産までいただいた。
sentences.english: I was treated to a delicious dinner at Tanaka-san's house. On top of that, I even received rare souvenirs.
sentences.useLabel: Higher-degree addition with そのうえ / さらに
sentences.nuanceNote: そのうえ / さらに adds a point of an even higher degree or unexpected generosity.

sentences.japanese: 駅の南口は商業施設が多くていつもにぎやかだ。それに対して、北口は住宅街でとても静かだ。
sentences.english: The south exit of the station has many commercial facilities and is always bustling. In contrast, the north exit is a residential area and very quiet.
sentences.useLabel: Direct contrast with それに対して / 一方
sentences.nuanceNote: それに対して / 一方 sets up a direct contrast between two distinct subjects or aspects.

sentences.japanese: 発熱の原因は季節性の風邪かもしれない。あるいは、インフルエンザの可能性もある。
sentences.english: The cause of the fever might be a seasonal cold. Alternatively, there is also the possibility of influenza.
sentences.useLabel: Alternative declarative possibility with あるいは
sentences.nuanceNote: あるいは presents another possibility or alternative option in declarative statements.

sentences.japanese: 今の会社でこのまま仕事を続けるべきか。それとも、大学院へ進学するべきか。
sentences.english: Should I continue working at my current company as I am? Or should I go on to graduate school?
sentences.useLabel: Alternative choice in questions with それとも
sentences.nuanceNote: それとも presents an alternative option specifically in question sentences.

sentences.japanese: この高原都市は標高1,000メートルの高地にある。そのため、真夏でも比較的涼しい。
sentences.english: This plateau city is located at an altitude of 1,000 meters. For that reason, it is relatively cool even in midsummer.
sentences.useLabel: Factual cause and effect with そのため
sentences.nuanceNote: そのため states the objective, factual result resulting from the preceding cause.

sentences.japanese: 構内は全域にわたり終日禁煙となっております。したがって、喫煙所をご利用ください。
sentences.english: The entire premises are strictly non-smoking all day long. Consequently, please use the designated smoking areas.
sentences.useLabel: Formal logical conclusion with したがって
sentences.nuanceNote: したがって introduces a formal, authoritative logical consequence or conclusion.

sentences.japanese: 講義の中でどうしても理解できない点があった。そこで、授業後に先生に質問してみた。
sentences.english: There was a point in the lecture that I simply could not understand. Therefore, I went and asked the professor after class.
sentences.nuanceNote: そこで introduces an intentional action deliberately taken by the agent in response to the preceding situation.

sentences.japanese: 太郎が小箱のふたを静かに開けた。すると、中から白い煙がもくもくと立ち上ってきた。
sentences.english: Taro quietly opened the lid of the small box. Thereupon, white smoke came billowing out from inside.
sentences.useLabel: Triggered occurrence and discovery with すると
sentences.nuanceNote: すると introduces an automatic, triggered occurrence or surprise discovery resulting immediately from the action.

sentences.japanese: 大学で素晴らしい友人に恵まれ、研究も軌道に乗った。こうして、私の充実した留学生活が始まった。
sentences.english: Blessed with wonderful friends at university, my research also got on track. In this manner, my fulfilling study-abroad life began.
sentences.useLabel: Summary of unfolding result with こうして / このように
sentences.nuanceNote: こうして / このように synthesizes and summarizes how a situation unfolded over time into an overall conclusion.

sentences.japanese: 無理をして派手な結婚式を挙げる必要はないと思う。なぜなら、多額の費用がかかるからだ。
sentences.english: I do not think it is necessary to go out of one's way to hold a lavish wedding. This is because it incurs a huge expense.
sentences.useLabel: Stating rationale with なぜなら / というのは
sentences.nuanceNote: なぜなら / というのは introduces the backward explanatory reason or rationale for a preceding opinion.

sentences.japanese: このクラシック映画は半世紀以上前に制作された。だが、今も世界中で高い人気を誇っている。
sentences.english: This classic movie was produced over half a century ago. However, it still enjoys tremendous popularity worldwide.
sentences.useLabel: General formal contrast with だが
sentences.nuanceNote: だが introduces a formal contrast running contrary to the expected development.

sentences.japanese: 何度も念入りに計算を確認したはずだった。ところが、集計の数字に大きな食い違いがあった。
sentences.english: We were supposed to have checked the calculation thoroughly many times. However, contrary to expectations, there was a major discrepancy in the aggregate figures.
sentences.useLabel: Unexpected contrary outcome with ところが
sentences.nuanceNote: ところが introduces an unexpected, surprising, or contrary outcome beyond the speaker's control.

sentences.japanese: 毎日欠かさず厳しい特訓を重ねてきた。それなのに、本番の試合で呆気なく初戦敗退してしまった。
sentences.english: I had maintained rigorous special training every single day without fail. Even so, to my great disappointment, I lost easily in the very first round of the official match.
sentences.useLabel: Dissatisfaction or regret with それなのに
sentences.nuanceNote: それなのに expresses dissatisfaction, regret, or complaint that an adverse outcome occurred despite great effort.

sentences.japanese: 宝くじが一等に当たる確率は天文学的に低い。それでも、多くの人々は夢を求めて買い続ける。
sentences.english: The probability of winning first prize in the lottery is astronomically low. Even so, many people continue buying tickets pursuing the dream.
sentences.useLabel: Persistence despite facts with それでも
sentences.nuanceNote: それでも indicates that an action, conviction, or attitude persists unchanged even in the face of the preceding reality.

sentences.japanese: 来週から大学は夏季休業に入る。つまり、毎朝満員電車に乗って登校しなくてもいいのだ。
sentences.english: Starting next week, the university enters summer recess. That is to say, I do not have to ride packed trains to commute to school every morning.
sentences.useLabel: Restatement and clarification with つまり / 要するに
sentences.nuanceNote: つまり rephrases the situation in other words; 要するに distills it down to its core takeaway.

sentences.japanese: この国民的アニメを知らない日本人はほとんどいないだろう。いわば、現代の日本文化を象徴する作品だ。
sentences.english: There is probably hardly any Japanese person who does not know this nationwide anime. So to speak, it is a work that symbolizes modern Japanese culture.
sentences.nuanceNote: いわば introduces a figurative comparison or metaphorical characterization ('so to speak / as it were').

sentences.japanese: 図書館の定期休館日は毎週月曜日です。ただし、祝日と重なる場合は翌日の火曜日に休館します。
sentences.english: The library's regular closing day is every Monday. However, when it coincides with a national holiday, it closes on the following Tuesday instead.
sentences.useLabel: Limiting proviso and exception with ただし
sentences.nuanceNote: ただし introduces a strict limiting condition, exception, or proviso to a preceding general rule.

sentences.japanese: 私はテニスをするのが大好きだ。もっとも、最近は仕事が忙しくて全くコートに立てていない。
sentences.english: I love playing tennis. Mind you, lately I have been so busy with work that I have not been able to step onto a court at all.
sentences.useLabel: Preemptive qualification with もっとも / ただ
sentences.nuanceNote: もっとも / ただ preemptively corrects or tempers an assumption that the listener might jump to from the previous assertion.

sentences.japanese: 本日の全体説明会は午後3時をもって終了いたします。なお、希望者には個別相談会も実施いたします。
sentences.english: Today's general briefing will conclude at 3:00 PM. Furthermore, individual consultations will also be provided for those interested.
sentences.useLabel: Supplementary administrative notice with なお
sentences.nuanceNote: なお introduces supplementary, practical, or administrative information without modifying the main statement.

sentences.japanese: 長らくご無沙汰しておりますが、いかがお過ごしでしょうか。さて、本日は来月の学術大会の件でご連絡いたしました。
sentences.english: It has been a long time since we last spoke, and I hope you are doing well. Now then, I am writing to you today regarding next month's academic conference.
sentences.useLabel: Deliberate topic transition with さて
sentences.nuanceNote: さて transitions the discourse forward purposefully into the main agenda or next topic.

sentences.japanese: もうすぐ新年を迎えますね。お正月の準備は整いましたか。ところで、12月31日を大晦日と呼ぶのはなぜでしょうか。
sentences.english: The New Year is approaching soon. Have you finished your New Year preparations? By the way, why is December 31st called 'Omisoka'?
sentences.useLabel: Digressive topic change with ところで
sentences.nuanceNote: ところで diverts the conversation purposefully into a completely different subject ('by the way').

sentences.japanese: 母の実の兄、すなわち私にとっての伯父が、定年退職を機に故郷へ戻ってくることになった。
sentences.english: My mother's biological elder brother, that is to say my uncle, has decided to return to his hometown upon his retirement.
sentences.useLabel: Precise identity and reformulation with すなわち
sentences.nuanceNote: すなわち states an exact identity, strict definition, or precise reformulation of the preceding term.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 186 (PDF p. 196). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: SKM N2: The 9 Discourse Connector Categories (pp. 186–187)
table.subtitle: Sentence-initial discourse markers systematically distinguished by rhetorical function.

rows.label: 1. Adding Points (累加・付加)
cells: しかも, そのうえ, さらに, そればかりか, そればかりでなく
しかも: adds surprising/escalating extra detail. そのうえ: "on top of that". さらに: step-by-step progressive increment. そればかりか: "not merely that, but even..."
この料理は美味しく、しかも値段が手頃だ。
rows.note: Escalation beyond prior statement.

rows.label: 2. Contrast & Comparison (対比)
cells: それに対して, 一方(で)
それに対して: sharp directional contrast between two distinct entities. 一方: balancing two parallel facts or sides of the same entity.
兄は社交的だ。それに対して、弟は物静かな性格だ。
rows.note: A vs B juxtaposition.

rows.label: 3. Alternatives & Choices (選択)
cells: あるいは, それとも
あるいは: formal/written alternative ("or alternatively"). それとも: conversational question alternative ("A? Or is it B?").
郵送、あるいはメールで提出してください。
rows.note: それとも is restricted to interrogative choices.

rows.label: 4. Consequence & Action (結末・行動)
cells: そのため, したがって, そこで, すると, このように, こうして
そのため: objective causal result. したがって: logical conclusion ("therefore"). そこで: motivated deliberate action taken in response. すると: instantaneous discovery/mechanical result.
雨が降り出した。そこで、近くの喫茶店に入った。
rows.note: Trap: そこで requires speaker's deliberate volition; すると excludes personal intention!

rows.label: 5. Rationale & Background (理由・説明)
cells: なぜなら(ば), というのは
なぜなら(ば): formal retrospective reason ("the reason why is..."). というのは: explanatory elaboration of context.
昨夜は欠席しました。というのは、急な発熱があったからです。
rows.note: Often concludes with 〜からだ / 〜ためだ.

rows.label: 6. Adversative & Persistence (逆接・譲歩)
cells: だが, ところが, それなのに, それでも
だが: standard formal but. ところが: unexpected, surprising twist. それなのに: indignant frustration against expectation. それでも: persistence despite counterweight.
必死に頼み込んだ。それでも、彼は承諾しなかった。
rows.note: ところが cannot introduce speaker's volitional request.

rows.label: 7. Restatement & Analogy (換言・要約)
cells: つまり, 要するに, すなわち, いわば
つまり: summarizing meaning ("in short"). 要するに: distilling to core essence. すなわち: formal exact equivalence ("namely"). いわば: figurative metaphor ("so to speak").
彼は私の恩人、いわば人生の師匠だ。
rows.note: いわば requires a metaphorical comparison.

rows.label: 8. Qualification & Provisos (補足・条件)
cells: ただし, もっとも, なお
ただし: strict conditions, provisos, or exceptions to the preceding rule. もっとも: natural partial concession or reservation. なお: neutral supplementary admin detail.
入場は無料です。ただし、事前登録が必要です。
rows.note: ただし is standard for legal and contract terms.

rows.label: 9. Topic Shift & Transition (転換)
cells: さて, ところで
さて: closes previous topic and smoothly advances forward to main business ("now then"). ところで: abrupt complete change of subject ("by the way").
雑談はここまでにして、さて、本題に入りましょう。
rows.note: Do not confuse discourse ところで with temporal 〜たところで!

title: 文章：省略・繰り返し・言い換え
meaning: Recover omitted material and recognize paraphrases.
connection: Omitted subject/object; lexical repetition; paraphrase
nuance: Restore the omitted participant mentally, then check that later paraphrases refer to the same idea. Do not assume a change of wording means a new topic.
keyTakeaway: Omitted subject/object; lexical repetition; paraphrase

sentences.japanese: この方法は時間がかかります。つまり、すぐには結果が出ません。
sentences.english: This method takes time. In other words, it does not give immediate results.

sentences.japanese: 彼は一言も返事をしなかった。つまり、納得していないということだ。
sentences.english: He did not utter a single reply. In other words, he does not agree.
sentences.nuanceNote: つまり restates the essential meaning of an observation in clearer terms.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは資料を手に取り、しばらく黙って（資料を）眺めていた。
sentences.english: Tanaka picked up the document and gazed at it silently for a while.
sentences.nuanceNote: Cohesive prose omits previously mentioned direct objects to avoid cumbersome repetition.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 190 (PDF p. 200). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 文章：文体の一貫性
meaning: Keep register consistent with genre and voice.
connection: です/ます versus だ/である; conversation versus exposition
nuance: An essay, a notice and a personal conversation have different expectations. Quotations and rhetorical questions can legitimately differ from the surrounding narration.
keyTakeaway: です/ます versus だ/である; conversation versus exposition

sentences.japanese: 本調査は学生を対象とする。結果は来月公表する。
sentences.english: This survey targets students. The results will be published next month.

sentences.japanese: 本研究の目的は、日本語の文法構造を解明することにある。
sentences.english: The objective of this research consists in elucidating Japanese grammatical structures.
sentences.nuanceNote: Expository academic writing consistently maintains だ/である forms.

sentences.japanese: ご不明な点がございましたら、いつでも担当者までご連絡ください。
sentences.english: Should you have any unclear points, please contact the person in charge at any time.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite business correspondence maintains consistent です/ます honorific harmony.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 194 (PDF p. 204). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: X は Y です (Synthesis Reference Sheet)
meaning: Identify or describe a topic: as for X, it is Y.
connection: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.
nuance: は is written は but pronounced わ when it marks the topic. It tells the listener what the statement is about; it is not simply a replacement for the English subject. If both speakers already know the topic, omit it: 学生です can mean I am a student, she is a student, or they are students, depending on context. Japanese nouns generally do not require a/an and do not automatically change for plural number. です makes the noun predicate polite and non-past; it does not change with person or number. Do not append です to an ordinary finite verb such as 行くです. Adjectives have their own patterns, introduced later: 静かです and 高いです, but not 静かだです or 高いだです. Use a name/title rather than repeatedly translating English you as あなた.
keyTakeaway: State the topic only when needed; put the identifying noun before polite です.

sentences.japanese: 私はカリフォルニア大学の留学生です。
sentences.english: I am an international student at the University of California.
sentences.literal: I topic UC's international-student am.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standard polite self-introduction formula.

sentences.japanese: スミスさんは学生ですか。はい、（私は）学生です。
sentences.english: Are you a student, Smith-san? Yes, I am.
sentences.nuanceNote: Once the topic is established by conversational context, Japanese naturally omits the pronoun.

sentences.japanese: 昼ご飯は食べましたが、朝ご飯は食べませんでした。
sentences.english: I ate lunch, but as for breakfast, I didn't eat.
sentences.nuanceNote: は marks contrast between two parallel contextual topics.

quiz.question: 田中さん（　　）日本人です。
quiz.translation: Tanaka-san is Japanese.
quiz.grammarFocus: Topic marker は
quiz.ruleHint: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.

explanations.reason: Correct! は marks Tanaka-san as the topic being identified as Japanese.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects of action verbs, not copula topics.
Incorrect. に indicates direction, time, or location of existence.
Incorrect. へ indicates direction of movement.

sourceReference: Supplementary comparison note; not counted as verified textbook section coverage.
comparisonNote: For the primary step-by-step textbook lesson, study X は Y です (X is Y / Topic & Copula) in Genki I Lesson 1.

title: 動詞の３分類 (Synthesis Reference Sheet)
meaning: Japanese verbs are strictly classified into Ru-verbs (一段), U-verbs (五段), and Irregular verbs (する, くる).
connection: Ru-verbs: stem + ます | U-verbs: u-vowel changes to i-vowel + ます | Irregular: する→します, くる→きます
nuance: Not every verb ending in る is a Ru-verb! Verbs like 帰る (かえる - to return) and 知る (しる - to know) end in る but are 五段 U-verbs (帰ります, 知ります).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Ru-verbs drop る. U-verbs change final u to i (行く→行きます, 飲む→飲みます).

sentences.japanese: 毎晩図書館で日本語を勉強します。
sentences.english: I study Japanese in the library every night.
sentences.literal: Every-night library-at Japanese study-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: 勉強する is an irregular compound verb (勉強します).

sentences.japanese: 食べる→食べます、見る→見ます、起きる→起きます。
sentences.english: Eat -> eat (polite); see -> see (polite); wake up -> wake up (polite).
sentences.nuanceNote: Ru-verbs drop final る and attach ます without vowel alternation.

sentences.japanese: 書く→書きます、話す→話します、待つ→待ちます。
sentences.english: Write -> write (polite); speak -> speak (polite); wait -> wait (polite).
sentences.nuanceNote: U-verbs shift the final u-vowel to the corresponding i-vowel before ます.

sentences.japanese: する→します、くる（来る）→きます（来ます）。
sentences.english: Do -> do (polite); come -> come (polite).
sentences.nuanceNote: Irregular verbs する and くる conjugate with stem changes.

quiz.question: 明日友達と映画を（　　）ます。
quiz.translation: I will watch a movie with a friend tomorrow.
quiz.grammarFocus: Ru-verb stem connection to ます
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: stem + ます | U-verbs: u-vowel changes to i-vowel + ます | Irregular: する→します, くる→きます

explanations.reason: Correct! 見る drops る to form 見ます.
Incorrect. Cannot retain dictionary る before ます.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach directly to ます.
Incorrect. 見ら is part of passive/potential, not polite stem.

sourceReference: Supplementary comparison note; not counted as verified textbook section coverage.
comparisonNote: For the primary step-by-step textbook lesson, study 動詞の活用・語順・助詞 in Genki I Lesson 3.

title: て形 (Synthesis Reference Sheet)
meaning: The fundamental connective form of Japanese verbs, used for requests (〜てください), permission (〜てもいい), prohibition (〜てはいけない), and sequence.
connection: う・つ・る→って | む・ぶ・ぬ→んで | く→いて (行く→行って!) | ぐ→いで | す→して | る(一段)→て
nuance: CRITICAL EXCEPTION: 行く は「いいて」にならず、「行って」と促音便になります。
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + ください = Please do. Prohibited: V-て + はいけません = Must not.

table.title: The Te-Form (て形) Conjugation Matrix
table.subtitle: The foundational gateway for ~ている, ~てから, ~てもいい, ~てはいけない, and ~てしまう.

rows.label: Group 1: う・つ・る
cells: 買う, 待つ, 取る
買って, 待って, 取って
買った, 待った, 取った
う・つ・る → って / った (促音便: 小さい「っ」+ て)
rows.note: Classic rhythm: "u, tsu, ru" becomes "tte"

rows.label: Group 1: む・ぶ・ぬ
cells: 飲む, 遊ぶ, 死ぬ
飲んで, 遊んで, 死んで
飲んだ, 遊んだ, 死んだ
む・ぶ・ぬ → んで / んだ (撥音便: 濁音の「で」)
rows.note: Voiced consonants always take で, not て.

rows.label: Group 1: く / ぐ
cells: 書く, 泳ぐ
書いて, 泳いで
書いた, 泳いだ
く → いて, ぐ → いで (イ音便: い + て/で)
rows.note: CRITICAL EXCEPTION: 行く は「いいて」にならず、「行って・行った」と促音便になります。

rows.label: Group 1: す
cells: 話す, 出す
話して, 出して
話した, 出した
す → して / した
rows.note: Behaves cleanly like polite shimasu.

rows.label: Group 2: る (一段動詞)
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べて, 見て, 起きて
食べた, 見た, 起きた
る を取って「て・た」を付ける
rows.note: Vowel before る is usually e or i (たべ・み).

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular (変格動詞)
cells: する, 来る
して, 来て
した, 来た
不規則活用: 来る は「来て（きて）・来た（きた）」と読みが変化します。
rows.note: Notice 来る changes reading to 「き」 in て/た form: 来て（きて）, 来た（きた）.

sentences.japanese: すみませんが、窓を開けてください。
sentences.english: Excuse me, but please open the window.
sentences.literal: Excuse-me but, window open please.
sentences.nuanceNote: 開ける is Ru-verb: stem 開け + て + ください.

sentences.japanese: 朝起きて、顔を洗って、朝ご飯を食べました。
sentences.english: I woke up in the morning, washed my face, and ate breakfast.
sentences.nuanceNote: The te-form links successive actions in chronological order.

sentences.japanese: 大事な話ですから、静かに聞いてください。
sentences.english: Because this is an important matter, please listen quietly.
sentences.useLabel: Polite request with ください
sentences.nuanceNote: V-て + ください forms a standard polite request.

quiz.question: ここで写真を（　　）はいけません。撮影禁止です。
quiz.translation: You must not take photos here. Photography is prohibited.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜てはいけません prohibition
quiz.ruleHint: う・つ・る→って | む・ぶ・ぬ→んで | く→いて (行く→行って!) | ぐ→いで | す→して | る(一段)→て

explanations.reason: Correct! 撮る conjugates to 撮って + はいけません for strict prohibition.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot connect to はいけません.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot connect to はいけません.
Incorrect. Past form cannot connect to はいけません.

sourceReference: Supplementary comparison note; not counted as verified textbook section coverage.
